sections.zh: 会话、上下文窗口与轮次

description.en: A moving label, not a technology. Points at whatever computers can newly, impressively do — right now, large language models.
description.zh: 一个不断变化的称呼，而不是某项固定技术；如今通常指大型语言模型。

en: A moving label, not a technology. "AI" doesn't name a fixed thing the way model or token does — it points at whatever computers can newly, impressively do. Right now it points at large language models. It has pointed at very different things before:

| Era       | What "AI" meant                                                                                       |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1950s     | Symbolic reasoning — theorem provers, checkers programs.                                              |
| 1960s–70s | Rule-based symbolic programs — ELIZA, SHRDLU.                                                         |
| 1980s     | Expert systems — thousands of hand-written if-then rules encoding human expertise.                    |
| 1990s     | Game-tree search — Deep Blue beating Kasparov (1997). Researchers avoided the word "AI" entirely      |
| 2000s     | Statistical machine learning — spam filters, recommenders. Still sold as "machine learning", not "AI" |
| 2010s     | Deep learning — image recognition (AlexNet, 2012), AlphaGo (2016).                                    |
| 2020s     | Large language models — ChatGPT (2022) made "AI" mean chatbots                                        |

The pointer moves by a known mechanism, sometimes called the AI effect: once a technique works reliably, it gets renamed — it's "just" search, "just" statistics — and "AI" slides forward to the next unsolved thing. The observation is old. Bertram Raphael put it this way in 1971: "AI is a collective name for problems which we do not yet know how to solve properly by computer." Larry Tesler's version, from around 1979: "Intelligence is whatever machines haven't done yet."

This is why conversations about AI so often talk past each other. A claim like "AI can't reason" or "AI is overhyped" carries a hidden timestamp — it may be about expert systems, about 2010s image classifiers, or about last month's LLM, and each reference supports a different conclusion. When a discussion about AI stalls, the fix is usually to swap the word for whichever precise term is actually meant: the model, the harness, the agent, the context it was given.
Avoid: "AI" in any technical claim — name the part you mean instead. "AI coding" as a label for the practice is fine; "the AI is hallucinating" is not.
Usage:
"The CTO wants to know whether AI could handle the triage queue."
"Translate that before scoping it — she means an LLM in a harness with access to the ticket system. 'AI' on its own isn't a spec."
zh: 一个不断移动的标签，而非一项技术。"AI" 并不像 Model 或 Token 那样指代某个固定的东西——它指向计算机新近能够做到、且令人印象深刻的事。眼下它指向大语言模型。而在过去，它曾指向过截然不同的事物：

| 时代 | "AI" 的含义 |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1950 年代 | 符号推理 —— 定理证明器、西洋跳棋程序。 |
| 1960–70 年代 | 基于规则的符号程序 —— ELIZA、SHRDLU。 |
| 1980 年代 | 专家系统 —— 数千条手写的 if-then 规则，将人类专业知识编码其中。 |
| 1990 年代 | 博弈树搜索 —— Deep Blue 击败 Kasparov（1997）。研究者完全回避 "AI" 一词 |
| 2000 年代 | 统计机器学习 —— 垃圾邮件过滤器、推荐系统。仍然以 "machine learning" 的名义出售，而不是 "AI" |
| 2010 年代 | 深度学习 —— 图像识别（AlexNet，2012）、AlphaGo（2016）。 |
| 2020 年代 | 大语言模型 —— ChatGPT（2022）让 "AI" 的含义变成了聊天机器人 |

这个指针的移动有已知的机制，有时被称为 AI 效应：一旦某项技术稳定可靠地工作，它就会被重新命名——"不过是"搜索，"不过是"统计——而 "AI" 则向前滑向下一件尚未解决的事。这个观察由来已久。Bertram Raphael 在 1971 年这样表述："AI 是我们尚不知道如何用计算机妥善解决的问题的集合名称。" Larry Tesler 在 1979 年前后的版本是："智能就是机器尚未做到的事。"

这正是关于 AI 的对话常常各说各话的原因。像 "AI 不会推理" 或 "AI 被过度炒作了" 这样的论断都带有一个隐藏的时间戳——它可能说的是专家系统，可能是 2010 年代的图像分类器，也可能是上个月的 LLM，而每一种所指都支撑着不同的结论。当关于 AI 的讨论陷入僵局时，通常的解法是把这个词换成真正想要表达的精确术语：Model、Harness、Agent，或者提供给它的 Context。
避免：在任何技术性论断中使用 "AI"——改为点名你实际所指的那个部分。用 "AI coding" 作为这项实践的标签没问题；"AI 在幻觉" 则不行。
用法
"CTO 想知道 AI 能否处理分诊队列。"
"先翻译一下再界定范围——她指的是一个能访问 Ticket 系统的 Harness 中的 LLM。单独的 'AI' 不是一份 Spec。"

summary.zh: AI 不是某种固定的机器结构，而是一个会随时代移动的标签。过去它先后指符号推理、专家系统、机器学习和深度学习；今天常被用来指大型语言模型。讨论能力或问题时，最好进一步说清楚是 Model、Harness、Agent，还是提供给它们的 Context。

description.en: The parameters. Stateless — does next-token prediction and nothing else. Cannot do anything agentic on its own.
description.zh: 由训练得到的 parameters 构成，本身不保留会话状态，只做 next-token prediction；单独不能像 Agent 一样行动。

en: The parameters. Stateless — does next-token prediction and nothing else. "Claude Opus 4.x" and "GPT-5.x" are models. On its own a model can't do anything agentic; it has to be harnessed.

Models can't read files, run commands, browse the web, or remember yesterday — it takes tokens in and predicts tokens out, once per model provider request. Everything that feels like an agent working — choosing tools, reading results, looping until the task is done — is the harness orchestrating many of those predictions in a row.

Model providers ship models in tiers: a large one that's smartest but slow and expensive, and smaller ones that are faster and cheaper but less capable. Picking a tier is a real decision — heavyweight for planning and hard debugging, lightweight for mechanical changes — and harnesses let you switch mid-session.

Being strict about the word also sharpens diagnosis. "The model is bad at this" is a specific claim — the same model in a different harness, or with a different context, often behaves completely differently. Before blaming the model, check what it was given: most disappointing output traces back to context or harness, not parameters.
Usage:
"Should we switch the model from Sonnet to Opus for the planning step?"
"Try it — but the harness is doing most of the lifting on this task. The model swap won't help if the system prompt and tools are wrong."
zh: Parameters。Stateless——只做 next-token prediction，仅此而已。"Claude Opus 4.x" 和 "GPT-5.x" 都是 Model。单靠 Model 本身做不了任何 agentic 的事，它必须由 Harness 驱动。
Model 不能读文件、跑命令、浏览网页，也记不住昨天的事——每次 model provider request，它只是输入 Token、预测输出 Token。所有那些感觉像是 Agent 在干活的部分——选择工具、读取结果、循环到任务完成——都是 Harness 在把一连串这样的预测编排起来。
Model provider 按档位发布 Model：大号的最聪明，但慢且贵；小号的更快更便宜，但能力弱一些。选档位是个实打实的决定——规划和硬核调试用重量级，机械性改动用轻量级——而 Harness 让你能在 Session 中途切换。
对这个词较真，也能让诊断更锐利。"这个 Model 不擅长这件事"是一个具体的断言——同一个 Model 换一个 Harness，或者换一个 Context，表现常常完全不同。在怪罪 Model 之前，先看它拿到了什么：大多数令人失望的输出，根子在 Context 或 Harness，而不是 Parameters。
用法
"规划这一步，我们该把 Model 从 Sonnet 换成 Opus 吗？"
"试试吧——但这个任务里主要出力的是 Harness。如果 System prompt 和工具不对，换 Model 也帮不上忙。"

summary.zh: Model 是训练后固定的一组 parameters。它接收 Tokens 并做 next-token prediction，不会自己读取文件、调用工具或记住昨天的对话。我们看到的 Agent 行为来自 Harness 把多次 Model 请求与工具执行串起来；同一个 Model 在不同 Harness 和 Context 下，表现可能很不一样。

description.en: The numbers inside a model — often billions — tuned during training. Everything the model knows lives in them. Also called weights.
description.zh: Model 内部经训练调好的大量数值，也称 weights；模型学到的模式存放在这里。

en: The numbers inside a model — often billions of them — tuned during training. Everything the model "knows" lives in them. Training sets them; inference uses them unchanged. Also called weights.

Mechanically, the parameters are what turn input into output. Next-token prediction is a giant calculation: the tokens in the context window go in, get multiplied through the parameters, and a prediction for the next token comes out. There is no database of facts inside the model, no code lookup table — just these numbers, arranged so that the calculation tends to produce useful output. Facts the model can recite from training, like a standard library API, are parametric knowledge: stored in the parameters, not retrieved from anywhere.

The detail worth internalising is that parameters are frozen after training. Nothing you do in a session changes them — no correction you make, no codebase you show it, no mistake it learns from. Every session runs on the same numbers. This is why the model is stateless, why its built-in knowledge stops at the knowledge cutoff, and why anything project-specific has to arrive via context instead. The only way parameters change is more training — which produces, in effect, a different model.
Usage:
"Can we fine-tune it on our codebase?"
"That'd update the parameters — different model afterwards. For one project it's almost always cheaper to load the codebase as context than to retrain."
zh: Model 内部的数字 —— 常常有数十亿个 —— 在 Training 期间被调校。Model“知道”的一切都存在于其中。Training 设定它们；Inference 原封不动地使用它们。也叫权重（weights）。

从机制上说，Parameters 起着把输入转化为输出（turn input into output）的作用。Next-token prediction 是一次庞大的计算：Context window 里的 Token 输入进来，经过 Parameters 的乘法运算，输出的是对下一个 Token 的预测。Model 内部没有事实数据库，也没有代码查找表——只有这些数字，它们的排列方式让这一计算倾向于产生有用的输出。Model 能从 Training 中背诵出来的事实，比如某个标准库 API，属于 Parametric knowledge：它们存储在 Parameters 中，而不是从任何地方检索来的。

值得内化的细节是：Parameters 在 Training 之后就冻结了。你在一次 Session 里做的任何事都不会改变它们 —— 你做的纠正、你给它看的代码库、它从中得到的教训，都不行。每个 Session 都跑在同一批数字上。这就是 Model 为什么是 Stateless 的，为什么它内置的知识止步于 Knowledge cutoff，以及为什么任何与项目相关的东西都必须改由 Context 传入。改变 Parameters 的唯一途径是更多的 Training —— 而这实际上会产出一个不同的 Model。
用法
"我们能在自己的代码库上对它做 fine-tune 吗？"
"那会更新 Parameters —— 之后就是不同的 Model 了。只针对一个项目的话，把代码库作为 Context 加载，几乎总是比 retrain 更划算。"

summary.zh: Parameters 是训练阶段调出的数值，也称 weights。它们参与每一步 Token 预测，而不是一张可直接查询的事实表。一次 Session 中的对话不会修改 parameters；要让 Model 使用新的项目知识，通常应把资料放进 Context，而不是指望它在聊天时完成训练。

description.en: The process that sets a model's parameters by exposing it to vast amounts of text and adjusting to improve next-token prediction.
description.zh: 通过大量文本反复调整 parameters、改进 next-token prediction 的过程。

en: The process that sets a model's parameters, by exposing it to vast amounts of text and adjusting parameters to improve next-token prediction. A one-time, expensive process done by the model provider. Encompasses both pre-training (the bulk run) and post-training (later refinements like instruction-following and safety); the distinction doesn't matter at this glossary's level.

The mechanism is repetition at scale: show the model a stretch of text, have it predict the next token, nudge the parameters toward whatever the actual next token was, and repeat across trillions of tokens. Nothing is stored as facts or rules — everything the model "knows" is a side effect of getting better at prediction, compressed into the parameters as parametric knowledge.

Two consequences matter day to day. Training ends at a point in time, so the model has a knowledge cutoff — it hasn't seen the library version you upgraded to last month. And training is not something you can do: when the model doesn't know your codebase, your conventions, or your internal APIs, the fix is never "teach the model" — it's putting that material into context, the one input you control.
Usage:
"Can we get it to know our internal API?"
"Not via training — that's a months-long process by the model provider. Load the API docs into context instead, that's the lever you actually have."
zh: 设定 Model 的 Parameters 的过程：通过让 Model 接触海量文本并调整 Parameters 来改进 next-token prediction。这是由 Model provider 完成的、一次性且昂贵的过程。它同时涵盖 pre-training（主体的大规模训练）与 post-training（后续的细化，如 instruction-following 和安全性）；在本词条的层面上，这一区分并不重要。
其机制是大规模重复：给 Model 看一段文本，让它预测下一个 Token，再把 Parameters 朝着实际的下一 Token 微调，如此在数万亿个 Token 上反复进行。没有任何内容以事实或规则的形式被存储——Model "知道" 的一切，都是它在预测上变得更好的副作用，被压缩进 Parameters，成为 parametric knowledge。
有两个后果在日常工作中至关重要。Training 会在某个时间点结束，因此 Model 有 knowledge cutoff——它没见过你上个月才升级到的那个库版本。而且 Training 不是你所能做的事：当 Model 不了解你的代码库、你的约定或内部 API 时，解决办法从来不是 "教 Model"——而是把那些材料放进 Context，那是你唯一能掌控的输入。
用法
"我们能让它了解我们的内部 API 吗？"
"没法靠 Training 做到——那是 Model provider 耗时数月的过程。改为把 API 文档放进 Context，那才是你真正拥有的杠杆。"

summary.zh: Training 用大量文本让 Model 反复预测下一个 Token，再根据误差调整 parameters。这包括大规模预训练，也可包括后续指令训练。训练结束后得到固定的 Model；你的项目代码、最新 API 或团队约定，需要通过 Context 交给它。

description.en: Running a trained model to generate output — what happens on every model provider request. Parameters stay fixed.
description.zh: 运行训练好的 Model 生成输出的过程；每次请求都会发生，parameters 不会因此改变。

en: Running a trained model to generate output — what happens on every model provider request. Parameters stay fixed; the model just does next-token prediction over the context it's given. Cheap relative to training, but billed per token and the dominant cost of using a model.
A model's life splits into two phases:

| Phase     | When it happens                  | What it does                                                    | Parameters    |
| --------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Training  | Once, before release             | Produces the parameters from a training corpus                  | Being written |
| Inference | Every time anyone uses the model | Runs the frozen parameters over your context to generate tokens | Read-only     |

Nothing you do at inference time writes back to the parameters — that's the reason a correction you make today doesn't stick tomorrow. The model that makes the same mistake next session, after you carefully explained the fix, hasn't ignored you; it's incapable of learning from the exchange. The model is stateless — continuity has to come from outside it — from the context window or a memory system.

This mechanism also explains how you're billed. Every request runs the model over the full context, so cost scales with input tokens and output tokens, and an agent making dozens of tool calls pays for inference on each round trip. This is why context size is a cost question as well as a quality one.
Usage:
"Why does the bill scale with usage instead of being a flat license?"

"You're paying for inference — every model provider request runs the model on the provider's hardware. Training already happened, but inference costs accrue per request, and a single turn can expand into many requests when tools are called."
zh: 运行一个训练好的模型来生成输出——也就是每一次 Model provider request 时实际发生的事。Parameters 保持不变；模型只是对给定的 Context 做 Next-token prediction。相对 Training 而言成本很低，但按 Token 计费，并且是使用模型时占主导的成本。
一个 Model 的生命周期分为两个阶段：

| 阶段 | 何时发生 | 它做什么 | Parameters |
| --------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Training | 一次，在发布之前 | 从 Training corpus 中生成 Parameters | 正在写入 |
| Inference | 每次任何人使用 Model 时 | 在你的 Context 上运行冻结的 Parameters，以生成 tokens | 只读 |
你在 Inference 时做的任何事情都不会写回 Parameters——这就是你今天做的一处纠正，到明天并不保留的原因。下一个 Session 里又犯同样错误的那个 Model，即使你已经仔细解释过修正方法，也并不是无视了你；它根本没有能力从这次交流中学习。Model 是 Stateless 的——连续性必须来自它之外——来自 Context window 或 Memory system。
这一机制同样解释了你是如何被计费的。每个请求都会让 Model 在完整的 Context 上运行，因此成本随 Input tokens 和 Output tokens 增长，而一个发起数十次 Tool 调用的 Agent，每一轮往返都要为 Inference 付费。这就是为什么 Context 的大小既是一个成本问题，也是一个质量问题。
用法
"为什么账单会随用量增长，而不是一笔固定的许可费？"
"你是在为 Inference 付费——每一次 Model provider request 都会在 Model provider 的硬件上运行模型。Training 已经发生过了，但 Inference 的成本是按请求累积的，而且当 Tool 被调用时，一次 Turn 可能膨胀成许多次请求。"

summary.zh: Inference 是用已经训练好的 Model 生成输出。每次 Model provider request 都会运行它，但不会改变 parameters。对用户而言，这就是输入 Context、等待 Model 逐个生成输出 Tokens 的过程。

description.en: A dial for how much reasoning the model does before it answers. More effort spends more output tokens for a better shot at hard problems.
description.zh: 控制 Model 回答前投入多少推理计算的设置；更高 Effort 往往消耗更多 output tokens。

en: Effort is a dial for how much reasoning a model does before it answers. Set per model provider request, it controls the length of the thinking the model works through before it starts writing the response you see. That thinking is generated at inference time like everything else; the harness often hides it, but it's real work the model is doing.

Higher effort costs more and runs slower. The reasoning is emitted as tokens, billed as output tokens even when you never see them, and produced one token at a time — so turning effort up lengthens the wait before the answer arrives and adds to the bill. The trade is more deliberation against speed and cost.
Most harnesses expose effort as a small ladder:

| Level  | What it's for                                                          |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Low    | Mechanical edits, lookups, well-specified changes with one clear path. |
| Medium | Everyday coding — the usual default.                                   |
| High   | Tricky bugs, design decisions, multi-step plans.                       |
| Max    | The hardest problems, where a wrong answer is expensive to unwind.     |

The symptom of getting it wrong cuts both ways. Set effort too low on a hard problem and you get a confident, shallow answer that skipped the reasoning the problem needed — it reads fine and is wrong in a way that costs you later. Set it to max for a one-line rename and you sit through a long think that produces nothing the lowest setting wouldn't have.
Match effort to the task, not the session. Turn it up for the part that's genuinely hard to reason about, and back down for the rote work around it.
Usage:
"It keeps botching this concurrency fix — I've re-explained it three times."
"Bump the effort up. That's a reasoning-heavy bug, and on the default setting it's not thinking long enough before it commits to an approach."
zh: Effort 是一个旋钮，用来调节 Model 在作答之前做多少推理。它按 Model provider request 逐次设置，控制 Model 在开始写出你看到的响应之前所经历的思考长度。那段思考和其他一切内容一样，是在 Inference 阶段生成的；Harness 常常会把它隐藏起来，但那是 Model 正在做的真实工作。
更高的 Effort 花费更多、运行更慢。推理是以 Token 的形式产生的，即使你从未看见，也会按 Output tokens 计费，而且是一个 Token 一个 Token 地生成——所以调高 Effort 会拉长答案到来之前的等待，并推高账单。这笔权衡是用更多的深思熟虑，去换速度与成本。
大多数 Harness 会把 Effort 呈现为一个小的档位阶梯：

| 级别 | 适用场景 |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Low | 机械性编辑、查找，以及规格明确、只有一条清晰路径的改动。 |
| Medium | 日常编码——通常的默认选项。 |
| High | 棘手的 bug、设计决策、多步骤计划。 |
| Max | 最难的问题，答错后纠正的代价很高。 |
把 Effort 设错的症状是双向的。在一个难题上把 Effort 设得太低，你会得到一个自信却浅薄的答案，它跳过了这个问题所需的推理——它读起来没问题，却错得会在日后让你付出代价。而为了改一行名字就把 Effort 设到最高，你就得熬过一段漫长的思考，而它产出的一切，最低的档位一样能给。
让 Effort 匹配任务，而不是整个 Session。真正难以推理的部分，就把这一 Turn 的 Effort 调高；围绕它的机械性工作，则调低。
用法
"它总是把这个并发修复搞砸——我已经重新解释了三遍。"
"把 Effort 调高。那是个对推理要求很高的 bug，在默认档位下，它在选定某个方案之前思考得不够久。"

summary.zh: Effort 控制回答前投入的推理量。提高设置通常会消耗更多 output tokens，增加时间和费用，也可能提高复杂任务的成功率。简单的机械工作不一定需要最高 Effort，难题则可能受益于更充分的推理。

description.en: The atomic unit a model reads and writes. Roughly word-sized but not exactly. Context window size, cost, and latency all count tokens.
description.zh: Model 读写文本的基本单位，大小不等同于一个词；上下文容量、成本和延迟都以 Token 计算。

en: The atomic unit a model reads and writes. Roughly word-sized but not exactly — common words are one token, rare or long ones split into several. Context window size, cost, and latency are all counted in tokens.

Text becomes tokens via a tokenizer: a fixed vocabulary of tens of thousands of fragments, learned before training, that splits any input into a sequence of vocabulary entries. The model never sees characters or words — every piece of text is converted to tokens on the way in, and next-token prediction produces output one token at a time on the way out.

As a rule of thumb, a token is about three-quarters of an English word, so a thousand tokens is roughly 750 words. Code is less predictable: common keywords and idioms tokenize compactly, while generated identifiers, hashes, base64 blobs, and minified output split into many tokens per "word". The pattern: text that appeared often in the tokenizer's source material gets short, efficient encodings; text that didn't gets chopped into many small pieces. A hash like a3f9c2e1 never appeared anywhere, so it splits into many tokens, while function is one. This is why a small-looking file full of unusual strings can occupy a surprising share of the context window.

Tokens are the unit everything else is measured in. Cost is per token — providers bill input tokens and output tokens separately. Speed is tokens per second, since output is generated one token at a time. And the context window is a fixed number of tokens, so the token count of your files decides how much fits.
Avoid: "word" — token boundaries don't match word boundaries, and tokens-per-second / tokens-per-dollar are the units that actually matter.
Usage:
"How big is this prompt going to be?"
"Run it through the tokenizer — the schema's compact but the JSON keys are weird, so they'll split into more tokens than you think."
zh: Model 读写的最小原子单位。大致与词等长，但并不精确——常见词是一个 token，罕见或较长的词会拆成好几个。Context window 的大小、成本和延迟都以 token 计数。
文本经由 tokenizer 变成 token：这是一份由数万个片段组成的固定词表，在 training 之前就已学得，能把任意输入切分成一串词表条目。Model 从不接触字符或单词——进入时每段文本都被转换成 token，输出时则由 next-token prediction 一次一个 token 地产生结果。

经验法则是，一个 token 大约相当于四分之三个英文单词，所以一千个 token 约合 750 个单词。代码的可预测性更低：常见的关键字和惯用写法能以紧凑的方式 tokenize，而自动生成的标识符、哈希、base64 数据块以及压缩后的产物，每个「单词」都会拆成许多 token。规律是：在 tokenizer 的语料中频繁出现的文本会得到短小高效的编码；没出现过的则被切成许多小片段。像 a3f9c2e1 这样的哈希从未在任何地方出现过，所以会拆成很多 token，而 function 只占一个。这就是为什么一个看似很小、却塞满罕见字符串的文件，可能占用 context window 中惊人比例的空间。
Token 是衡量其他一切的基准单位。成本按 token 计——服务商分别对 input tokens 和 output tokens 计费。速度是每秒 token 数，因为输出是一次一个 token 生成的。而 context window 是固定的 token 数量，所以你文件的 token 数决定了能装下多少。
避免：「word」——token 的边界与单词边界并不一致，真正重要的单位是 tokens-per-second ／ tokens-per-dollar。
用法
「这个 prompt 会有多大？」
「把它跑一遍 tokenizer——schema 本身很紧凑，但 JSON 的 key 很奇怪，所以它们会比你想象中拆成更多的 token。」

summary.zh: Token 是 Model 的读写单位，不等同于字符或单词；一个常见英文词可能只占一个 Token，长标识符和代码片段则可能拆成多个。Context window 的容量、请求成本与生成速度都按 Tokens 计算，因此长历史和大文件会直接影响工作。

description.en: What the model actually does. Samples one next token from the context, appends it, and runs again. Its only mode of operation.
description.zh: Model 根据当前上下文预测下一个 Token，再把它接到已有内容后重复此过程。

en: What the model actually does. Given a context, it samples one next token, appends it, and runs again. Every output — a sentence, a tool call, a thousand-line file — is built one token at a time. The model has no other mode of operation.

Each step works the same way: the tokens in the context window are run through the parameters, which produce a probability for every token in the vocabulary — this one is very likely next, that one less so. One token is sampled from those probabilities, appended, and the loop runs again with the slightly longer context. That sampling step is why the same prompt produces different output on different runs: non-determinism is built into the mechanism, not a bug layered on top.

Holding onto this mechanism explains behaviour that otherwise looks strange. The model never checks whether a token is true before emitting it — only whether it's likely — which is the root of hallucination. It commits to each token as it goes, so a confident-sounding opening sentence can steer the rest of the answer wrong. And because output tokens are produced strictly one at a time, generation speed puts a floor on how fast any agent can work.
Usage:
"How does the agent 'decide' to call a tool?"
"It doesn't — it's next-token prediction all the way down. The tool call is just a structured string the harness parses out of the output stream."
zh: Model 实际做的事。给定一段 Context，它会采样下一个 Token，将其追加，然后再次运行。每一份输出——一句话、一次 Tool call、一个上千行的文件——都是一次一个 Token 构建出来的。Model 没有其他的运行模式。

每一步的运作方式都相同：Context window 中的 Token 会经过 Parameters 运算，为词表中的每一个 Token 生成一个概率——这个 Token 很可能是下一个，那个则可能性较小。从这些概率中采样出一个 Token，追加到末尾，循环再次运行，此时 Context 略微更长。正是这个采样步骤，使得同一个 prompt 在不同次运行中会产生不同的输出：Non-determinism 内建于这一机制之中，而不是叠加在其之上的 bug。
牢牢把握这套机制，就能解释那些原本显得奇怪的行为。Model 在输出每个 Token 之前，从不检查它是否为真——只判断它是否可能——而这正是 Hallucination 的根源。它一路生成、就一路为每个 Token 定下结论，所以一句听起来自信的开场白，就可能把答案的其余部分带偏。而且由于 Output tokens 严格地一次只生成一个，生成速度就为任何 Agent 的工作速度设定了下限。
用法
"Agent 是如何“决定”调用 Tool 的？"
"并非如此——一路到底都是 Next-token prediction。Tool call 只不过是 Harness 从输出流中解析出来的一段结构化字符串。"

summary.zh: Model 根据当前 Context 为下一个 Token 计算候选概率，选出一个并接到序列末尾，然后继续预测。这是它生成回答、代码和 tool calls 的共同机制；看似不同的任务，底层仍是连续的 Token 预测。

description.en: The same input can produce different output. A property of how models generate text and how providers serve requests.
description.zh: 相同输入也可能得到不同输出，这是文本生成方式和服务端执行方式带来的特性。

en: The same input can produce different output. Run a model twice with identical context and you may get two different answers — sometimes a word, sometimes a completely different approach. Nothing in your code has to change for this to happen.

It's a property of how models generate text, and how model providers serve requests. During inference, the model produces a probability distribution over possible next tokens and one is sampled from it — usually with some randomness on purpose, since always picking the most likely token produces repetitive, lower-quality text. One differently-sampled token early in a response changes every token after it, which is how a single different word becomes a completely different approach. Provider-side serving adds more variation on top: requests are batched together on shared hardware, and tiny floating-point differences between batches can tip a close call between two tokens. There's no setting you can flip to make it all go away.

Expect a spread of results from an agent on the same task. Most responses fall within a reasonable bell curve of quality — that's why the non-determinism is tolerable at all — but the tails are real: some days the model will feel sharp; some days it'll feel like it's lost the plot. Same task, different rolls of the dice. This has two practical consequences. Retrying is a legitimate strategy: a failed attempt is one draw from the distribution, and a fresh attempt at the same task may simply land better. And verification matters more than it would with deterministic tools — you can't test an agent's behaviour once and rely on it repeating, so automated checks have to catch the bad draws.
Be careful not to over-narrativize this. Humans are pattern-matching machines, and a string of bad runs can feel like proof that "the model got worse this week." Usually it's just the distribution.
Usage:
"Claude has been awful today. Did they ship a worse version?"
"Probably not — model output is non-deterministic. You're going to have good days and bad days on the same task. Try again tomorrow before you go looking for a cause."
zh: 相同的输入可能产生不同的输出。用完全一样的 context 把 model 跑两次，你可能会得到两个不同的答案——有时只差一个词，有时则是完全不同的思路。而这一切的发生，不需要你改动代码里的任何东西。

这是 model 生成文本的方式，也是 model 供应商处理请求的方式所决定的固有属性。在 inference 期间，model 会针对可能的下一个 token 生成一个概率分布，再从中采样出一个——通常是刻意加入一些随机性，因为总是挑最可能的那个 token 会产出重复、质量更低的文本。响应早期只要有一个 token 的采样结果不同，它之后的每一个 token 都会随之改变，于是一个词的差异就变成了一条完全不同的思路。供应商一侧的处理还会在此基础上叠加更多变化：请求会在共享硬件上被合并批处理，批与批之间微小的浮点差异就可能让两个 token 之间的接近选择发生倾斜。没有任何设置能一劳永逸地让它消失。

对同一个任务，要预期 agent 给出的是一个结果分布。大多数响应落在一条合理的质量钟形曲线之内——这正是 non-determinism 尚可忍受的原因——但两侧的尾部是真实存在的：有些日子 model 会显得很敏锐，有些日子它则像是完全乱了阵脚。同样的任务，不同的掷骰结果。这带来两个实际后果。重试是一种正当的策略：一次失败的尝试只是从分布里抽出的一个样本，对同一个任务重新来一次，可能恰好就落得更好。而验证比在确定性工具那里更为重要——你没法测试一次 agent 的行为就指望它能重复，所以自动化检查必须能抓住那些抽得不好的结果。
注意不要对此过度地叙事化解读。人类是模式匹配的机器，一连串糟糕的运行会让人感觉那就是「这周 model 变差了」的证明。通常，这只是分布使然。
用法
“Claude 今天糟透了。他们是不是发布了一个更差的版本？”
“大概不是——model 的输出本来就是 non-deterministic 的。同一个任务，你总会有状态好的日子和状态差的日子。明天再试一次，然后再去找原因。”

summary.zh: 同一个提示不保证每次得到完全相同的结果。生成过程中的采样，以及 Provider 的服务方式，都可能引入差异。因此评估 Agent 工作时应看可重复的检查和结果，而不是把一次输出当成永久稳定的行为。

description.en: Whatever serves a model for inference. Usually remote (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google), but can also be local (Ollama, llama.cpp).
description.zh: 提供 Model 推理服务的一方，可以是云端服务，也可以是本地运行环境。

en: Whatever serves a model for inference. Usually a remote service (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google), but can also be local — Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp running on your own machine. The harness doesn't run the model itself; it asks a provider to.

The provider owns the machinery: the parameters live on its hardware, and every model provider request is the harness sending tokens over the network and getting predictions back. That makes the provider the source of a whole category of problems that get misattributed to the model or the harness — rate limits, degraded capacity, and outages all live here. When the agent stalls mid-session or errors on every turn, the provider's status page is worth checking before anything else.

The provider also sets the commercial terms: per-token pricing for input and output tokens, prefix cache discounts, and which models are available at all. Note that the provider and the model's maker can be different companies — Bedrock, Vertex, and OpenRouter serve other people's models.
Local providers trade capability for control: the models that fit on your own hardware are far smaller than the frontier ones, but nothing leaves the machine and there's no bill per token.
Usage:
"Can we run this offline for the air-gapped client?"
"Swap the model provider to a local one — Ollama or llama.cpp on their box. The harness doesn't care, it just hits a different endpoint."
zh: 任何为 Model 提供 Inference 服务的角色。通常是远程服务（Anthropic、OpenAI、Google），但也可以是本地的——运行在你自己机器上的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp。Harness 自己并不运行 Model，而是向 Model provider 发出请求。

Model provider 拥有整套机器：Parameters 存放在它的硬件上，每一次 Model provider request 都是 Harness 通过网络发送 Token 并取回预测结果。这使得 Model provider 成为一整类问题的源头，而这些问题常被错误归咎于 Model 或 Harness——速率限制、容量降级和故障都属于这一类。当 Agent 在 Session 中途停滞，或每个 Turn 都报错时，最值得先检查的就是 Model provider 的状态页。
Model provider 还决定商业条款：输入与 Output tokens 的按 Token 计价、Prefix cache 折扣，以及究竟哪些 Model 可供使用。注意，Model provider 与 Model 的制造方可能是不同的公司——Bedrock、Vertex 和 OpenRouter 就在提供他人的 Model。
本地 Model provider 用能力换取控制权：能装进你自己硬件的 Model 远小于前沿 Model，但没有任何数据离开这台机器，也没有按 Token 计费的账单。
用法
"我们能给这个气隙隔离的客户离线运行吗？"
"把 Model provider 换成本地的——在他们的机器上跑 Ollama 或 llama.cpp。Harness 不在乎，它只是访问另一个 endpoint。"

summary.zh: Model provider 负责托管或运行 Model，并提供推理接口。它可能是云服务，也可能是本地软件。Harness 把 Context 发送给 Provider，再拿回 Model 的输出；不同 Provider 的价格、速度与可用模型可能不同。

description.en: Everything around the model that turns it into an agent: tools, system prompt, context-window management, permissions, hooks.
description.zh: 围绕 Model 的运行框架，负责 tools、system prompt、context 管理、权限与 hooks，使其能作为 Agent 工作。

en: Everything around the model that turns it into an agent: tools, system prompt, context-window management, permissions, hooks. Claude.ai and Claude Code run on the same model but behave differently because their harnesses differ.

The model itself only does one thing: take text in, produce text out. It can't read a file, run a command, or remember the last turn. The harness supplies all of that. It assembles the context for each model provider request, executes the tool calls the model asks for, feeds the tool results back in, stores the session history, asks you for permission before risky actions, and decides when to compact. The agent loop — model proposes, harness executes, repeat — is run by the harness.

This matters for diagnosis. When behaviour differs between two products, or between yesterday and today, the model is often not the variable — the harness is. A different system prompt, a different set of tools, a changed permission default, or a new context-management strategy all change behaviour without any change to the model. It also means the harness is where most of your configuration lives: AGENTS.md files, permission settings, and hooks are all instructions to the harness, not the model.
Examples: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI — and Claude.ai, which is a chat harness rather than a coding one.
Usage:
"Same model, why is Claude Code editing files and Claude.ai just answering questions?"
"Different harnesses — Claude Code has filesystem tools, a different system prompt, and a permission layer. The model isn't the variable here."
zh: 围绕 Model 的一切、把它变成 Agent 的东西：Tool、System prompt、Context 窗口管理、权限、hooks。Claude.ai 和 Claude Code 跑在同一个 Model 上，却表现不同，因为它们的 Harness 不同。

Model 本身只做一件事：把文本收进来，把文本吐出去。它不能读取文件，不能运行命令，也记不住上一个 Turn。这些全都由 Harness 提供。它为每一次 Model provider request 组装 Context，执行 Model 请求的 Tool 调用，把 Tool 结果回填进去，保存 Session 历史，在有风险的操作之前向你请求权限，并决定何时进行压缩。Agent 循环——Model 提议、Harness 执行、如此往复——是由 Harness 来运行的。

这对诊断很重要。当两个产品之间、或者昨天与今天之间的行为出现差异时，变量往往不是 Model——而是 Harness。不同的 System prompt、不同的 Tool 集合、一个被改动的默认权限，或者一种新的 Context 管理策略，都能在 Model 毫无变化的情况下改变行为。这也意味着你的大部分配置都住在 Harness 里：AGENTS.md 文件、权限设置和 hooks，全都是发给 Harness 的指令，而不是发给 Model 的。
例子：Claude Code、Cursor、Codex CLI——以及 Claude.ai，它是一个聊天的 Harness，而不是编码用的 Harness。
用法
"同一个 Model，为什么 Claude Code 在编辑文件，而 Claude.ai 只是在回答问题？"
"不同的 Harness——Claude Code 有 Filesystem 工具、不同的 System prompt，还有一层权限。这里的变量不是 Model。"

summary.zh: Model 只能根据输入生成输出；Harness 才负责把它变成能做事的 Agent。Harness 组织每次请求的 Context，执行 Model 提出的 tool calls，把 tool results 送回去，还管理会话历史、权限与压缩。Agent 的循环是“Model 提议，Harness 执行，再继续”。

description.en: One round-trip from the harness to the model provider. The harness sends context; the provider returns one response.
description.zh: Harness 向 Model provider 发起的一次往返请求：发送 context，接收一次响应。

en: One round-trip from the harness to the model provider. The harness sends the current context; the provider returns one response (a tool call or a final answer). A single user message can spawn many model provider requests if the agent calls tools — each tool result triggers another request.

Each request carries everything: the system prompt, the full conversation so far, every tool result. The model is stateless, so the provider keeps nothing between requests — request forty re-sends what request thirty-nine sent, plus one more tool result. The prefix cache exists to make this repetition affordable.

The request is also the unit of billing. Input tokens, output tokens, and cache discounts are all counted per request, which is why an innocuous-looking question can cost a surprising amount: the cost isn't proportional to your message, it's proportional to the number of requests times the size of the context each one carries.
It's worth keeping the request distinct from the turn. A turn is one exchange with you, and a single turn — "fix the failing test" — plays out as a chain of requests:

| Request | Model returns                     | Harness then                          |
| ------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| 1       | Tool call: run the tests          | Runs them, appends the failure output |
| 2       | Tool call: read the test file     | Appends the file contents             |
| 3       | Tool call: read the source file   | Appends the file contents             |
| 4       | Tool call: edit the source file   | Applies the edit, appends the result  |
| 5       | Tool call: run the tests again    | Runs them, appends the pass output    |
| 6       | Final answer: "fixed, tests pass" | Shows it to you                       |
Six requests for one turn — each one re-sending the whole context. When you wonder where the tokens went, count the requests, not the turns.
Usage:
"One question burned forty thousand tokens?"
"Look at the tool calls — twelve grep, eight read, four edits. Each tool result spawns another model provider request, and the whole session prefix re-sends every time."
zh: Harness 到 Model provider 的一次往返。Harness 发送当前 Context；Model provider 返回一个响应（一次 Tool call 或最终答案）。如果 Agent 调用 Tool，单条用户消息可以派生出许多次 Model provider request —— 每个 Tool result 都会触发另一次 request。

每一次 request 都携带全部内容：System prompt、到目前为止的完整对话、每一个 Tool result。Model 是 Stateless 的，因此 Model provider 在 request 之间不保留任何东西 —— 第四十次 request 会重新发送第三十九次 request 发过的内容，再加上一个新的 Tool result。Prefix cache 的存在就是为了让这种重复变得可负担。
request 也是计费单位。Input tokens、Output tokens 和缓存折扣都按 request 计算，这就是为什么一个看起来无害的问题可能花费惊人：成本并不与你的消息成正比，而是与 request 的数量乘以每一个 request 所携带的 Context 大小成正比。
值得把 request 与 Turn 区分开来。一个 Turn 是与你的一个来回，而单个 Turn ——「修复失败的测试」—— 会展开成一连串 request：

| 请求 | Model 返回 | 接着 Harness |
| ------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| 1 | Tool call：运行测试 | 运行测试，追加失败输出 |
| 2 | Tool call：读取测试文件 | 追加文件内容 |
| 3 | Tool call：读取源文件 | 追加文件内容 |
| 4 | Tool call：编辑源文件 | 应用编辑，追加结果 |
| 5 | Tool call：再次运行测试 | 运行测试，追加通过输出 |
| 6 | 最终答案："已修复，测试通过" | 展示给你 |
一个 Turn 六次 request —— 每一次都重新发送整个 Context。当你疑惑 token 都去哪了，数 request，而不是数 Turn。
用法
「一个问题烧掉了四万个 token？」
「看看那些 Tool call —— 十二次 grep、八次 read、四次 edit。每个 Tool result 都会派生另一次 Model provider request，而整个 Session 前缀每次都会重新发送。」

summary.zh: 这是 Harness 与 Model provider 的一次往返。Harness 发送当前 Context；Provider 运行 Model 并返回一次响应。一个用户 Turn 可能包含多次请求，因为 Agent 需要在工具调用与结果之间反复继续。

description.en: Tokens the harness sends on each model provider request. Billed at a lower rate than output tokens.
description.zh: Harness 每次请求发送给 Model 的 Tokens，通常按低于 output tokens 的费率计费。

en: Tokens the harness sends on each model provider request — the system prompt, the conversation history, tool results, everything the model reads before it writes. Billed at a lower rate than output tokens, because they are less expensive to process than output tokens.

When doing AI coding, input tokens make up most of your bill. The model is stateless, so each turn re-sends the entire session as input: your first message, every response, every tool result since. The input for turn fifty contains the previous forty-nine turns. A single model provider request might produce a few hundred output tokens but re-send a hundred thousand input tokens of accumulated history.

The prefix cache reduces the cost: history that exactly matches a previous request is billed as cheap cache tokens rather than full-price input. When input costs still hurt, the fix is to shrink what gets re-sent — clearing or compacting between tasks.
Usage:
"Bill's high but the agent's barely writing anything."
"It's the input tokens — every turn re-sends the whole session. Without the prefix cache you re-pay for the history each request."
zh: Harness 在每次 Model provider request 中发送的 tokens —— System prompt、对话历史、Tool results，也就是 Model 在写出内容之前读到的全部内容。它们的计费费率低于 Output tokens，因为处理它们的成本比 Output tokens 更低。

做 AI coding 时，Input tokens 构成了你账单的大部分。Model 是 Stateless 的，所以每个 Turn 都会把整个 Session 作为输入重新发送：你的第一条消息、之后的每一次回复、自那以来的每一个 Tool result。第五十个 Turn 的输入里，包含了前面的四十九个 Turn。单次 Model provider request 可能只产出几百个 Output tokens，却要重新发送累积下来的十万个 Input tokens 历史。
Prefix cache 降低了这项成本：与先前请求完全匹配的历史，按便宜的 Cache tokens 计费，而不是按全价输入计费。当输入成本依然让人吃不消时，解决办法就是缩小被重新发送的内容 —— 在任务之间 Clearing 或 compacting。
用法
“账单很高，可 Agent 几乎什么都没写。”
“问题出在 Input tokens —— 每个 Turn 都在重新发送整个 Session。没有 Prefix cache，你每次请求都要为历史再付一次钱。”

summary.zh: Input tokens 是发送到 Provider 的内容，包括指令、对话历史、工具结果和当前任务资料。每次请求都可能重复发送一部分历史，因此长 Session 会抬高成本。命中 Prefix cache 的部分可能按更低费率计算。

description.en: Tokens the model generates back. Billed at a higher rate than input tokens, since they cost more compute to produce.
description.zh: Model 生成并返回的 Tokens；因为生成计算成本更高，通常比 input tokens 贵。

en: Tokens the model generates back. Billed at a higher rate than input tokens — commonly around five times the rate — since they cost more compute to produce.

Everything the model writes counts: the prose you read, the code it emits, tool calls, and any extended thinking the model does before answering. That last one surprises people — reasoning tokens are billed as output even when the harness often doesn't show them to you, and turning up effort spends more of them.

Output tokens also set the pace of a session. The model reads input quickly but generates output one token at a time, so when a turn feels slow, it's almost always the output being written, not the input being read. A long wait usually means a long answer is coming.
Usage:
"The refactor session is burning through credit even though the inputs are small."
"Agent's rewriting whole files instead of patching. Output tokens cost roughly five times the input rate — get it emitting edits and the bill drops."
zh: Model 生成并返回的 Tokens。计费费率高于 input tokens —— 通常约为其五倍 —— 因为生成它们需要消耗更多计算。
Model 写下的所有内容都算数：你读到的文字、它生成的代码、tool calls，以及 Model 在作答之前进行的任何 extended thinking。最后一项常让人意外 —— reasoning tokens 也按 output 计费，即便 Harness 往往并不把它们展示给你，而调高 Effort 会消耗更多这类 Token。
Output tokens 同时也决定了一个 Session 的节奏。Model 读取 input 很快，但生成 output 是一个 Token 一个 Token 地进行的；所以当一个 Turn 感觉慢时，几乎总是因为正在写 output，而不是正在读 input。漫长的等待通常意味着一个很长的回答即将到来。
用法
"这次重构 Session 正在快速烧掉额度，尽管 input 的体量很小。"
"Agent 在重写整个文件，而不是打补丁。Output tokens 的费率大约是 input 的五倍 —— 让它改为输出 edit，账单就会降下来。"

summary.zh: Output tokens 是 Model 新生成的内容，既可能是给用户的文字，也可能是 tool call 参数。生成每个 Token 都要继续运行推理，因此它们通常比 input tokens 贵，增加 Effort 也常使这部分用量上升。

description.en: The provider-side store that lets consecutive requests skip re-processing a shared prefix, billing those tokens at a lower rate.
description.zh: Provider 端复用请求共同前缀的缓存，让重复的 input tokens 不必再次完整处理。

en: The provider-side store that lets consecutive model provider requests skip re-processing a shared prefix. When the start of a request matches the start of a recent one — same system prompt, same history up to some point — the provider reuses its prior work and bills those tokens as cache tokens at a much lower rate.

The cache pays off because sessions grow append-only. Every request re-sends the whole history as input tokens (see that entry for why), and in a normal session the history only changes at the end — each request is the previous one plus a few new messages. The provider processes the long shared beginning once, stores the result, and picks up from where the prefix ends. Without the cache, a 50-turn session would pay to re-process turn one fifty times.

Caches also expire. How long an entry stays warm varies per model provider — typically minutes, not hours. Leave a session idle past the window and the next request rebuilds the prefix at full price once before caching resumes. This is mostly a harness builder's concern; as a user, the visible effect is that requests after a long pause cost more than the ones before it.
Usage:
"Why did the bill spike halfway through the session?"
"Harness started injecting the current time into the system prompt every turn. Prefix cache breaks at the first changed token, so every request after that billed at full rate."
zh: Prefix cache 是 provider 侧的一种存储，让连续的 model provider 请求可以跳过对共享前缀的重复处理。当一个请求的开头与近期某个请求的开头一致时——相同的 system prompt、到某一点为止相同的历史——provider 会复用先前的处理结果，并按低得多的费率把这些 token 计为 Cache tokens。

缓存之所以划算，是因为 session 是只追加式增长的。每个请求都会把整段历史作为 Input tokens 重新发送（原因见该词条），而在正常的 session 中，历史只在末尾发生变化——每个请求都是前一个请求再加上几条新消息。provider 只需处理一次那段很长的共享开头，把结果存下来，然后从前缀结束的地方继续。没有缓存的话，一个 50 个 turn 的 session 就要为把第一个 turn 重复处理 50 次而付费。
缓存还会过期。一条条目能保持热的时长因 model provider 而异——通常是几分钟，而不是几小时。让一个 session 闲置超过这个窗口，下一个请求就要按全价重建一次前缀，之后缓存才恢复。这主要是 harness 构建者关心的问题；对用户来说，可见的效果是长时间暂停之后的请求比之前的更贵。
用法
“为什么账单在 session 进行到一半时突然飙升？”
“Harness 开始在每个 turn 往 system prompt 里注入当前时间。Prefix cache 在第一个变化的 token 处就失效了，所以之后的每个请求都按全价计费。”

summary.zh: 连续请求常有相同的开头，例如固定指令和未变的会话历史。Provider 可以缓存这个共同前缀，在下一次请求中复用处理结果。缓存通常降低费用和延迟，但只有前缀保持一致时才容易命中。

description.en: Input tokens the provider has cached from a previous request via its prefix cache, billed at a much lower rate.
description.zh: 命中 prefix cache 的 input tokens，通常按更低的费率计费。

en: Input tokens the provider has cached from a previous model provider request so it doesn't have to re-process them. When consecutive requests share a prefix, the provider reuses the work via its prefix cache and bills the cached portion at a much lower rate. The lever that makes long sessions affordable — without it, every turn re-pays for the whole history.

The reason this matters is how sessions are billed. The model is stateless, so every request resends the entire conversation — system prompt, every message, every tool result — as input tokens. By turn fifty, each request carries fifty turns of history, and you'd pay full rate on all of it, every time. The cache changes the maths: tokens the provider has already processed in an identical prefix are billed as cache tokens, often at a tenth of the input rate or less. On a long session, most of what you send is cache tokens, and the bill stays sane.
An example shows when tokens are cached and when they're not. Each letter stands for a block of conversation content; each request sends the conversation so far:

| Request sends | Cached  | Billed at full rate | Why                                               |
| ------------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| AB          | nothing | AB                | First request — nothing to match against          |
| ABC         | AB    | C                 | AB is an exact prefix of the previous request   |
| ABCD        | ABC   | D                 | Prefix still intact                               |
| AXCD        | A     | XCD               | An edit changed B to X; the match fails there |

The cache is fragile in a specific way: it matches exact prefixes. If anything changes earlier in the conversation — the harness reorders content, a timestamp updates, a file's representation shifts — the cache misses from that point onward and everything after it is billed at full input rate. Caches also expire after a few minutes of inactivity, so a session resumed after a long pause re-pays its history once. When a session's cost jumps without an obvious cause, compare cache tokens to input tokens in the usage report — a broken cache shows up there first.
Usage:
"Cost on long sessions is brutal — eight bucks for a refactor."
"Check the cache tokens. If the harness is reordering the system prompt or files between turns, the prefix breaks and you re-pay full input rate every request."
zh: Input tokens 是 Model provider 从先前的 Model provider request 中缓存下来的 token，因此不必重新处理。当连续的请求共享同一个前缀时，Model provider 会通过其 Prefix cache 复用这份处理工作，并对缓存部分按低得多的费率计费。这是让长 Session 变得可负担的杠杆——没有它，每个 Turn 都要为整段历史重复付费。

这一点之所以重要，在于 Session 的计费方式。Model 是 Stateless 的，所以每次请求都会把整个对话——System prompt、每一条消息、每一个 Tool result——作为 Input tokens 重新发送一遍。到了第五十个 Turn，每个请求都携带五十个 Turn 的历史，而你每次都要为全部这些内容按全价付费。缓存改变了这笔账：Model provider 已在相同前缀中处理过的 token 会按 Cache tokens 计费，通常只有 Input tokens 费率的十分之一甚至更低。在长 Session 中，你发送的内容大部分都是 Cache tokens，账单也就保持在合理范围。
一个例子可以说明 token 何时会被缓存、何时不会。每个字母代表一块对话内容；每次请求都会发送到目前为止的整段对话：

| 请求发送内容 | 已缓存 | 按全价计费 | 原因 |
| ------------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| AB | 无 | AB | 第一个请求 — 没有可匹配的内容 |
| ABC | AB | C | AB 是上一个请求的精确前缀 |
| ABCD | ABC | D | 前缀仍然完整 |
| AXCD | A | XCD | 一次编辑把 B 改成了 X；匹配在此处失败 |

缓存的脆弱之处很具体：它只匹配完全一致的前缀。如果对话中较早的位置发生了变化——Harness 重新排列了内容、某个时间戳发生了更新、某个文件的呈现形式发生了改变——那么从该点起缓存就会失效（cache miss），其后的一切都按 Input tokens 全价计费。缓存还会在闲置几分钟后过期，所以长时间暂停后恢复的 Session 要为历史重新付费一次。当某个 Session 的成本在没有明显原因的情况下跳升时，去 usage report 里对比 Cache tokens 与 Input tokens——缓存失效会最先在那里显露出来。
用法
"长 Session 的成本太狠了——一次 refactor 就要八美元。"
"检查一下 Cache tokens。如果 Harness 在 Turn 之间重新排列 System prompt 或文件，前缀就会断裂，你每次请求都要按 Input tokens 全价重新付费。"

summary.zh: Cache tokens 是命中 Prefix cache 的 input tokens。它们仍属于发送给 Model 的 Context，但 Provider 不必按普通输入重新处理，通常以更低费率计费。实际规则取决于 Provider。

description.en: Carries no information forward. The model is stateless across requests; an agent is stateless across sessions by default.
description.zh: 不自动携带上一次的信息；Model 每次请求都是 stateless，Agent 默认也不会跨 Session 记忆。

en: Carries no information forward. The model is stateless across model provider requests — each request resends the full context window, because the model has no way to see anything else. An agent is stateless across sessions by default: a new session starts empty, with no trace of prior ones. Counterpart to stateful.

The model itself is permanently stateless: its parameters are frozen after training, and nothing you do at inference changes them. The model doesn't learn from your corrections, doesn't remember being told the same thing yesterday, and isn't getting to know you — however much the conversation feels otherwise. The feeling of continuity within a session is manufactured by the harness, which keeps the transcript and re-sends it with every request. The model isn't remembering the conversation; it's re-reading it.

The practical consequence: if you want something remembered across sessions, you have to write it down somewhere the agent will read it back. That's what AGENTS.md files, memory systems, and handoff artifacts are — files that get loaded into the context of future sessions, standing in for the memory the model doesn't have. When the agent keeps making a mistake you've corrected before, the question isn't why it didn't learn — it can't — but where that correction should be written down so every future session reads it.
Usage:
"Why does it forget the convention every time I clear?"
"The model's stateless — the new session starts empty. If you want it carried, write it to AGENTS.md or a memory file the harness loads at session start."
zh: 不向前携带任何信息。在多次 model provider 请求之间，model 是 stateless 的——每次请求都会重发完整的 context window，因为 model 没有任何别的途径看到其他内容。默认情况下，agent 跨 session 时是 stateless 的：新 session 从空开始，没有先前 session 的任何痕迹。是 stateful 的对立面。

model 本身永久处于 stateless 状态：它的 parameters 在 training 之后就被冻结，你在 inference 时做的任何事都不会改变它们。model 不会从你的纠正中学习，不记得昨天被告诉过同样的事，也不是在逐渐了解你——无论这场对话感觉上多么像那么回事。session 内部的连续感是由 harness 制造出来的：它保存对话记录，并在每次请求时重新发送。model 并不是在记住这场对话，而是在重新阅读它。

实际后果是：如果你想让某些东西跨 session 被记住，就必须把它写下来，放在 agent 会读回来的地方。AGENTS.md 文件、memory 系统、handoff 产物就是干这个的——这些文件会被载入未来 session 的 context，代替 model 并不拥有的那份记忆。当 agent 一再犯你之前纠正过的错误时，问题不是它为什么没学会——它学不会——而是这条纠正应该写在哪里，好让未来每一个 session 都读到它。
用法
“我每次 clear 之后，它为什么就把这个约定忘了？”
“model 是 stateless 的——新 session 从空开始。如果你想让它被带过去，就把它写进 AGENTS.md，或者写进 harness 在 session 开始时加载的 memory 文件。”

summary.zh: Stateless 指一次运行不会自动记住上一次。Model 本身每次请求都重新接收 Context；默认情况下，Agent 跨 Session 也不会保留信息。需要延续进度时，必须由 Harness、Memory system 或明确的 Handoff 提供内容。

description.en: The relevant information the agent has access to right now — what the agent knows that's pertinent to the task.
description.zh: Agent 此刻可用、且与当前任务有关的信息。

en: The relevant information the agent has access to right now. The abstract noun — not the raw input the model sees (that's the context window), not the running history (that's the session), but what the agent knows that's pertinent to the task. "Loading something into context" means making it part of this set; "context engineering" is the discipline of curating it.
The three terms separate cleanly:

| Term           | What it names                                                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Context        | The task-relevant information the agent currently has               |
| Context window | The literal token sequence the model sees per request |
| Session        | The running conversation the harness stores         |

The separation matters because context is a measure of quality, not quantity. A context window can be nearly full and the context still poor — thousands of tokens of stale tool output, none of it about the task at hand. It can also be nearly empty and the context excellent: the one type definition the task turns on.

Most day-to-day failures trace back to context. When the agent invents an API, contradicts a decision, or guesses at a schema, the first question is what was in context when it did — usually the relevant fact was never loaded, or was buried under attention degradation. The fix is curation: load what the task needs, keep out what it doesn't.
Usage:
"It keeps inventing fields that aren't in the type."
"The type file isn't in context — it's reading the call sites and guessing. Read the definition in first."
zh: Agent 当前可访问的相关信息。这是抽象名词——不是 Model 看到的原始输入（那是 Context window），不是运行中的历史记录（那是 Session），而是 Agent 所掌握的、与任务相关的信息。"把某内容加载进 Context"意味着让它成为这一集合的一部分；"Context engineering"（上下文工程）就是策展它的学科。
这三个术语有着清晰的边界：

| 术语 | 所指内容 |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Context | Agent 当前拥有的与任务相关的信息 |
| Context window | Model 每次请求时实际看到的字面 Token 序列 |
| Session | Harness 存储的进行中的对话 |
这种区分之所以重要，是因为 Context 衡量的是质量，而非数量。Context window 可以几乎填满而 Context 依然很差——成千上万个 token 的陈旧 Tool 输出，没有一条关乎当前任务。它也可以几乎为空而 Context 极佳：一条定义类型，而任务正取决于它。
大多数日常失败都可追溯到 Context。当 Agent 编造出一个 API、与某个决定相矛盾，或对 schema 妄加猜测时，首先要问的是它做这些时 Context 里有什么——通常那个相关事实从未被加载，或者被淹没在 Attention degradation 之中。解决办法就是策展：加载任务所需，排除任务所不需。
用法
"它老是编造类型里根本没有的字段。"
"类型文件不在 Context 里——它在读调用点然后猜。先把定义读进来。"

summary.zh: Context 是 Agent 眼前可用且与任务有关的信息，不只是聊天记录。它可以包括代码、文档、工具结果和用户指令。Model 不能凭空看到环境里的文件；相关事实要先被装入 Context，才会影响当前回答。

description.en: Everything the model sees on each model provider request. Finite, model-specific, the only surface through which the model perceives.
description.zh: 每次 Model provider request 中 Model 能看到的全部内容；容量有限，并且因 Model 而异。

en: Everything the model sees on each model provider request. Finite, model-specific, and the only surface through which the model perceives anything.

It's a single sequence of tokens: the system prompt, the conversation so far, every tool result the harness has fed back in. If something is in that sequence, the model can use it; if it isn't, the model doesn't know it exists — not your codebase, not the file you edited yesterday, not the instruction you gave three sessions ago. Anything outside the window has to be brought in, usually via a tool call, before it can affect anything.

Finite means it fills up. Every turn appends more — your messages, the model's responses, tool results — and a long session will eventually hit the limit, forcing compaction or clearing. It also means everything in the window competes: each token you load is one less available for the rest, and content you didn't need still occupies the model's attention. The practical stance is to treat the window as a budget — load what the task needs, leave the rest out.
Avoid: "memory" — the context window is working state and doesn't persist across sessions. Memory is a separate concept layered on top.
Usage:
"Can I just paste the whole monorepo into the prompt?"
"The context window's 200k tokens — that's maybe a fifth of the repo. Pick the files the task touches, leave the rest behind a tool call."
zh: Model 在每次 Model provider request 时看到的一切。它是有限的、因 Model 而异的，也是 Model 感知外界的唯一界面。

它是一条单一的 Token 序列：System prompt、到目前为止的对话、Harness 回填进来的每一个 Tool result。某个东西在这条序列里，Model 就能用它；不在这条序列里，Model 就不知道它存在——不是你的代码库，不是你昨天编辑的文件，也不是你三个 Session 之前给出的指令。窗口之外的一切都必须先被取进来（通常是通过一次 Tool call），然后才能影响任何事。

有限意味着它会被填满。每一 Turn 都在往里追加——你的消息、Model 的回应、Tool result——一个长 Session 最终会触到上限，被迫进行 Compaction 或 Clearing。有限还意味着窗口里的一切都在竞争：你载入的每一个 Token，都让其余内容可用的额度少一份；而你并不需要的内容，仍然占据着 Model 的注意力。务实的立场是把窗口当作一笔预算——任务需要什么就载入什么，其余的都不放进去。
避免：“memory”——Context window 是工作状态，不跨 Session 持久化。Memory 是叠加在其之上的另一个概念。
用法
“我能把整个 monorepo 直接粘到 prompt 里吗？”
“Context window 的 200k Token——大概只占这个仓库的五分之一。挑出任务会碰到的文件，其余的留在一次 Tool call 之后去取。”

summary.zh: Context window 是一次请求中 Model 实际看到的全部 Tokens，有固定容量且因 Model 而异。它可能装着 system prompt、历史消息、文件和工具结果。窗口装满后必须丢弃、压缩或重新选择内容；容量更大也不代表每个细节都同样容易被注意到。

description.en: Carries information forward. Sessions are stateful across turns; agents can be made stateful across sessions via a memory system.
description.zh: 能把信息带到后续步骤；Session 在多个 Turn 之间保持状态，Agent 也可借助 Memory system 跨 Session 保持状态。

en: Carries information forward. A session is stateful across turns — context accumulates as the session runs, which is why long sessions drift into the dumb zone. An agent can be made stateful across sessions by adding a memory system that persists information into the environment and reloads it at the start of future sessions. The model is never stateful; any apparent continuity is the harness re-feeding context. Counterpart to stateless.
Where state lives at each layer:

| Layer       | Stateful?       | How                                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Model       | Never           | Parameters are frozen; it sees only what's in each request                                          |
| Session     | Across turns    | The harness appends every message and tool result to the context                                 |
| Harness     | Across sessions | Memory files, AGENTS.md, handoff artifacts — written down, reloaded later |
| Environment | Always          | Files persist whether or not any session is running                                                                    |

Each layer's statefulness is built by re-reading something stored a layer below: the session feels continuous because the harness re-sends the message history to the stateless model, and the agent remembers across sessions because the harness re-loads files from the environment. No state is ever stored in the model itself.

State isn't always wanted. Everything carried forward influences what comes next, so a wrong assumption made early in a session is carried forward too. Clearing is the deliberate act of throwing session state away and starting from what's written down.
Usage:
"It remembered my preferences from yesterday — does that mean the model learned them?"
"No, the agent's stateful because the harness wrote them to a memory file and reloaded them at session start. The model itself saw nothing of yesterday."
zh: 把信息向前传递。session 在多个轮次之间是 stateful 的——随着 session 运行，context 不断累积，这正是长 session 会滑入 dumb zone 的原因。通过添加一个 memory system，把信息持久化到 environment 中，并在未来 session 启动时重新载入，agent 就能跨 session 变为 stateful。model 从来不是 stateful 的；任何表面上连续的表现，都是 harness 在重新投喂 context。与 stateless 相对。
状态在各层分别存放在哪里：

| 层级 | 是否 Stateful？ | 方式 |
| ----------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Model | 从不 | Parameters 被冻结；它只能看到每次请求里的内容 |
| Session | 跨轮次 | Harness 会把每条消息和 Tool result 追加到 Context 中 |
| Harness | 跨 Session | 记忆文件、AGENTS.md、Handoff 产物 —— 写下来，之后再重新载入 |
| Environment | 始终 | 无论是否有 Session 在运行，文件都持久存在 |
每一层的 stateful 特性，都是靠重新读取存放在下一层的东西构建起来的：session 之所以感觉连续，是因为 harness 把消息历史重新发送给 stateless 的 model；agent 之所以能跨 session 记住内容，是因为 harness 从 environment 重新载入文件。状态从来不会存储在 model 自身之中。
状态并不总是想要的。所有被向前携带的内容都会影响接下来发生的事，所以 session 早期做出的错误假设也会被一并携带下去。Clearing 是一种刻意行为：把 session 状态丢掉，从已经写下来的内容重新开始。
用法
"它记住了我昨天的偏好——这是不是意味着 model 学会了它们？"
"不是，agent 之所以是 stateful 的，是因为 harness 把它们写进了一个 memory 文件，并在 session 启动时重新载入。model 自身对昨天一无所知。"

summary.zh: Stateful 意味着信息能延续到下一步。Session 会积累 Turn 历史，因此在会话内表现为有状态；Memory system 可以把部分信息保存到环境中，让后续 Session 再读取。状态总需要某个具体的承载机制。

description.en: A model harnessed with tools, a system prompt, and a context window, that takes turns with a user. The model in motion.
description.zh: 由 Model 加上 Harness、tools、system prompt 和 context window 构成的可交互工作系统。

en: A model harnessed with tools, a system prompt, and a context window, that takes turns with a user. Claude Code is an agent. Cursor is an agent. Claude.ai is an agent. An agent is what you actually talk to — it's the model in motion, configured for a purpose.

Unlike most terms in this dictionary, "agent" doesn't name a mechanical part. The model is a file of parameters; the harness is software you can point at. The agent is neither — it's the unit you're speaking to. People anthropomorphize AI constantly, and the agent is the anthropomorphized unit: the thing you delegate to, the thing that reads your message and answers, the "it" in "it broke the build again". When you say the agent did something, you mean the model-plus-harness did it, but you're addressing the combination as a single actor.
The idea is older than this wave of AI. Software agents — programs you delegate a goal to, which act on your behalf — have been a concept for as long as AI has.
Avoid: "the AI", "the bot" (too vague — they hide whether you mean the parameters or the harnessed thing).
Usage:
"Which agent are you using for the migration?"
"Claude Code locally, Cursor for the UI work — same model underneath, different harnesses."
zh: 一个用工具、System prompt 和 Context window 装配起来的 Model，与用户轮流对话。Claude Code 是一个 Agent。Cursor 是一个 Agent。Claude.ai 是一个 Agent。Agent 就是你实际对话的那个东西——它是运转中的 Model，为某个目的而配置。

与这本词典里大多数词条不同，「agent」指的不是某个机械部件。Model 是一个 Parameters 文件；Harness 是你能指明路径的软件。Agent 两者都不是——它是你在对话的那个单元。人们一直在把 AI 拟人化，而 Agent 就是那个被拟人化的单元：你把事情托付给它的东西，读取你的消息并作答的东西，「它又把构建搞坏了」里的那个「它」。当你说 Agent 做了某件事，你是指 Model 加 Harness 做了这件事，但你是把这个组合当作一个单一行动者来对话。
这个想法比这一波 AI 更早。软件 Agent——你把一个目标托付给它、由它代你行动的程序——其历史与 AI 本身一样长。
避免：「the AI」「the bot」（太含糊——它们让你看不出你指的是 Parameters 还是那个被装配好的东西）。
用法
「这次迁移你用哪个 Agent？」
「本地用 Claude Code，UI 的部分用 Cursor——底层是同一个 Model，Harness 不同。」

summary.zh: Agent 是 Model 在 Harness 中运行形成的工作系统。Harness 给它指令、Context 与 tools，再把 Model 的决定转换成实际操作；因此“Agent 能读文件”描述的是整个系统，而非 Model 单独拥有文件权限。

description.en: The instructions the harness prepends to every model provider request — the agent's standing brief. Usually stable across a session.
description.zh: Harness 在每次请求前加入的常驻指令，通常在一个 Session 内保持稳定。

en: The instructions the harness prepends to every model provider request — the agent's standing brief: who it is, how to behave, which tools it can call, what conventions to follow. Usually stable across a session.

The system prompt is written by the harness vendor, not by you, and in coding harnesses it's big — often tens of thousands of tokens of behavioural rules, tool descriptions, and edge-case handling, all paid as input tokens on every turn. Your own standing instructions ride along with it: files like AGENTS.md are loaded next to the system prompt at the start of the session, so the model reads the vendor's brief and yours together before it ever sees your message.
Because it's identical on every request, it forms the start of the prefix cache — which is part of why harnesses keep it fixed for a whole session rather than editing it as they go.

Models are trained to prioritise the system prompt over user messages. So when an agent insists on a convention you never asked for, or formats output in a way you can't shake, it's usually obeying its system prompt — and your message is losing the argument. Some harnesses are customisable: they give you full access to the system prompt, so you can read what the agent is actually being told and change it.
Usage:
"Two harnesses, same model, totally different behavior on the same prompt."
"Different system prompts. One's tuned for terse code edits, the other for explaining — that's where the divergence lives, before your message even arrives."
zh: Harness 在每次 Model provider request 之前预置的指令——Agent 的常驻简报：它是谁、该如何行事、可以调用哪些 Tool、遵循哪些约定。通常在 Session 内保持稳定。

System prompt 由 Harness 厂商撰写，而非你自己，而且在编码类 Harness 里它体量很大——常常是数万 token 的行为规则、Tool 描述和边界情况处理，且每个 Turn 都作为 Input tokens 付费。你自己的常驻指令也与它同行：AGENTS.md 这类文件会在 Session 开始时紧挨着 System prompt 一并加载，因此 Model 在看到你的消息之前，就已经把厂商的简报和你的简报一起读过了。
因为它在每次请求中都完全相同，所以构成了 Prefix cache 的开头部分——这也是 Harness 会在整个 Session 中让它保持不变、而不是边用边改的原因之一。
Model 被训练成把 System prompt 置于用户消息之上。所以当 Agent 坚持一条你从未要求的约定，或以一种你甩不掉的方式格式化输出时，它通常是在服从自己的 System prompt——而你的消息正在这场争论中落败。有些 Harness 是可定制的：它们让你完全访问 System prompt，因此你可以读到 Agent 实际被告知了什么，并加以修改。
用法
"两个 Harness，同一个 Model，面对同一个 prompt 却表现完全不同。"
"System prompt 不同。一个为简洁的代码编辑调优，另一个为讲解调优——分歧就出在这里，在你的消息到达之前就已经存在。"

summary.zh: System prompt 是 Harness 在请求前放入 Context 的常驻指令，规定角色、边界和工作方式。它通常在一个 Session 内稳定，但不能代替真实工具或最新资料。诊断输出问题时，需要同时看 system prompt、Context 与 Harness 行为。

description.en: One bounded run of interaction with an agent. Starts empty, accumulates, ends when cleared, closed, or compacted into a fresh session.
description.zh: 与 Agent 进行的一段有边界的连续交互；它积累历史，也会结束或被压缩。

en: One bounded run of interaction with an agent. Starts empty, accumulates messages, tool results, and files read, and ends when cleared, closed, or compacted into a fresh session. The session is what fills the context window: if the context window is the box, the session is the stuff slowly filling it up. Work too large for a single context window must be split across sessions.

The session's message history is the agent's working memory. The model is stateless, so everything it appears to remember — what you asked for, what the tests said, what it decided three turns ago — is in the message history, re-sent with every model provider request. Whatever isn't in the session doesn't exist for the agent.

That memory ends with the session. A new session starts from nothing: the agent that knew your codebase well at the end of yesterday's session knows none of it this morning. What survives is the filesystem — files written during one session can be read by the next, which is what handoffs, memory systems, and AGENTS.md rely on.

You choose where a session ends. Everything in a session influences every later turn, so unrelated tasks done in one session leave residue that colours the next answer. One task per session keeps the context relevant; finishing a task is a natural point to clear.
Usage:
"How long can one session run before it falls apart?"
"Depends on the work — a focused refactor stays sharp longer than open-ended research. Once the session bloats, hand off or compact, don't push through."
zh: 与 Agent 进行的一次有边界的交互运行。它从空开始，不断累积消息、Tool 结果和读取过的文件，并在被清除、关闭或压缩进一个全新的 Session 时结束。Session 就是填满 Context window 的东西：如果 Context window 是盒子，Session 就是缓慢把它填满的内容。超出单个 Context window 承载能力的工作，必须拆分到多个 Session 中完成。
Session 的消息历史就是 Agent 的工作记忆。Model 是 Stateless 的，所以它看上去记得的一切——你要求过什么、测试说了什么、三个 Turn 之前它决定了什么——都在消息历史里，并随每一次 Model provider request 重新发送。不在 Session 里的东西，对 Agent 来说就不存在。
这份记忆随 Session 一起结束。新的 Session 从零开始：昨天 Session 结束时还很熟悉你代码库的 Agent，今天早上对它一无所知。能留存下来的是 Filesystem——在一个 Session 中写入的文件可以被下一个 Session 读取，交接、记忆系统和 AGENTS.md 依赖的正是这一点。
Session 在哪里结束由你决定。Session 中的一切都影响之后的每一个 Turn，所以在同一个 Session 里做无关的任务会留下残留，影响下一个回答。一个 Session 只做一件事能让 Context 保持相关；任务完成时，就是一个自然的清除节点。
用法
"一个 Session 能跑多久才会开始崩坏？"
"取决于工作内容——聚焦的重构比开放式的调研能保持敏锐更久。一旦 Session 变得臃肿，就交接或压缩，不要硬撑下去。"

summary.zh: Session 是一次有边界的连续交互。它从初始 Context 开始，随用户 Turn、工具结果和 Agent 回复逐渐增长；关闭、Clearing 或 Compaction 后会进入新 Session。跨 Session 的信息需要交接或记忆机制。

description.en: One user message plus everything the agent does in response, up until it yields back to the user. Contains one or more provider requests.
description.zh: 一条用户消息以及 Agent 为回应它所做的全部工作，直到把控制权交还用户。

en: One user message plus everything the agent does in response, up until it yields back to the user. Contains one or more model provider requests — many, if the agent calls tools. A clarifying question closes the turn; your reply opens the next one. The hierarchy is session > Turn > Model provider request.

What makes the turn worth naming is that its length is the agent's decision, not yours. You hand over one message; the agent decides how many tool calls to chain before yielding. A turn can be a one-sentence answer or twenty minutes of reading, editing, and running tests. That's the same property from two angles: long turns are what make AFK work possible, and long turns are also where things go wrong unsupervised — by the time the agent yields, it may have drifted a long way from what you meant.

The turn is also the natural unit for steering. Everything inside a turn happens without you; the gaps between turns are where you redirect. Most harnesses soften this: you can interrupt mid-turn to stop the agent and redirect it, or type a message while it works, which gets read once the turn completes. If you find yourself repeatedly unhappy with where turns end up, the fix is usually to ask for smaller ones — a plan first, one step at a time — trading autonomy for more frequent gaps to steer in.
Usage:
"One turn took two minutes?"
"It made fourteen tool calls inside that turn — each one is a separate model provider request. Latency stacks up before the agent finally yields back to you."
zh: 一条用户消息，加上 agent 为响应它所做的一切，直到它把控制权交还给用户为止。其中包含一次或多次 model provider request——如果 agent 调用了 tool，就会有很多次。一个澄清性问题会结束当前 turn；你的回复则开启下一个 turn。层级关系是 Session > Turn > Model provider request。

Turn 之所以值得单独命名，在于它的长度是 agent 的决定，而不是你的。你只交出一条消息；agent 决定在让出控制权之前要串联多少次 tool 调用。一个 turn 可能只是一句回答，也可能是二十分钟的阅读、编辑和运行测试。这是同一特性的两个侧面：长 turn 让 AFK 工作成为可能，而长 turn 也正是无人监督时容易出问题的地方——等到 agent 让出控制权时，它可能已经偏离你的本意很远了。

Turn 也是进行引导的自然单位。turn 内部发生的一切都不需要你参与；turn 之间的间隙才是你重新调整方向的地方。大多数 harness 会把这个边界软化：你可以在 turn 进行到一半时打断，让 agent 停下来并改变方向，或者在它工作时输入一条消息，这条消息会在 turn 结束后被读到。如果你发现自己反复对 turn 的落点不满意，解决办法通常是要求更小的 turn——先给一个计划，一步一步来——用自主性换取更频繁、可用于引导的间隙。
用法
"一个 turn 花了两分钟？"
"它在那一个 turn 里做了十四次 tool 调用——每一次都是一次独立的 model provider request。在 agent 最终把控制权交还给你之前，延迟会不断累积。"

summary.zh: Turn 从一条用户消息开始，包含 Agent 为回应它发起的所有 Model provider requests、tool calls 和内部步骤，直到它把控制权交还用户。一次 Turn 不等于一次 Model 请求，复杂任务通常需要多轮内部往返。

description.en: The world the agent acts on — anything outside the harness that the agent perceives via tool results and changes via tool calls.
description.zh: Agent 通过 tool results 感知、通过 tool calls 修改的外部世界。

en: The world the agent acts on — anything outside the harness that the agent perceives through tool results and changes through tool calls. The harness runs the agent; the environment is what the agent works in. A file like AGENTS.md lives in the environment; the harness is what loads it into the context window. A filesystem is the most common kind of environment, but not the only one (a database, a remote API, a browser session can all be environments).

The agent only sees the environment when it looks. Everything it knows about the environment arrived through a tool result, so its picture is a collection of snapshots, each accurate at the moment it was taken. If a file changes after the agent read it — you edit it by hand, a build step regenerates it — the agent keeps reasoning from the stale copy until something prompts a re-read. An agent confidently describing a file that no longer looks like that is usually this: the environment moved, the snapshot didn't.

The environment is also the layer that persists — the only one that is always stateful. A session's context is gone when the session ends, but files written to the environment remain for the next session to read — which is what memory systems, handoff artifacts, and AGENTS.md rely on. Anything an agent should still know tomorrow has to end up in the environment.

You decide how big the environment is. A sandbox shrinks it, limiting what the agent can reach; adding a tool extends it, bringing a database or an API into reach. What's inside the boundary is what the agent can perceive and change; everything outside it doesn't exist for the agent. How well the environment is set up to support the agent's work is the codebase's AX.
Avoid: using "environment" for the runtime or the harness itself — the harness is the wrapper, the environment is the workspace.
Usage:
"The agent can't see the staging DB schema."
"Wire it into the environment — give it a psql tool scoped to read-only on staging. The harness is fine, it just has nothing to act on."
zh: Agent 所作用的世界——Harness 之外的一切：Agent 通过 Tool result 感知它，通过 Tool 调用改变它。Harness 运行 Agent；Environment 是 Agent 工作的场所。像 AGENTS.md 这样的文件存在于 Environment 中；把它载入 Context window 的是 Harness。Filesystem 是最常见的 Environment，但不是唯一的一种（数据库、远程 API、浏览器 Session 都可以是 Environment）。

Agent 只有在去看的时候才看得见 Environment。它关于 Environment 所知道的一切都是通过 Tool result 抵达的，所以它脑中的画面是一组快照的集合，每一张都只在拍下的那一刻准确。如果某个文件在 Agent 读过之后发生了变化——你手动编辑了它，构建步骤重新生成了它——Agent 会继续基于那份过期的副本推理，直到有东西促使它重新读取。一个 Agent 自信地描述着一个早已不再长成那样的文件，通常就是这个原因：Environment 变了，快照没变。
Environment 也是持久留存的那一层——唯一始终 Stateful 的一层。Session 的 Context 在 Session 结束时就不复存在，但写入 Environment 的文件会留下来供下一个 Session 读取——记忆系统、Handoff 产物和 AGENTS.md 依赖的正是这一点。任何 Agent 明天还应该知道的东西，都必须落到 Environment 里。
Environment 有多大由你决定。Sandbox 把它缩小，限制 Agent 能够触达的范围；增加一个 Tool 把它扩大，让数据库或 API 进入可及范围。边界之内才是 Agent 能够感知和改变的东西；边界之外的一切对 Agent 而言都不存在。Environment 为支持 Agent 工作所做准备的好坏，就是这套代码库的 AX。
避免：用 "environment" 指代 runtime 或 Harness 本身——Harness 是外壳，Environment 是工作区。
用法
"Agent 看不到 staging 数据库的 schema。"
"把它接入 Environment——给它一个限定为 staging 只读的 psql Tool。Harness 没问题，只是它没有可作用的对象。"

summary.zh: Environment 是 Agent 所处的外部世界，例如文件系统、浏览器或数据库。Agent 只能通过 Harness 暴露的 tools 感知和改变它；tool results 才是它看到环境状态的入口。环境变化也可能来自其他人或进程。

description.en: A tree of files and directories the agent reads from, writes to, and executes within — the default environment for a coding agent.
description.zh: 由文件和目录构成的树，是 Coding Agent 读取、写入和执行内容的常见环境。

en: A tree of files and directories the agent reads from, writes to, and executes within — the default kind of environment for a coding agent. AGENTS.md, skills, source code, build scripts, and tool configs all live in a filesystem. When a harness "starts in your project," it's pointing the agent at a filesystem.

The agent touches it only through tool calls — reading a file, writing one, running a shell command. Nothing on disk is in the context window until a tool call loads it, which is what lets the agent work in a repository far larger than the window: the filesystem holds everything, the context holds only what the current task has read. Some harnesses do load the current directory's filenames into the context window by default — not the contents, just the tree — which act as context pointers: the agent sees what exists and reads the files it needs.
And it's shared with you. The files the agent edits are the same ones you open in your editor and diff in git — the filesystem is the common workspace where you review what the agent did.
Usage:
"Why isn't it picking up my AGENTS.md?"
"It's running against a different filesystem — the sandbox mounted the parent dir, not the project root. Repoint the harness."
zh: 由文件和目录构成的一棵树，Agent 从中读取、向其写入并在其中执行——这是 coding agent 默认的 Environment 类型。AGENTS.md、Skills、源代码、构建脚本和 Tool 配置都存在于一个 Filesystem 之中。当 Harness "在你的项目中启动" 时，它就是在把 Agent 指向一个 Filesystem。

Agent 只能通过 Tool call 接触它 —— 读一个文件、写一个文件、运行一条 shell 命令。在 Tool call 把它载入之前，磁盘上的任何内容都不在 Context window 中，这正是 Agent 能在远大于窗口的仓库里工作的原因：filesystem 承载一切，Context 只保留当前任务已读取的那部分。有些 Harness 确实会默认把当前目录的文件名载入 Context window —— 不是文件内容，只是目录树 —— 它们充当 Context 指针：Agent 由此看到有哪些文件存在，再读取自己需要的那些。
而且它与你共享。Agent 编辑的文件，就是你在编辑器里打开、在 git 里 diff 的同一批文件 —— filesystem 是共同的工作空间，你在这里审阅 Agent 做了什么。
用法
“为什么它没有读到我的 AGENTS.md？”
“它跑在另一个 filesystem 上 —— sandbox 挂载的是父目录，而不是项目根目录。把 Harness 重新指过去。”

summary.zh: Filesystem 以目录和文件组成树。Coding Agent 通常借助工具读取、修改和运行其中的内容。文件里的资料不是 Model 天然知道的；它需要通过 tool result 进入 Context，写入则要通过相应 tool call。

description.en: A function the harness exposes for the agent to call — Read, Write, Bash, Search. How an agent perceives and acts on the environment.
description.zh: Harness 提供给 Agent 的可调用函数，使它能读取或改变环境。

en: A function the harness exposes for the agent to call — Read, Write, Bash, Search. Tools are how an agent perceives and acts on the environment: it can't see the environment except through tool results, and can't change it except through tool calls. Each tool call costs an extra model provider request, since the result has to go back to the model before it can decide what to do next.
Tools most coding agents ship with:

| Tool   | What it does                                                 |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Read   | Returns a file's contents as a tool result                   |
| Write  | Creates or edits a file in the filesystem |
| Bash   | Runs a shell command and returns its output                  |
| Search | Finds files or text matching a pattern across the codebase   |

A tool is defined by three things: a name, a description of what it does, and a schema for its parameters. The harness sends these definitions to the model with every request, and the model chooses a tool the same way it produces everything else — by writing tokens, in this case a structured call with arguments. The model never executes anything itself; the harness reads the call, runs the function, and sends back the result.

The tool list sets what the agent can do. A capable model with a narrow tool set is a narrow agent: it will route everything through whatever it has, which is why agents lean so heavily on Bash — a shell is one tool that reaches most of the system. To give an agent a capability cleanly, add a tool for it; MCP is the standard for plugging in tools from outside the harness.
Tool definitions occupy context on every request, so a large tool set has a standing cost before any tool is called — and many similarly-described tools make the model worse at picking the right one.
Usage:
"Can the agent query staging directly?"
"Add a psql tool to the harness, scoped read-only on staging. Without a tool for it, the agent's blind to anything outside the filesystem."
zh: Harness 暴露给 Agent 调用的函数——Read、Write、Bash、Search。Tool 是 Agent 感知 Environment 并对其采取行动的方式：它只能通过 Tool 的结果看到 Environment，也只能通过 Tool call 改变 Environment。每次 Tool call 都会额外消耗一次 Model provider request，因为结果必须先送回 Model，它才能决定下一步做什么。
大多数 coding Agent 自带的 Tool：

| Tool | 它的作用 |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Read | 以 Tool result 的形式返回文件内容 |
| Write | 在 Filesystem 中创建或编辑文件 |
| Bash | 运行 shell 命令并返回其输出 |
| Search | 在整个代码库中查找与某个模式匹配的文件或文本 |
一个 Tool 由三样东西定义：名称、它做什么的描述，以及用于其 Parameters 的 schema。Harness 在每次请求中都会把这些定义发给 Model，而 Model 选择 Tool 的方式与它产出其他一切内容的方式相同——靠写 token，在这里就是一次带参数的结构化调用。Model 自己从不执行任何东西；Harness 读取这次调用，运行该函数，再把结果发回去。

Tool 列表决定了 Agent 能做什么。一个能力很强的 Model 若只有狭窄的 Tool 集合，就是一个能力狭窄的 Agent：它会把手头的一切都绕道它现有的 Tool，这正是 Agent 如此重度依赖 Bash 的原因——一个 shell 就是一把能触达系统大部分角落的 Tool。要干净地赋予 Agent 一项能力，就为它加一个 Tool；MCP 是从 Harness 之外接入 Tool 的标准。
Tool 定义在每次请求中都会占用 Context，因此庞大的 Tool 集合在任何 Tool 被调用之前就有一笔固定成本——而且许多描述相似的 Tool 会让 Model 更难挑对那一个。
用法
"Agent 能直接查询 staging 吗？"
"给 Harness 加一个 psql Tool，作用域为在 staging 上只读。没有对应的 Tool，Agent 对 Filesystem 之外的东西就一无所知。"

summary.zh: Tool 是 Harness 提供的可调用能力，例如读文件、执行命令或搜索。Model 可以请求使用 Tool，但是否真正执行、如何执行，以及结果如何返回，都由 Harness 控制。工具集合直接决定 Agent 能接触哪些环境。

description.en: The model's output naming a tool and its arguments — just structured text. The harness has to read it and execute.
description.zh: Model 输出的工具名称与参数；Harness 读取后执行相应操作。

en: The model's output naming a tool and its arguments — just structured text. It doesn't do anything on its own; the harness has to read it and execute. Produced by the model in one model provider request.
The lifecycle of a tool call:

| Step | Who     | What happens                                                                            |
| ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Model   | Learns which tools exist from descriptions in the system prompt |
| 2    | Model   | Emits a call — tool name plus arguments, usually JSON — and stops                       |
| 3    | Harness | Parses the call and checks it against the permission mode     |
| 4    | Harness | Executes it if allowed                                                                  |
| 5    | Harness | Sends the outcome back as a tool result in the next request       |
One turn of agent work is usually many of these round trips chained together.

Because the call is generated by next-token prediction like everything else, it can be wrong the way any model output can be wrong: a path that doesn't exist, a flag the command doesn't have, arguments that are plausible rather than correct. The harness executes what was written, not what was meant — a mistyped path doesn't error gracefully, it edits the wrong file.
Usage:
"It said it ran the tests but the file timestamps haven't changed."
"Look at the transcript — did it actually emit a tool call, or just describe running them? The model produces the call, but if the harness didn't execute it, nothing happened."
zh: Model 的输出中指明一个 Tool 及其参数——仅仅是结构化文本。它自己不会做任何事；必须由 Harness 读取并执行。它由 Model 在一次 Model provider request 中生成。
一次 Tool call 的生命周期：

| 步骤 | 谁 | 发生了什么 |
| ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | Model | 从 System prompt 中的描述了解到有哪些 Tool 存在 |
| 2 | Model | 发出一次调用——Tool 名称加参数，通常是 JSON——然后停止 |
| 3 | Harness | 解析这次调用，并对照 Permission mode 进行检查 |
| 4 | Harness | 如果被允许就执行它 |
| 5 | Harness | 在下一次请求中把结果作为 Tool result 回传 |
Agent 工作中的一个 Turn，通常由许多这样的往返串联而成。
因为这个调用和其他所有内容一样是由 Next-token prediction 生成的，所以它会像任何 Model 输出一样出错：不存在的路径、命令并不具备的 flag、看似合理但并不正确的参数。Harness 执行的是写出来的内容，而不是本来想表达的内容——路径打错不会优雅地报错，而是会去编辑错误的文件。
用法
“它说它跑了测试，但文件时间戳没有变化。”
“看看 transcript——它到底真的发出了一个 Tool call，还是只是描述了运行它们的过程？Model 会生成这个调用，但如果 Harness 没有执行它，那就什么也没发生。”

summary.zh: Tool call 是 Model 给出的结构化请求，包含工具名与参数，本身只是输出文本。Harness 会解释它、检查权限、执行操作，再把结果返回。一次错误的参数可能导致失败，因此 Harness 不能把请求文本当成已完成的动作。

description.en: What the harness sends back after executing a tool call — file contents, output, or error. The agent's only view of the environment.
description.zh: Harness 把工具执行结果送回 Model 的内容，可能是文件、输出或错误。
