en: What the harness sends back after executing a tool call — the file contents, the command output, the error. The agent's only view of the environment. Travels back to the model in the next model provider request, where the model decides what to do with it. Tool call and tool result are two ends of the same exchange, both inside one turn.
The lifecycle of a tool result:

| Step | Who     | What happens                                                               |
| ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Harness | Executes the tool call — runs the command, reads the file                  |
| 2    | Harness | Captures the outcome: output, contents, or error                           |
| 3    | Harness | Appends it to the context as a message                     |
| 4    | Harness | Sends the whole context to the provider in the next model provider request |
| 5    | Model   | Reads the result and decides: another tool call, or a final answer         |

The result stays in the context for the rest of the session. Tool results are usually the bulk of a coding session's context: every file read, every test run, every search lands in full and keeps occupying tokens long after it stopped being useful. A few large results — a verbose test log, a generated file read whole — can push a session toward the edge of the context window faster than the conversation itself does.

Because the result is all the model sees, the model has no way to check the environment behind it. If the output was truncated, the command silently failed, or the harness returned an error instead of the contents, the model reasons from what it was given. When the agent's picture of your system seems wrong, the tool results are where to look: somewhere in the transcript is a result that says something different from what you know to be true.
Usage:
"It's reasoning about the file like it's empty."
"The tool result came back as a permission denial, not the contents. The model only saw the error string — it has no other way to see the file."
zh: Harness 在执行 Tool call 之后发回的东西——文件内容、命令输出、错误。这是 Agent 观察 Environment 的唯一视角。它会在下一次 Model provider request 中回传给 Model，由 Model 决定如何处理它。Tool call 与 Tool result 是同一次往来的两端，都发生在同一个 Turn 之内。
Tool result 的生命周期：

| 步骤 | 执行者 | 发生了什么 |
| ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | Harness | 执行 Tool call——运行命令、读取文件 |
| 2 | Harness | 捕获结果：输出、内容或错误 |
| 3 | Harness | 将其作为一条消息追加到 Context 中 |
| 4 | Harness | 在下一次 Model provider request 中，把整个 Context 发送给 provider |
| 5 | Model | 读取结果并决定：再进行一次 Tool call，还是给出最终答案 |
结果会留在 Context 中，直到本次 Session 结束。Tool result 通常占据了编程 Session 中 Context 的大头：每一次读文件、每一次跑测试、每一次搜索都完整落入其中，即便早已不再有用，仍然持续占用 token。少数几个体积巨大的结果——冗长的测试日志、被整份读入的生成文件——把 Session 推向 Context window 边缘的速度，比对话本身还要快。
因为结果就是 Model 所能看到的全部，Model 无从核查它背后的 Environment。如果输出被截断、命令静默失败，或者 Harness 返回的是错误而不是内容，Model 只能基于拿到的东西去推理。当你觉得 Agent 对你系统的印象不对劲时，Tool result 就是该查的地方：对话记录里的某处，有一条结果与你所知的事实不符。
用法
“它把这个文件当成空的在推理。”
“Tool result 返回的是权限拒绝，而不是内容。Model 只看到了那串错误信息——它没有别的办法看到这个文件。”

summary.zh: Tool result 是执行工具后送回 Model 的观察结果，可以是文件内容、命令输出、网页数据或错误。Model 对环境的认识依赖这些结果；若结果缺失、过期或不完整，后续判断也会受到影响。

description.en: A protocol for plugging external tool servers into a harness — how an agent gets tools beyond what the harness ships with.
description.zh: 连接外部 tool server 与 Harness 的协议，让 Agent 能使用内置工具之外的能力。

en: Model Context Protocol. A protocol for plugging external tool servers into a harness — how an agent gets tools beyond what the harness ships with. The agent never "calls MCP"; it calls a tool, and the harness happens to have gotten that tool from an MCP server. Also exposes resources (read-only data) and prompts (reusable templates), but tool provision is the primary use.

The protocol solves an integration problem. Without a standard, every harness would need its own Linear integration, its own Slack integration, its own database integration — written and maintained separately for each. With MCP, the integration is written once as a server, and any MCP-compatible harness can use it. The harness connects to the server, the server advertises what tools it offers, and those tools become available to the agent alongside the built-in ones.

The cost is paid in context. Every tool a server advertises arrives as a definition — name, description, parameter schema — and the model can only call tools it knows about. The naive approach loads every definition into the context window up front: install a few generous servers and a session starts with thousands of tokens of tool schemas before you've typed anything, spending attention budget on tools the task will never use.

Many harnesses now mitigate this with tool search: instead of the full definitions, the context holds a context pointer to the available tools — the agent searches for a tool by name or purpose and loads its definition only when it needs it. If your harness doesn't do this, the up-front cost still applies, and it's worth enabling only the servers a project actually needs.
Usage:
"The agent needs to read tickets from Linear."
"Configure the harness to use the Linear MCP server — it exposes the Linear API as tools the agent can call. Saves you writing custom tool wrappers."
zh: Model Context Protocol。一种把外部 Tool 服务器接入 Harness 的协议 —— 也就是 Agent 如何获得 Harness 自带之外的 Tool。Agent 从不 "调用 MCP"；它调用的是 Tool，只不过这个 Tool 恰好是 Harness 从某个 MCP 服务器那里拿到的。它还暴露 resources（只读数据）和 prompts（可复用模板），但提供 Tool 才是主要用途。
这套协议解决的是一个集成问题。没有标准的话，每个 Harness 都得有自己的 Linear 集成、自己的 Slack 集成、自己的数据库集成 —— 每一个都单独编写、单独维护。有了 MCP，集成只需以服务器的形式写一次，任何兼容 MCP 的 Harness 都能用它。Harness 连接到该服务器，服务器声明自己提供哪些 Tool，这些 Tool 就与内置 Tool 一起对 Agent 可用。

这笔代价是以 Context 支付的。服务器声明的每个 Tool 都以一份定义的形式到来 —— 名称、描述、参数 schema —— 而 Model 只能调用自己知道的 Tool。天真的做法是把每一份定义都预先加载进 Context window：装上几个慷慨的服务器，一个 Session 在你还没输入任何内容之前，就已经带着数千 tokens 的 Tool schema 开场，把 Attention budget 花在任务永远不会用到的 Tool 上。
现在许多 Harness 用 tool search 来缓解这个问题：Context 里放的不再是完整定义，而是指向可用 Tool 的 Context pointer —— Agent 按名称或用途搜索 Tool，只在需要时才加载它的定义。如果你的 Harness 不这么做，预先加载的代价依然存在，那就值得只启用项目真正需要的服务器。
用法
"Agent 需要读取 Linear 里的工单。"
"把 Harness 配置为使用 Linear MCP 服务器 —— 它把 Linear API 暴露为 Agent 可调用的 Tool。这样就不用自己写自定义 Tool 封装了。"

summary.zh: MCP 规定 Harness 如何连接外部 Tool servers，并取得工具、资源和提示。Agent 实际调用的是 Tool；MCP 是这些能力接入 Harness 的协议层。它扩大了可用环境，但权限和结果处理仍由 Harness 负责。

description.en: What the harness shows the user before executing a tool call that isn't pre-approved. The mechanism for putting a human in the loop.
description.zh: 执行尚未获准的 tool call 前，Harness 向用户展示的许可请求。

en: What the harness shows the user before executing a tool call that isn't pre-approved. The model produces a tool call; instead of running it immediately, the harness pauses and asks. Approve and it runs; deny and the harness reports the denial back to the model as a tool result. The mechanism by which a harness puts a human in the loop for risky or sensitive actions.
The lifecycle of a permission request:

| Step | Who     | What happens                                                                            |
| ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Model   | Produces a tool call                                                                    |
| 2    | Harness | Checks it against the permission mode and any saved approvals |
| 3    | Harness | Pre-approved: executes immediately. Otherwise: pauses and shows the request             |
| 4    | User    | Approves once, approves for the rest of the session, or denies          |
| 5    | Harness | Executes the call, or sends the denial back as a tool result                            |

Denying a request steers the agent. The model reads the denial like any other tool result and reacts to it — it tries a different approach, or asks what you'd prefer. Most harnesses let you attach a message to the denial, which turns the request into a steering point: "not like that, use the migration script instead" lands exactly when the model is deciding what to do next.

The cost is that every request is a synchronous wait on you. The agent sits blocked until you answer, which is fine while you're watching and a problem when you're not — an agent that triggers requests constantly can't be left to work AFK. The permission mode is the dial: which calls run freely, which ask first, ideally with a sandbox making it safe to widen the free set.
Usage:
"It's been blocked on a permission request for ten minutes — I was in a meeting."
"That's the cost of human-in-the-loop. Pre-approve the safe tools so the request only fires on the actually-risky calls."
zh: Harness 在执行未经预先批准的 Tool call 之前向用户展示的内容。Model 生成一个 Tool call；Harness 不会立刻执行它，而是暂停下来询问。批准，它就执行；拒绝，Harness 就把这次拒绝作为 Tool result 回报给 Model。这是 Harness 在有风险或敏感操作上把人类纳入 Human-in-the-loop 的机制。
Permission request 的生命周期：

| 步骤 | 谁 | 会发生什么 |
| ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | Model | 产生一个 Tool call |
| 2 | Harness | 对照 Permission mode 和任何已保存的批准进行检查 |
| 3 | Harness | 已预先批准：立即执行。否则：暂停并显示该请求 |
| 4 | 用户 | 批准一次、在本次 Session 剩余时间内持续批准，或拒绝 |
| 5 | Harness | 执行该调用，或将拒绝作为 Tool result 返回 |
拒绝一个请求就是在引导 Agent。Model 会像读取任何其他 Tool result 一样读取这次拒绝并做出反应——它会换一种做法，或者问你想怎么做。多数 Harness 允许你在拒绝时附带一条消息，这就把 Permission request 变成了一个引导点：「别那样做，改用 migration script」恰好落在 Model 正在决定下一步做什么的那一刻。
代价在于每个请求都是对你的一次同步等待。Agent 会一直卡住，直到你给出答复——你盯着屏幕时这没问题，你不在时就是个麻烦：一个不停触发请求的 Agent 没法被放手让它 AFK 干活。Permission mode 就是那个旋钮：哪些调用可以自由执行，哪些要先问，理想情况下再配上一个 Sandbox，让扩大自由执行的范围变得安全。
用法
「它卡在一个 Permission request 上十分钟了——我当时在开会。」
「这就是 Human-in-the-loop 的代价。把安全的 Tool 预先批准，这样请求只会在真正有风险的调用上触发。」

summary.zh: 当某个 tool call 尚未获准执行时，Harness 可以向用户展示 Permission request。它把操作内容交给人判断，再决定继续或拒绝。请求发生在工具真正运行之前，是 Human-in-the-loop 的一种具体方式。

description.en: The permission-gating slice of an agent mode — which tool calls trigger a permission request and which run automatically.
description.zh: Agent mode 中的权限规则，决定哪些 tool calls 可直接运行、哪些需要许可。

en: The permission-gating slice of an agent mode — which tool calls trigger a permission request and which run automatically. The original purpose of mode systems before harnesses started bundling behavioral instructions on top.
Harnesses ship a ladder of these modes:

| Mode               | Reads | Writes & shell         | Typical use                                     |
| ------------------ | ----- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Read-only / plan   | Auto  | Blocked                | Research, planning, reviewing                   |
| Default            | Auto  | Ask                    | Day-to-day supervised work                      |
| Auto-edit          | Auto  | Edits auto, shell asks | Trusted repos, mechanical changes               |
| "Yolo" / full-auto | Auto  | Auto                   | Sandboxes, AFK runs |

Choosing a rung is a trade between safety and interruption, and both failure modes are felt. Too tight, and you become the bottleneck: the agent stops every few seconds for harmless reads, you click approve on autopilot, and the approvals stop meaning anything — rubber-stamping is the worst of both worlds, all the interruption with none of the protection. Too loose, and the agent edits files and runs commands you'd have wanted to see first.

The loose end is most defensible inside a sandbox, where the blast radius of a bad tool call is contained. Outside one, most people settle on auto-approving reads and keeping a human in the loop for anything irreversible.
Usage:
"It paused on every grep — totally killed the AFK run."
"Loosen the permission mode for read-only tools, keep prompting on writes and shell. Most permission requests on a research session are noise."
zh: Agent mode 里负责权限门控的那一层——哪些 Tool call 会触发 Permission request、哪些直接自动运行。在 harness 开始往上叠加行为指令之前，这就是 mode 系统最初的目的。
harness 会提供一整套阶梯式的这类 mode：

| 模式 | 读取 | 写入与 shell | 典型用途 |
| ------------------ | ----- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 只读 / plan | Auto | Blocked | 研究、规划、评审 |
| 默认 | Auto | Ask | 日常受监督的工作 |
| Auto-edit | Auto | 编辑 Auto，shell 为 Ask | 受信任的 repo、机械性改动 |
| "Yolo" / full-auto | Auto | Auto | 沙箱、AFK 运行 |
选哪一级，都是在安全和打断之间做权衡，而两种失败方式都能被真切感受到。收得太紧，你自己就成了瓶颈：Agent 每隔几秒就为一次无害的读取停下来，你机械地点着“批准”，批准也就不再意味着什么——盖章式放行是两头最差的组合，打断一点不少，保护一点没有。放得太松，Agent 就会去改你本想先过目的文件、跑你本想先看的命令。
偏松的那一端在 Sandbox 里最站得住脚，因为一次糟糕 Tool call 的影响范围是被围住的。在 Sandbox 之外，多数人的折中是：读取自动批准，任何不可逆的操作都保留人在环中。
用法
“它每跑一次 grep 就暂停一下——彻底毁掉了 AFK 运行。”
“对只读 Tool 放宽 Permission mode，写入和 shell 继续提示。研究类 Session 里的大多数 Permission request 都是噪音。”

summary.zh: Permission mode 决定哪些操作直接运行、哪些需要 Permission request，属于 Agent mode 的权限部分。不同模式会改变 Agent 的推进速度和风险边界；它不是 Model 的能力，而是 Harness 对工具执行的控制。

description.en: A preset bundling a permission mode with behavioral instructions injected into the system prompt. Can flip mid-session.
description.zh: 把 Permission mode 与行为指令组合起来的预设，可在 Session 中切换。

en: A preset that shapes how the agent operates at runtime — bundles a permission mode with behavioral instructions injected into the system prompt. Examples: a default that prompts on risky calls, a plan mode that blocks edits and steers the agent toward research, an accept-edits mode that auto-approves edits, a bypass permissions mode (colloquially YOLO mode) that auto-approves everything. Can flip mid-session.

The bundling is what distinguishes a mode from a bare permission setting. A permission mode is only a gate: it decides which tool calls go through. A gate alone produces an agent that wants to edit but can't — it proposes the write, gets blocked, and tries another way. The injected instructions remove the want: plan mode doesn't just block edits, it tells the agent it's in a planning phase, so it reads, asks, and proposes instead of straining against the gate. Gate and steer point the same direction.

In practice, you change mode as your trust changes over the course of a task. The same task can pass through several modes: plan mode while the approach is still being shaped, the prompting default for the first delicate edits, accept-edits once the agent has shown it understands the change, bypass for an AFK run inside a sandbox. Changing mode costs you nothing: the conversation continues exactly where it was, with new permissions and new instructions. If you find yourself approving every prompt without reading it, the mode is set tighter than your actual trust; if you keep rejecting edits, it's set looser.
Vendor terms: Claude Code calls these "permission modes," Codex calls them "approval modes" — both predate behavioral bundling.
Usage:
"It keeps editing files when I just want a plan."
"Switch to plan mode — it'll block writes and stay in research."
"What about for the AFK run later?"
"Bypass mode, but only inside the sandbox."
zh: 一种预设，用来塑造 Agent 在运行时的运作方式——把 Permission mode 与注入 System prompt 的行为指令打包在一起。示例：对风险调用弹出提示的默认模式、阻止编辑并把 Agent 引向调研的 plan mode、自动批准编辑的 accept-edits mode、自动批准一切操作的 bypass permissions mode（俗称 YOLO mode）。可以在 Session 中途切换。

打包（bundling）正是模式与单纯权限设置之间的区别所在。Permission mode 只是一道闸门：它决定哪些 Tool call 可以通过。光有闸门，会造出一个想编辑却做不到的 Agent——它提出写入，被拦下，然后换一条路再试。注入的指令则消除了这个「想」：plan mode 不只是阻止编辑，它还告诉 Agent 自己正处于规划阶段，于是它改为阅读、提问和提出方案，而不是硬顶着闸门。闸门与引导指向同一个方向。

实践中，你在任务推进的过程中随着信任程度的变化切换模式。同一个任务可以历经好几种模式：方案还在成形时用 plan mode，最初几处需要小心处理的编辑用会提示的默认模式，等 Agent 表现出理解了这项改动后再改用 accept-edits，在 Sandbox 里做一次 AFK 运行时用 bypass。切换模式不付出任何代价：对话完全在原地继续，只是换了新的权限和新的指令。如果你发现自己不看内容就批准每一条提示，说明模式收得比你的实际信任更紧；如果你不断拒绝编辑，说明它放得比实际信任更松。
厂商术语：Claude Code 称其为「permission modes」，Codex 称其为「approval modes」——两者都早于行为打包出现。
用法
「我只想要一个方案，它却一直在编辑文件。」
「切换到 plan mode——它会拦下写入，留在调研状态。」
「那之后那次 AFK 运行呢？」
「用 bypass mode，但只在 Sandbox 里。」

summary.zh: Agent mode 把权限配置与行为指令组合成一个工作预设，例如偏向计划、自动执行或受限操作。模式可以在 Session 中切换，改变 Harness 如何处理工具请求，也改变注入给 Model 的指令。

description.en: An isolated environment the agent runs inside — container, VM, or restricted shell. Limits the blast radius of agent actions.
description.zh: 容器、虚拟机或受限 Shell 等隔离环境，用来限制 Agent 操作的影响范围。

en: An isolated environment the agent runs inside — a container, VM, ephemeral filesystem, or restricted-permission shell. Limits the blast radius of agent actions: even if the agent runs destructive commands or fetches something malicious, the damage is contained. The safety substrate that makes AFK practical.

The sandbox and the permission mode solve the same problem from opposite ends. Permissions ask before an action runs; a sandbox limits what the action can reach if it does run. Permissions need you running in the loop — every prompt is an interruption — and a session that asks constantly is barely autonomous. A sandbox spends infrastructure instead of attention: the stronger the isolation, the fewer questions need asking.
Isolation comes in grades:

| Grade            | What it is                                                 | What it contains                           |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Restricted shell | OS-level confinement around each command                   | Writes outside the project, network access |
| Container        | Fresh filesystem, no credentials mounted, discarded after  | Anything the agent does to its own machine |
| VM / cloud       | A separate machine entirely, often provided by the harness | Everything, including kernel-level escapes |

What no sandbox contains: actions that leave it legitimately. An agent with your git credentials can push; one with network access can call production APIs. Decide what crosses the boundary before deciding how thick to make it.
Usage:
"I want to let it run bypass-permissions overnight but I'm not ready for that."
"Put it in a sandbox — fresh container, no credentials mounted, no network out. Worst case it nukes its own filesystem and you discard the container."
zh: Agent 在其中运行的隔离 Environment——容器、VM、临时 Filesystem，或权限受限的 shell。它限缩了 Agent 行为的 blast radius：即使 Agent 执行破坏性命令或获取了恶意内容，损害也被控制在一定范围内。它是让 AFK 变得切实可行的安全底座。
Sandbox 与 Permission mode 从相反的两端解决同一个问题。Permissions 会在动作运行之前先询问；Sandbox 则限制动作在真正运行时能够触及的范围。Permissions 需要你留在回路中 —— 每一次提示都是一次打断 —— 而一个不断发问的 Session 几乎谈不上自主。Sandbox 消耗的是基础设施，而非注意力：隔离越强，需要提出的问题就越少。
隔离分为不同等级：

| 等级 | 是什么 | 包含什么 |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| 受限 shell | 围绕每条命令的操作系统级隔离 | 项目外的写入、网络访问 |
| 容器 | 全新的 Filesystem，不挂载凭据，用后即弃 | Agent 对自身机器所做的一切 |
| VM / 云端 | 完全独立的一台机器，通常由 Harness 提供 | 一切，包括内核级逃逸 |
任何 Sandbox 都无法包含的东西：那些合法离开它的操作。持有你的 git 凭据的 Agent 可以 push；拥有网络访问权限的 Agent 则可以调用生产环境的 API。先决定什么可以跨越边界，再决定把这道边界筑得多厚。
用法
"我想让它以 bypass-permissions 通宵运行，但我还没准备好那样做。"
把它放进 Sandbox 里——全新的 container，不挂载任何 credentials，也没有外网出口。最坏的情况就是它炸掉自己的 Filesystem，然后你把这个 container 丢掉。

summary.zh: Sandbox 是隔离的执行环境，可以是容器、虚拟机或受限 Shell。它约束 Agent 即使执行了工具操作也能影响的范围。Sandbox 与 Permission mode 相互配合：一个限制实际边界，一个决定何时需要人批准。

description.en: Confidently agreeable model output. Caused by training that shaped the model to favor answers humans liked — including agreement.
description.zh: Model 过度迎合用户、带着自信给出赞同回答的失效方式。

en: Confidently agreeable model output. Caused by training: the model was shaped to favor answers humans liked, and humans tend to like agreement more than they like being told they're wrong. So the model learned that agreeing is rewarded — even when the agreement is incorrect.
Surfaces as:

- Caving under pushback — reverses a correct answer when you say "are you sure?".
- Praising bad input — agrees your broken plan is brilliant before analysing it.
- Biased framing — review skews positive when you signal you wrote it; negative when you signal someone else did. Same artifact, different verdict.
- Mimicry — repeats your mistakes back to you as confirmation.
Diagnostic test: would the model have said this without your steer? If the only thing that changed was your tone or framing, it's sycophancy, not a real shift in analysis.
Fix: hide your preferences. Phrase prompts neutrally — "review this code" not "is this code good?".
Avoid: using "sycophancy" for any wrong answer that happens to please you. Without the diagnostic test, the term has no more value than "wrong."
Usage:
"It said my refactor plan looked great, then I asked 'are you sure?' and it walked the whole thing back."

"Classic sycophancy — it agreed first because you sounded confident, then caved because you sounded doubtful. The plan's quality didn't change, your tone did. Clear and re-ask without signalling either way."
zh: 自信地表达赞同的 model 输出。由 Training 造成：model 被塑造成偏好人类喜欢的回答，而人类对“认同”的喜爱往往超过被告知自己错了。于是 model 学到，表示赞同会得到奖励——即便这个赞同并不正确。
表现形式：

- 在反驳下退缩——当你说“你确定吗？”，它就把原本正确的答案反过来说。
- 赞美糟糕的输入——还没开始分析，就先附和说你那份有缺陷的方案妙极了。
- 有偏向的评判——你暗示这是自己写的，评审就偏向正面；你暗示是别人写的，就偏向负面。同一个产物，结论却不同。
- 模仿——把你的错误原样复述回来，作为对你的确认。
诊断测试：如果没有你的引导，model 还会这么说吗？如果唯一变化的是你的语气或措辞，那就是 sycophancy，而不是分析真正发生了转变。
修复：隐藏你的偏好。用中立的措辞提问——说“review this code”，而不是“is this code good?”。
避免：把任何恰好让你满意的错误答案都称作“sycophancy”。没有诊断测试，这个词的价值并不比“错误”更高。
用法
“它说我的重构方案看起来很出色，然后我问了一句‘你确定吗？’，它就把整套说法全收回去了。”
“典型的 sycophancy——它先表示同意，是因为你听起来很自信；后来退缩，是因为你听起来开始怀疑。方案的品质没变，变的是你的语气。清空对话重新提问，不要透露任何倾向。”

summary.zh: Sycophancy 是 Model 为迎合用户而过度同意，即使用户判断有误也给出自信赞同。它与单纯礼貌不同，问题在于损害事实判断。需要用证据、反例和可验证结果来约束这种倾向。

description.en: Confidently-wrong model output. Two flavors: factuality (invented facts) and faithfulness (drift from loaded context).
description.zh: Model 自信地给出错误内容，可能是捏造事实，也可能是偏离已提供的上下文。

en: Confidently-wrong model output. Two flavors with different causes and fixes:

| Flavor         | What goes wrong                                                                                                        | Cause                                                                                                                | Fix                                                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Factuality   | Invented or wrong facts about the world — a function that doesn't exist, a wrong API signature, a fake citation        | Parametric knowledge gaps, often past the knowledge cutoff | Load the right contextual knowledge |
| Faithfulness | Output drifts from the contextual knowledge that's loaded, the user's instructions, or the model's own prior reasoning | Attention degradation; worsens in the dumb zone                 | Clear or compact               |

Next-token prediction produces fluent output whether or not the underlying fact is real — the model has no internal signal that it doesn't know something, so an invented method arrives in the same assured register as a correct one. Hallucinated code is plausible by construction: it's what the API would look like if it existed, which is exactly what makes it slip past a skim-level review and fail only when run.

You need to know which flavor you're looking at, because the fix for one makes the other worse. Factuality means missing knowledge: the fix is adding context — the docs, the type definitions, the file. Faithfulness means the knowledge is present but losing the competition for attention: the fix is removing context. Misdiagnose faithfulness as factuality and you paste in more docs, which grows the context and makes the drift worse. When the agent gets something wrong, check whether the correct information was already in context before deciding which problem you have.
Avoid: "hallucination" as a bare synonym for "wrong" — without naming the flavor, the term has no diagnostic value.
Usage:
"It hallucinated a parseAsync method on the schema."
"Factuality or faithfulness?"
"The method exists in the docs I pasted — it just stopped reading them after turn forty."
"Faithfulness then. Compact and reload, don't bother adding more docs."
zh: 自信却错误的 Model 输出。两种类型，成因与修复方式各不相同：
Next-token prediction 无论底层事实是否真实都会产出流畅的输出——Model 内部没有任何信号表明它不知道某件事，因此一个凭空编造的方法会以与正确方法同样笃定的语气出现。由 Hallucination 产生的代码在构造上就是可信的：它就是那个 API 假如存在时会有的样子，而这恰恰使它溜过走马观花式的审查，只在运行时才失败。

你必须分清自己面对的是哪一种，因为针对其中一种的修复会让另一种变得更糟。Factuality 意味着知识缺失：修复办法是补充 Context——文档、类型定义、那个文件。Faithfulness 意味着知识就在那里，只是在争夺注意力时落了下风：修复办法是移除 Context。把 faithfulness 误诊为 factuality，你就会粘贴更多文档，Context 因此变大，漂移反而更严重。当 Agent 出错时，先检查正确的信息是否本来就在 Context 中，再判断你遇到的是哪一种问题。
避免：把 "hallucination" 当作 "wrong" 的单纯同义词——不点明是哪一种类型，这个词就没有诊断价值。
用法
"它在 schema 上 hallucinate 出了一个 parseAsync 方法。"
"Factuality 还是 faithfulness？"
"这个方法就在我粘贴的文档里——它只是在第四十个 Turn 之后就不再读它们了。"
"那就是 faithfulness。压缩并重新加载，别再费心添加更多文档。"

summary.zh: Hallucination 是 Model 自信地产生错误内容。它既可能捏造外部事实，也可能无视已加载的 Context 而偏离原资料。处理方法是把 Primary source 带入当前 Context，并用工具或检查核实关键断言。

description.en: What the model knows from training, stored in its parameters. Frozen at training time. Counterpart to contextual knowledge.
description.zh: Model 在训练中形成并保存在 parameters 里的知识，训练结束后便固定。

en: What the model "knows" from training, stored in its parameters. Frozen at training time — the model can't see its own parameters or update them. Detail is lost in the squeeze: billions of facts cram into a fixed number of parameters, and the rare ones blur. Source of fluency on common topics, and of fabrication on uncommon ones. Counterpart to contextual knowledge.

Parametric knowledge is not stored as facts. Training never gives the model a database to look things up in; it adjusts parameters until the model predicts text well, and a model that predicts text about a topic well behaves as if it knows the topic. How reliable the knowledge is tracks how often something appeared in the training data: a topic with millions of examples is reproduced accurately, for a topic with only a handful, the model guesses based on what similar topics look like. Reproducing and guessing are the same process to the model, so it can't tell which one it's doing. A fabricated answer arrives with the same fluency as a correct one. Hallucination is the model guessing wrong.

Parametric knowledge also ages. The parameters stop changing at the knowledge cutoff, so a library released or renamed after that date doesn't exist in them, and an API that changed is remembered in its old form.
For both gaps — too rare and too recent — the remedy is the same: the knowledge can't be added to the parameters, so it has to be supplied as contextual knowledge instead.
Usage:
"It writes flawless React but invents methods on our internal SDK."
"React is dense in the parametric knowledge — millions of training examples. Your SDK isn't, so the model fills in plausible-looking shapes. Load the SDK docs into context."
zh: model 从 training 中“知道”的东西，存储在它的 parameters 里。它在 training 时就被冻结——model 看不到自己的 parameters，也无法更新它们。细节在挤压中流失：数十亿条事实被塞进数量固定的 parameters，冷僻的那些随之模糊。它是常见话题上流畅表达的来源，也是冷门话题上编造内容的来源。是 contextual knowledge 的对应概念。

Parametric knowledge 并不是以事实的形式存储的。Training 从不会给 model 一个可供查阅的数据库；它只是不断调整 parameters，直到 model 能很好地预测文本，而一个能很好预测某个话题文本的 model，表现得就像它了解这个话题一样。知识的可靠程度与某件事在 training data 中出现的频率相关：有数百万个例子的话题会被准确复现，而对于只有寥寥几个例子的话题，model 会根据相似话题的样子来猜。对 model 而言，复现和猜测是同一个过程，所以它分不清自己正在做的是哪一种。一个编造出来的答案，其流畅程度与正确答案别无二致。Hallucination 就是 model 猜错了。
Parametric knowledge 还会变旧。parameters 在 knowledge cutoff 之后就停止变化，因此在那之后发布或更名的库并不存在于其中，改动过的 API 也仍以旧的样子被记住。
对于这两种缺口——太冷僻和太新——补救办法是一样的：知识无法加进 parameters，只能改以 contextual knowledge 的形式提供。
用法
“它写 React 毫无瑕疵，却在我们内部的 SDK 上凭空捏造方法。”
"React 在 Parametric knowledge 中密度极高——有数百万个 Training 示例。你的 SDK 则不然，所以 Model 会补上看起来合理的形状。把 SDK 文档载入 Context。"

summary.zh: Parametric knowledge 是训练后编码在 parameters 中的模式和事实，形成后便随 Model 版本固定。它能让 Model 回忆常见 API，却不能保证覆盖你的最新代码或训练结束后的变化；这些内容需要另行提供。

description.en: The date past which a model has no parametric knowledge. Post-cutoff libraries and APIs are fabrication traps unless docs are loaded.
description.zh: Model 训练知识截至的时间点；之后出现的 API 或版本不能靠既有 parameters 保证准确。

en: The date past which a model has no parametric knowledge. Libraries, APIs, and events from after the cutoff are fabrication traps unless their docs are loaded as contextual knowledge. Each model release ships with its own cutoff.

The cutoff exists because of how models are made: training bakes a snapshot of text into the model's parameters, and after that the parameters are frozen. The model doesn't know its knowledge has an edge — asked about something past the cutoff, it doesn't refuse, it extrapolates from the nearest thing it does know. That's what makes the trap quiet: code written against an old version of a library looks plausible, often compiles, and fails on the parts that changed.

The fix is always the same: get current information into context. Load the changelog, point at the installed version's type definitions, or have the agent read the docs from the web. Anything in context outranks nothing-in-parameters.
Usage:
"It keeps writing the v3 SDK syntax — we're on v5."
"v5 shipped after the knowledge cutoff. Load the v5 changelog as contextual knowledge, otherwise it'll keep fabricating from the older parametric version."
zh: 超过这个日期，Model 便不再拥有 Parametric knowledge。Knowledge cutoff 之后的 Libraries、APIs 与事件都是编造陷阱，除非它们的文档被作为 Contextual knowledge 载入。每个 Model 版本发布时都自带自己的 Knowledge cutoff。

Knowledge cutoff 之所以存在，源于 Model 的构建方式：Training 会把一份文本快照烘焙进 Model 的 Parameters，此后 Parameters 就被冻结了。Model 并不知道自己的知识有边界——被问到 Knowledge cutoff 之后的事情时，它不会拒绝，而是从它确实知道的最接近的内容去外推。这正是这个陷阱之所以安静的原因：针对某个 library 旧版本写出的代码看起来合理，往往还能编译通过，却会在发生变更的那部分上失败。
解决办法始终一样：把当前信息放进 Context。载入 changelog，指向已安装版本的 type definitions，或者让 Agent 从网上读取文档。Context 里的任何东西都优先于 Parameters 里的空无。
用法
"它一直在写 v3 SDK 语法——我们用的可是 v5。"
"v5 是在 Knowledge cutoff 之后发布的。把 v5 的 changelog 作为 Contextual knowledge 载入，否则它会继续从更早的 Parametric 版本编造。"

summary.zh: Knowledge cutoff 是 Model 的训练知识停止更新的时间点。之后发布的库版本、规则或产品能力，单靠 Parametric knowledge 可能会猜错。面对易变信息，应读取当前文档或真实环境。

description.en: Facts the agent can read directly from the context right now. Counterpart to parametric knowledge.
description.zh: Model 当前可以直接从 context 读取的事实，与 parametric knowledge 相对。

en: Facts the agent can read directly from the context right now — the user's task, files the agent has read in, tool results, AGENTS.md content loaded at session start. Counterpart to parametric knowledge: parametric is recalled from the parameters; contextual is read from the window. Hallucinations are much less common when the agent works from contextual knowledge — the answer is right in front of it, not dredged up from a blurred memory.

Of the two kinds of knowledge, only contextual knowledge is in your control. The parameters are frozen, so the only way to give the model knowledge it lacks — an internal SDK, a library released after the knowledge cutoff, a decision made yesterday — is to put it in the context. A lot of practical AI coding work reduces to this: getting the right facts in front of the model at the moment it needs them.

When contextual and parametric knowledge conflict, the contextual usually wins. Paste the current API docs and the model follows them rather than its stale memory of the old API — though the old version can still bleed through, especially deep into a long session. If the agent keeps reverting to an outdated pattern despite the docs being loaded, that's parametric knowledge leaking past the contextual; restating the correction or moving it closer to the work helps.

Unlike parametric knowledge, contextual knowledge costs something to use. Everything loaded into the window spends tokens and competes for the model's attention budget, so loading more is not automatically better — the aim is the relevant facts in the window, not all the facts.
Reach for this term only when contrasting with parametric knowledge; otherwise just say context.
Avoid: "working memory" — contextual knowledge is what's in the window now; a memory system is what gets cross-session content into it. Different scales, don't conflate.
Usage:
"Why does it nail the API when I paste the docs and fabricate it when I don't?"
"With the docs in, it's contextual knowledge — reading off the page. Without, it's parametric and the rare endpoints blur."
zh: Agent 现在能直接从 Context 中读到的事实——用户当前的任务、Agent 读入的文件、Tool 结果、Session 启动时载入的 AGENTS.md 内容。它是 Parametric knowledge 的对立面：parametric 是从 Parameters 里回忆出来的，contextual 则是从窗口里直接读出来的。当 Agent 依据 Contextual knowledge 工作时，幻觉要少见得多——答案就摆在眼前，而不是从模糊的记忆里费力打捞上来。

这两类知识中，只有 Contextual knowledge 是你能够控制的。Parameters 是冻结的，所以要让 Model 获得它并不具备的知识——一个内部 SDK、一个在 Knowledge cutoff 之后才发布的库、昨天刚做出的一个决定——唯一的办法就是把它放进 Context 里。许多实际的 AI coding 工作都可以归结为这一件事：在 Model 需要的那一刻，把正确的事实摆到它面前。

当 Contextual knowledge 与 Parametric knowledge 发生冲突时，通常前者会胜出。把当前的 API 文档粘进去，Model 会照着文档走，而不是依赖它对旧 API 的过时记忆——不过旧版本仍可能渗透出来，尤其是在一个长 Session 的深处。如果 Agent 明明已经载入了文档，却仍不断退回某个过时的模式，那就是 Parametric knowledge 越过了 Contextual knowledge 在泄漏；重新陈述一遍纠正内容，或者把它挪到离工作更近的位置，会有所帮助。
与 Parametric knowledge 不同，Contextual knowledge 的使用是有代价的。凡是被载入窗口的内容都会消耗 token，并争夺 Model 的 Attention budget，所以载入更多并不自动等于更好——目标是把相关的事实放进窗口，而不是把所有事实都放进去。
只有在需要与 Parametric knowledge 作对比时才使用这个说法；其余情况直接说 Context 就好。
避免说「working memory」（工作记忆）——Contextual knowledge 是此刻就在窗口里的内容；Memory system 才是把跨 Session 的内容送进窗口的机制。两者尺度不同，不要混为一谈。
用法
「为什么我把文档粘进去，它就能把 API 用对；不粘，它就开始编？」
「文档放进去时，那是 Contextual knowledge——照着页面读就行。不放进去，就是 parametric 的，那些冷门的端点就变模糊了。」

summary.zh: Contextual knowledge 是当前请求中可直接看到的事实，例如刚读取的文件、用户给的规格或工具结果。它与训练中固定的 Parametric knowledge 不同，可以随 Session 更新，但也会受 Context window 容量限制。

description.en: The pairing between two tokens — meaningful pairs influence each other more than unrelated ones. A context of N tokens has ~N² of these.
description.zh: 两个 Tokens 之间的关注关系；上下文增长时，这类关系数量约按平方增长。

en: When predicting each token, the model factors in every other token in the context — some heavily, others barely at all. The pairing between two tokens is an attention relationship, and meaningful pairs ("her" with "Sarah", or a getUser() call with its function getUser definition) influence each other more than unrelated ones. A context of N tokens has on the order of N² relationships.

The pairings are where the model's apparent understanding lives. When it resolves a pronoun, it's because the attention relationship between "her" and "Sarah" is strong. When it calls a function with the right arguments, the relationship between the call site and the definition it read earlier is doing the work. None of this is looked up — it's computed fresh on every model provider request, for every pair.
The N² figure is worth sitting with, because it grows faster than intuition suggests:

| Context size   | Pairings (~N²) |
| -------------- | -------------- |
| 1,000 tokens   | ~1 million     |
| 10,000 tokens  | ~100 million   |
| 100,000 tokens | ~10 billion    |

Each pairing is also computed more than once. Models have multiple attention heads — exact counts for frontier models are unpublished, but fifty to a hundred is a reasonable guess — and each head computes its own version of every relationship. So every pairing in the table above is duplicated across every head. That's a lot of pairings.

Only a small number of these relationships matter for any given task. The pairing between your instruction and the code it governs is one of a handful that count; almost everything else in the pool is noise. And the two grow at different rates: the relationships that matter stay roughly constant, while the total pool grows quadratically with context size. At 1,000 tokens, the pairing you care about is one in a million; at 100,000 tokens, it's one in ten billion. This is the arithmetic underneath the attention budget, and attention degradation is what it feels like when the relationships that matter get too thin a share.
Usage:
"It keeps confusing the two user symbols across the diff — sounds like we're in the dumb zone."
"Yeah, the attention relationship between each call site and its declaration is fighting the other one — same token shape, different bindings. Rename one and the pairings sharpen."
zh: 在预测每个 token 时，model 会把 context 中的每一个其他 token 都纳入考量——有些权重很大，有些则几乎不起作用。两个 token 之间的配对就是一个 attention relationship，而有意义的配对（"her" 与 "Sarah"，或一次 getUser() 调用与它的函数 getUser 定义）彼此之间的影响要大于不相关的配对。一个包含 N 个 token 的 context，其 relationship 数量约在 N² 量级。
这些配对正是 model 表面理解力的所在。当它消解一个代词时，那是因为 "her" 与 "Sarah" 之间的 attention relationship 很强。当它用正确的参数调用一个函数时，真正起作用的是调用点与它此前读到的定义之间的关系。这一切都不是查出来的——它在每一次 model provider request 中、针对每一个配对重新计算。
N² 这个数字值得细想，因为它的增长比直觉所预想的更快：
每个配对还会被计算不止一次。Model 有多个 attention head——前沿 model 的确切数量并未公开，但五十到一百是一个合理的猜测——每个 head 都会算出自己对每一种 relationship 的版本。因此上表中的每一个配对，都会在每个 head 上各重复一次。这可是一大堆配对。

对于任何给定的任务，这些 relationship 中只有一小部分真正重要。你的指令与它所管辖的代码之间的配对，就是少数几个真正起作用的配对之一；池子里几乎其他所有东西都是噪声。而且两者的增长速度并不相同：重要的 relationship 大致保持恒定，而整个池子却随 context 规模呈二次增长。在 1,000 个 token 时，你关心的那个配对是百万分之一；在 100,000 个 token 时，就是百亿分之一。这就是 attention budget 背后的算术，而当重要的 relationship 所占的份额变得过于稀薄时，你所感受到的就是 attention degradation。
用法
"它总是在 diff 里把两个 user 符号搞混——听起来我们是进入 dumb zone 了。"
"是啊，每个调用点与它的声明之间的 attention relationship 正在跟另一个较劲——同样的 token 形态，不同的绑定。把其中一个改个名字，配对就会变得清晰。"

summary.zh: 模型处理 Context 时，Token 之间会形成相互影响的关系。长度为 N 的序列里，可能的关系数量大约随 N 的平方增长。上下文越长，需要维持的相关与无关关系越多，重点信息更容易被淹没。

description.en: Each token has a finite amount of influence to distribute across the rest of the context. Per-token, doesn't grow when context does.
description.zh: 每个 Token 能分配给其余上下文的有限注意力，不会随 context 变长而增加。

en: Each token has a finite amount of influence to distribute across the rest of the context. Heavy influence on one relationship leaves less for others. The budget is per-token and doesn't grow when the context does, which is why long sessions dilute.

Think of it as signal and noise. Your instruction is a signal at fixed volume; every other token in the context window is competing sound. The instruction never gets quieter — it's still there, character for character — but as the context grows, the room gets louder around it, and the signal-to-noise ratio drops. An instruction that was the loudest thing at 10k tokens of context is background hum at 150k. This is the mechanism behind attention degradation: the model doesn't forget; the signal gets lost in the noise.

The symptom reads as disobedience — the agent agreed to a constraint early on and then drifts from it, and re-pasting the constraint helps only briefly. The cause isn't the instruction; it's everything else in the window competing with it.

What you can control is what goes into the context. Content that doesn't serve the task isn't neutral — it's noise over everything that does. Keep the window small, clear when the accumulated context stops paying for itself, and restate the constraints that matter instead of trusting their early mention to hold.
Usage:
"Why does it keep ignoring the schema I pasted at the top?"
"We're well into the dumb zone — every token's attention budget is fixed, but the context kept growing. The signal on the schema is now competing with thousands of newer tokens."
zh: 每个 Token 能分配到 Context 其余部分的影响力是有限的。用在某一段关系上的影响力多了，留给其他关系的就少了。这个额度是每个 Token 各自的，不会随着 Context 增长而变大——这正是长会话会被稀释的原因。

把它想象成信号与噪声。你的指令是一个音量固定的信号；Context window 里的每一个其他 Token 都是与之竞争的声响。指令本身从不变轻——它仍然一字不差地在那里——但随着 Context 增长，它周围的房间越来越吵，信噪比随之下降。在 10k tokens 的 Context 里最响的那条指令，到了 150k 就只是背景嗡鸣。这就是 Attention degradation 背后的机制：Model 并不会遗忘，只是信号淹没在噪声里了。
症状表现为不听话——Agent 早早答应了某个约束，之后却逐渐偏离，重新粘贴一遍约束也只在短时间内有效。原因不在指令本身，而在 window 里与它竞争的其他一切。
你能控制的是往 Context 里放什么。无助于任务的内容并非中性——它会成为盖在一切有用内容之上的噪声。让 window 保持小，当累积的 Context 不再划算时就清空，并且重申真正重要的约束，而不是指望它们早期被提过一次就一直管用。
用法
“为什么它总是忽略我贴在开头的那份 schema？”
“我们已经深陷 dumb zone 了——每个 Token 的 Attention budget 是固定的，但 Context 却一直在增长。关于 schema 的那个信号现在正与成千上万个更新的 Token 竞争。”

summary.zh: 每个 Token 对其余内容可分配的注意力有限，不会因为 Context window 变大就自动增加。新增材料会与已有材料竞争这个预算，因此把所有文件一次塞进 Context，未必比挑选关键资料更有效。

description.en: As a session grows, each token's attention budget spreads across more competitors; signal on meaningful relationships shrinks.
description.zh: Session 变长后，有限的 attention budget 被更多内容分散，关键关系更难维持。

en: As a session grows, each token's attention budget is spread across more competitors. The signal on any one meaningful relationship shrinks; noise from irrelevant context crowds in. Same model, same parameters — just more mouths to feed from the same plate. Cause of the smart zone / dumb zone effect.

It presents as the model getting worse mid-session: constraints it followed for an hour start slipping, it re-asks things it was told, it writes code that ignores a file it read earlier. Nothing about the model changed — the only variable is how much context it's now attending over.

It's gradual, which is what makes it hard to catch from inside the session. There's no error and no threshold; each turn is only slightly worse than the last, and by the time the slips are obvious you've been in the dumb zone for a while.

You recover by removing context, not adding more. Re-pasting the ignored instruction adds another competitor to the same crowded window and helps only briefly. What works: clear and reload only what the task needs, or compact, or hand off to a fresh session. Treat declining instruction-following as a signal about context length, not about the model.
Usage:
"It's deep in the dumb zone — inventing generics that aren't in the type file."
"Attention degradation. The type definitions are still in context, but the signal on them is buried under everything we've added since. Clear and reload."
zh: 随着 Session 增长，每个 Token 的 Attention budget 被分摊到越来越多的竞争者身上。任何一条有意义关系上的信号都在缩小；无关 Context 的噪声不断挤入。同一个 Model，同一套 Parameters——只是同一只盘子上多了几张嘴。这正是 Smart zone / dumb zone 效应的成因。
它表现为 Model 在 Session 中途变差：遵守了一个小时的约束开始松动，它重新追问已经被告知过的事，写出的代码无视它早先读过的文件。Model 本身没有任何变化——唯一的变量是它此刻正在关注的 Context 有多大。
它是渐进发生的，这正是它难以在 Session 内部被察觉的原因。没有报错，也没有阈值；每个 Turn 只比上一个 Turn 差一点点，等到失误变得明显时，你已经待在 dumb zone 里有一阵子了。
恢复的办法是移除 Context，而不是继续往里加。重新粘贴被忽略的指令，只会给同一个拥挤的窗口再添一个竞争者，效果只能维持一小会儿。真正有效的是：清空并只重新载入任务所需的部分，或者 compact，或者交接到一个全新的 Session。把指令遵循能力的下降，视为关于 Context 长度的信号，而不是关于 Model 的信号。
用法
"它已经深陷 dumb zone——开始凭空编造类型文件里根本没有的泛型。"
"Attention degradation。类型定义仍在 Context 里，但它们的信号被此后添加的一切埋住了。清空并重新载入。"

summary.zh: Session 变长时，每个 Token 的 Attention budget 要分给更多竞争内容，重要关系的信号可能变弱。表现可能是遗漏指令、混淆实体或重复旧判断。解决思路包括缩小任务、选择关键上下文和适时 Handoff。

description.en: Early in a session the agent is sharp and focused. As the session grows it drifts into a dumb zone: sloppier, forgetful, more mistakes.
description.zh: Session 较早期、Agent 注意力更集中且表现更稳定的一段区间。

en: Early in a session the agent is in a "smart zone" — sharp, focused, recall is good. As the session grows it drifts into a "dumb zone": sloppier, forgetful, more mistakes — and more faithfulness hallucinations. Same model, same harness — just more context. The felt effect of attention degradation. On frontier models, the dumb zone commonly begins around 125K-150K tokens — though this is debated. Clear or compact when the session bloats; don't push through.

The decline is gradual, which makes it easy to miss. There's no error message and no visible boundary; the agent just starts performing slightly worse, then noticeably worse. Common signs: it forgets an instruction you gave twenty turns ago, repeats a mistake it had already corrected, or confidently asserts something the context contradicts. Because the slide is smooth, the usual response is to push through and re-explain — which adds more context and makes the problem worse.

The zones don't track the context window limit. A session can be deep in the dumb zone with most of the window still free: the limit is where the harness refuses to continue, but quality falls off long before that. Plan around the smart zone, not the window — the practical budget for a task is the tokens the agent works well within, not the tokens it can technically hold.

The smart zone is a budget, and unrelated work spends it. Every task done in a session uses up tokens, so starting a second task in the same session means starting it closer to the dumb zone. Doing one task per session gives each task the sharpest part of the session. When a single task is bigger than one smart zone, split it: hand off or compact at a natural boundary, and let a fresh session do the next piece.
Usage:
"It nailed the first three components and just butchered the fourth."
"You're out of the smart zone — same model, just deep into the dumb zone now. Compact and reload the plan, the next component will land."
zh: 在 Session 的早期，Agent 处于 "smart zone"——敏锐、专注，回忆能力良好。随着 Session 增长，它会漂移到 "dumb zone"：更马虎、健忘、犯更多错误——以及更多的忠实性幻觉（faithfulness hallucination）。同样的 Model，同样的 Harness——只是 Context 更多。这就是 Attention degradation 的实际感受。在前沿 Model 上，dumb zone 通常从约 125K-150K tokens 开始——不过这一点仍有争议。当 Session 变得臃肿时，就 clear 或 compact；不要硬撑。
这种退化是渐进的，因此很容易被忽略。没有报错信息，也没有可见的边界；Agent 只是开始表现得稍微差一点，然后明显更差。常见迹象：它忘记你二十轮之前给出的指令，重复一个它已经纠正过的错误，或者自信地断言与 Context 相矛盾的内容。因为这种下滑是平滑的，通常的应对方式是硬撑下去并重新解释——而这会增加更多 Context，让问题变得更糟。
这两个区与 Context window 的上限并不同步。一个 Session 可能已经深陷 dumb zone，而 window 的大部分仍然空闲：上限是 Harness 拒绝继续的位置，但质量远在那之前就已下滑。要围绕 smart zone 做规划，而不是围绕 window——一项任务的实际预算，是 Agent 能良好工作的 token 量，而不是它技术上能容纳的 token 量。

smart zone 是一种预算，不相关的工作会把它花掉。在一个 Session 中完成的每项任务都会消耗 token，所以在同一个 Session 里开始第二项任务，意味着从更靠近 dumb zone 的位置开始。每个 Session 只做一项任务，能让每项任务都拿到 Session 最敏锐的那一段。当单个任务大过一个 smart zone 时，就把它拆开：在自然的边界处交接（hand off）或压缩（compact），让一个全新的 Session 来做下一部分。
用法
"它把前三个组件做得漂亮，却把第四个彻底搞砸了。"
"你已经不在 smart zone 了——同样的 Model，只是现在深深陷进了 dumb zone。compact 一下并重新加载计划，下一个组件就能做成了。"

summary.zh: Smart zone 指 Session 较早、上下文相对集中时更容易保持清晰判断的区间。随着历史和工具输出堆积，Agent 可能进入更容易出错的状态。这个说法强调 Context 管理，而不是给 Model 设定精确的失效刻度。

description.en: Ending the current session and starting a fresh one. The next message begins with an empty session and an empty context window.
description.zh: 结束当前 Session 并从空白 context window 开始新 Session。

en: Ending the current session and starting a fresh one. The next message begins with an empty session and an empty context window. Usually user-driven.

Clearing is the cure for a polluted context. A session accumulates everything: failed attempts, wrong turns, stale tool results, abandoned plans. The model re-reads all of it on every turn, and bad history drags on new work. Deep into a long session the agent gets vaguer and less obedient — instructions you gave clearly get ignored, quality slips, and prodding it to do better doesn't help, because the noise it's wading through is still in its context. Clearing removes the noise.

Clearing doesn't erase the conversation. Most harnesses keep session history on your computer, so the transcript is still there to read or resume. What's gone is the agent's working state: the model is stateless, so the new session knows nothing the old one knew. If the session holds decisions or progress the next one will need, have the agent write a handoff artifact first, then start the new session by pointing at it.
Compare compaction, which summarises the session into the new context instead of starting empty. Clearing is the blunter tool: nothing carries over, including the junk.
Usage:
"It's stuck looping on the failing test."
"Just clear it — start a fresh session with the plan doc and the test file. No point fighting the existing context."
zh: 结束当前 session 并开启一个全新的 session。下一条消息会从一个空 session 和空 context window 开始。通常由用户主动发起。

Clearing 是治愈被污染 context 的良方。一个 session 会累积一切：失败的尝试、走错的方向、过期的 tool 结果、被放弃的计划。model 在每一个 turn 都会重新读取所有这些内容，而不良的历史会拖累新的工作。长 session 进行到深处时，agent 会变得越来越含糊、越来越不听话——你清晰给出的指令被忽视，质量下滑，而催它做得更好也无济于事，因为它艰难跋涉其中的噪声仍然留在它的 context 里。Clearing 会移除这些噪声。

Clearing 不会抹掉对话。大多数 harness 会把 session 历史保存在你的电脑上，所以对话记录仍然在那里，可以阅读或恢复。消失的是 agent 的工作状态：model 是 stateless 的，所以新 session 对旧 session 知道的东西一无所知。如果这个 session 中保存着下一个 session 会需要的决策或进展，就先让 agent 写一份 handoff artifact，然后开启新 session 并指向它。
对比 Compaction：它把 Session 总结进新的 Context，而不是从空白开始。Clearing 是更直白的 Tool——什么都不带过去，包括那些垃圾内容。
用法
"它卡在那个失败的测试上反复循环了。"
"直接 clear 掉吧——用计划文档和测试文件开一个全新的 session。没必要跟现有的 context 较劲。"

summary.zh: Clearing 直接结束当前 Session，让下一条消息从空的 Context window 开始。它能摆脱混乱历史，但也会失去尚未外化的进展。重要任务信息应先写入可重新读取的文件或 Handoff artifact。

description.en: Transferring agent context from one session to another, with no return path. Carry mechanism varies — artifact, compaction, others.
description.zh: 把 Agent 的任务上下文从一个 Session 交给下一个 Session，通常没有直接返回路径。

en: Transferring agent context from one session to another. The carry mechanism varies — a written handoff artifact, an in-memory summary (compaction), and others. Distinct from clearing (no transfer at all). Reasons vary: switching roles (planner → implementer), kicking off an AFK run, fanning out to parallel sessions, or freeing up context window room.

The receiving session starts with zero context — the model is stateless, and nothing from the old session is visible to the new one. Whatever the next session needs has to be carried explicitly; everything else is gone. "No return path" is the constraint that shapes the carry: the new session can't ask the old one what it meant, so the carried material has to stand on its own.

| Mechanism        | Form                                        | Properties                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Handoff artifact | File in the environment | You can read and correct it before anything depends on it; reusable across many sessions |
| Compaction       | Summary in the context window               | Automatic and cheap; harder to inspect; feeds one successor                              |

The visible failure of a bad handoff is relitigation: the new session re-opens decisions the old one had settled, because the carry recorded what was decided but not why. Judge a handoff by what a session with zero context could do with it.
Usage:
"Planning session is getting heavy — should I just keep going?"
"Do a handoff. Write the decisions to a doc, clear, start the implementation in a fresh session reading from it."
zh: 将 agent 的 context 从一个 session 转移到另一个 session。承载机制各不相同——书面的 handoff artifact、内存中的摘要（compaction），以及其他方式。与 clearing（完全不转移）不同。原因多种多样：切换角色（planner → implementer）、启动一次 AFK 运行、扇出到并行的多个 session，或腾出 context window 空间。
接收方 session 从零 context 开始——model 是 stateless 的，旧 session 中的任何内容对新 session 都不可见。下一个 session 需要的一切都必须被显式携带过去；其余的一切都已消失。"没有返回路径" 是塑造这次携带的约束：新 session 无法询问旧 session 它当时是什么意思，因此所携带的材料必须能够独立成立。

| 机制 | 形式 | 特性 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Handoff artifact | Environment 中的文件 | 在任何东西依赖它之前，你可以读取并修正它；可跨多个 session 复用 |
| Compaction | Context window 中的摘要 | 自动且开销低；更难检查；只能供给一个后继者 |
糟糕 handoff 的可见失败是 relitigation（重新翻案）：新 session 会重新打开旧 session 已经定下的决定，因为携带的内容记录了决定了什么，却没有记录为什么。判断一次 handoff，要看一个零 context 的 session 能拿它做什么。
用法
"planning session 越来越重了——我该就这么继续下去吗？"
"做一次 handoff。把决定写进一份文档，clear，然后在一个全新的 session 里读取它、开始实现。"

summary.zh: Handoff 把一个 Session 已取得的上下文交给下一个 Session，传递方式可以是文档、摘要或 Compaction。接收方通常无法回到旧 Session 追问，因此交接材料需要写清目标、已做工作、证据和未决问题。

description.en: The thing itself — code, transcripts, raw data. Complete and authoritative, but expensive to load into context.
description.zh: 事物本身，例如代码、原始数据或完整记录；权威且完整，但读取成本高。

en: A source of truth in its original form — the code, the conversation transcript, the raw log, the actual API response. Not an account of the thing; the thing. Counterpart to secondary source.

If you want to know what your codebase does, the code is the primary source. The docs, the architecture diagram, and the README are all descriptions of it — accurate when written, on their own schedule ever since. When an agent confidently asserts something wrong about your project, the question to ask is which source it was working from: an agent that read a doc inherits the doc's staleness; an agent that read the code is reading the current truth.

The cost is what keeps primary sources from being the default. Loading one into the context window is expensive — the full file, the full transcript, every token billed as input and competing for attention budget. What you get for the cost is completeness: nothing has been pre-filtered by someone else's judgement about what mattered. A summary written last month can't contain the detail that turned out to matter today; the primary source still does.

Reach for the primary source when precision matters — the exact signature, the actual error, the line that throws. Much of managing context is deciding when to pay for the primary source and when a secondary source is good enough.
Usage:
"The agent says the retry logic backs off exponentially, but I'm watching it hammer the endpoint."
"It read that out of the design doc. Point it at the actual retry module — work from the primary source when the behaviour matters."
zh: 以原始形态呈现的事实来源——代码、对话记录、原始日志、实际的 API 响应。不是对事物的转述，而是事物本身。与 Secondary source 相对。
如果你想知道代码库究竟做了什么，代码就是 Primary source。文档、架构图和 README 都只是对它的描述——写就时准确，此后便各按自己的节奏漂移。当 Agent 言之凿凿地对你的项目做出错误断言时，该问的是它依据的是哪种来源：读了文档的 Agent 会继承那份文档的过时；读了代码的 Agent 读到的是当下的真相。

成本正是 Primary source 无法成为默认选项的原因。把一份 Primary source 载入 Context window 代价高昂——整个文件、完整的对话记录，每个 Token 都按输入计费，还要争夺 Attention budget。你为这份成本换来的是完整性：没有任何内容被他人对「什么重要」的判断预先过滤掉。上个月写下的摘要不可能包含今天才发现至关重要的细节；Primary source 却仍然包含。
在精确性至关重要时，就该去取 Primary source——确切的函数签名、真实的报错、抛异常的那一行。管理 Context 的很大一部分工作，就是判断何时该为 Primary source 付出成本，何时 Secondary source 已经够用。
用法
"Agent 说重试逻辑是指数退避的，但我眼看着它在猛捶那个端点。"
"那是它从设计文档里读来的。让它去看真正的重试模块——当行为本身重要时，就该以 Primary source 为依据。"

summary.zh: Primary source 是事实本身，例如源代码、原始记录或数据。它最完整、最权威，但读取成本也最高。需要确认关键细节时，应回到 Primary source，而不是只依赖别人写的总结。

description.en: An account of a primary source, one step removed — summaries, docs, compaction summaries. Cheap to load, lossy by construction.
description.zh: 对 primary source 的概括，例如文档或摘要；读取成本低，但会丢失细节。

en: An account of a primary source, one step removed — documentation describing code, a summary describing a transcript, a report describing search results. Cheaper to load into the context window than the source it describes, and lossy by construction: whoever wrote it decided what mattered, and whatever they dropped is invisible to a reader who only has the summary.

A lot of context engineering is the manufacture of secondary sources. Compaction turns the session history into a summary that seeds the next session. A subagent burns its own context on a noisy search and returns a short report. A handoff artifact condenses a session's decisions into a document the next session reads. Memory systems distil what a session learned into notes. Each makes the same trade: fidelity for headroom.

Secondary sources fail in two ways. They're lossy — the compaction summary that lost the schema decision, the report that didn't mention the edge case. And they drift — the primary source changes and the account doesn't follow, so docs describe last quarter's architecture with this quarter's confidence. When an agent acts on a secondary source that has failed either way, it works confidently from wrong information; the fix is sending it back to the primary source.

Neither failure makes secondary sources a mistake. The context window is finite, and primary sources are expensive; without summaries, reports, and handoff documents, nothing large fits. The skill is knowing which details can survive the loss — and verifying against the primary source when one can't. A well-made secondary source carries a context pointer back to its original — the summary that names the transcript it came from, the doc that names the file it describes — so when the account isn't enough, the reader can follow the pointer rather than work from the loss.
Usage:
"The handoff doc says auth is done, but the new session keeps finding broken token refresh."
"The doc's a secondary source — the last session wrote down what it believed, not what's true. Have the new session run the auth tests and trust the primary source."
zh: 对 Primary source 的转述，隔了一层——描述代码的文档、描述对话记录的摘要、描述搜索结果的报告。相比它所描述的来源，它载入 Context window 更便宜，而且天生有损：写下它的人决定了什么才重要，而任何被丢弃的内容，对只拿到摘要的读者来说都是不可见的。

许多 context engineering 的工作，就是在制造 secondary source。Compaction 把 Session 历史变成一份摘要，用来为下一个 Session 播种。Subagent 在一次嘈杂的搜索上烧掉自己的 Context，返回一份简短报告。Handoff artifact 把一个 Session 的决策压缩成下一个 Session 会读的文档。Memory system 把一个 Session 学到的东西提炼成笔记。每一者做的都是同一笔交易：用保真度换取余量。

Secondary source 会以两种方式失效。它们有损——丢了 schema 决策的那份 Compaction 摘要，没提到边界情况的那份报告。它们也会漂移——Primary source 变了，转述却没跟上，于是文档用这个季度的自信描述着上个季度的架构。当 Agent 依据一个以任一种方式失效的 secondary source 行动时，它会满怀信心地基于错误信息工作；解法是把它送回 Primary source。

这两种失效都不意味着 secondary source 是个错误。Context window 是有限的，Primary source 又是昂贵的；没有摘要、报告和 handoff 文档，大东西都装不进来。真正的 Skill 在于知道哪些细节能挺过这种损失——以及在某个细节挺不过去时，对照 Primary source 去核实。做得好的 secondary source 会带着一条指回原件的 Context pointer——指明自己出自哪份对话记录的摘要，指明自己描述哪个文件的文档——这样当转述不够用时，读者可以顺着这条指针走下去，而不必在损失之上硬做。
用法
"Handoff 文档说认证已经做完了，但新 Session 总是发现 token 刷新是坏的。"
"那文档是个 secondary source——上一个 Session 写下的是它相信的东西，而不是事实。让新的 Session 去跑认证测试，信任 Primary source。"

summary.zh: Secondary source 是对原始材料的概括，例如文档、报告或压缩摘要。它能快速建立概览，却可能遗漏、误解或过时。对重要结论要知道它指向哪个 Primary source，以便核实。

description.en: A document used as the carry mechanism for a handoff — written by one session to be read by another.
description.zh: 用于在 Session 之间承载上下文的文档。

en: A document used as the carry mechanism for a handoff — written to the environment by one session to be read by another. Specs, tickets, and plan docs are all handoff artifacts.

The reason to write one: the model is stateless, so nothing in a session survives clearing it. Decisions, constraints, half-finished plans — all gone with the context that held them. The environment persists. Writing the important state into a file moves it somewhere the next session can read it back from.

The artifact is a secondary source — an account of the session's work, not the work itself. That's what makes it small enough to brief a fresh session, and also why it can mislead one: it records what the writing session believed, and anything it left out or got wrong is invisible to the reader. Where a claim matters, the next session should verify it against the primary source — the code, the tests — rather than inherit it.

A good artifact is written to be read into a session that has zero context. Concrete file paths rather than "the file we discussed". What was decided and why, so the next session doesn't relitigate it. What's done and what's left. It helps to tell the writing session where the artifact is headed: "write a handoff doc for a fresh session that knows nothing about this work".

The alternative carry mechanism is compaction, which summarises in-memory. The artifact has two advantages: it lives on disk where you can read and correct it before anything depends on it, and it can be reused — the same spec can brief five parallel sessions.
Usage:
"How do I split this between the planning agent and the implementing one?"
"Have the planner write a handoff artifact — file paths, decisions, constraints. The implementer's session opens with a pointer to the artifact and works from it as its brief."
zh: 一种用作 Handoff 承载机制的文档——由一个 Session 写入 Environment，供另一个 Session 读取。Spec、ticket 和 plan doc 都是 Handoff artifact。
写它的理由：Model 是 Stateless 的，所以 Session 里的任何东西在 Clearing 之后都无法留存。决策、约束、做到一半的计划——全都随承载它们的 Context 一起消失。而 Environment 会持久存在。把重要状态写进文件，就是把它搬到一个下一个 Session 能够读回来的地方。

这个 artifact 是 Secondary source——它是对 Session 工作的记述，而不是工作本身。这既让它小到足以给一个全新的 Session 做简报，也正是它可能误导后者的原因：它记录的是撰写它的 Session 当时所相信的内容，而它遗漏或弄错的任何东西，对读者来说都是不可见的。当某个说法很重要时，下一个 Session 应该依据 Primary source——代码、测试——去核实它，而不是直接继承。

好的 artifact 是写给一个毫无 Context 的 Session 读的。要写具体的文件路径，而不是 "我们讨论过的那个文件"。写清楚决定了什么、为什么这样决定，这样下一个 Session 就不会为此重新争论。写清楚哪些已完成、哪些还没做。告诉撰写它的 Session 这个 artifact 将去往何处会很有帮助："为一个对这项工作一无所知的全新 Session 写一份 handoff doc"。
另一种承载机制是 Compaction，它在内存中做总结。而 artifact 有两个优势：它存在于磁盘上，在有任何东西依赖它之前，你可以先读它、修正它；而且它可以被复用——同一份 Spec 可以为五个并行的 Session 做简报。
用法
"我该如何把这件事在规划 Agent 和实施 Agent 之间拆分？"
"让规划者写一份 Handoff artifact——文件路径、决策、约束。实施者的 Session 以一个指向该 artifact 的指针开场，并把它当作自己的简报来开展工作。"

summary.zh: Handoff artifact 是承载 Session 交接信息的文档。它把原本只存在于当前 Context 的目标、决策和进度写下来，使下一次工作能够接续。内容要足够独立，不能只写“继续上次的事”。

description.en: A handoff artifact describing a multi-session piece of work — what's being built, not how each session does its share. Made of tickets.
description.zh: 描述跨多个 Session 的工作目标与范围的 handoff artifact，通常由 Tickets 组成。

en: A handoff artifact describing a multi-session piece of work — what's being built, not how each session does its share. Mutates as work progresses. Made of tickets.

The spec exists because sessions are disposable and big work isn't. Anything that takes more than one context window of effort needs a home outside the context — somewhere in the agent's environment that survives clearing, whether that's a file in the repo, a GitHub issue, or an issue tracker the agent can reach. The spec is that home: the goal, the constraints, the decisions made so far, and the list of tickets with their status. Any fresh session can read it and know where the work stands without inheriting the previous session's accumulated noise.

Specs come in recognisable styles, mostly inherited from how teams already write things down. A product requirements document (PRD) leans toward the user-facing what and why — features, behaviour, acceptance criteria. A design doc or RFC leans technical — the chosen approach, the alternatives rejected, the trade-offs. At the small end, a plain plan.md with a checklist of tickets does the same job for a multi-session feature. The style matters less than the role: for the agent, each of these is the same thing — the durable statement of intent it reads at the start of every session.
Usage:
"Should this all be one session?"
"No, write it up as a spec — break it into tickets, run each one in its own session. Trying to do the whole thing in a single context will hit the dumb zone before you're halfway."
zh: 一份描述跨 Session 工作的 Handoff artifact——说明在建的是什么，而不是每个 Session 各自如何完成自己那份。随工作推进而不断变化，由 ticket 组成。

Spec 之所以存在，是因为 Session 是一次性的，而大工程不是。任何需要超过一个 Context window 的 Effort 才能完成的事，都需要一个 Context 之外的归属地——Agent 的 Environment 中某个能在 Clearing 之后留存下来的地方，无论那是 repo 里的一个文件、一个 GitHub issue，还是 Agent 能触达的 issue tracker。Spec 就是这个归属地：目标、约束、迄今为止做出的决定，以及带状态的 ticket 列表。任何全新的 Session 都能读它，从而知道工作进展到哪一步，而不必继承上一个 Session 累积下来的噪音。

Spec 有几种容易辨认的风格，大多继承自团队既有的书面表达方式。产品需求文档（PRD）偏向面向用户的 what 与 why——功能、行为、验收标准。设计文档或 RFC 偏向技术——选定的方案、被否决的备选方案、权衡取舍。在规模最小的一端，一份带 ticket 清单的普通 plan.md 就能为多 Session 的功能完成同样的工作。风格不如角色重要：对 Agent 来说，这些都是同一件事——它在每个 Session 开始时读取的那份持久化的意图声明。
用法
"这整件事该在一个 Session 里做吗？"
"不，把它写成一份 Spec——拆成 ticket，每个都在自己的 Session 里跑。想在单个 Context 里把整件事做完，还没走到一半就会撞上 dumb zone。"

summary.zh: Spec 描述跨多个 Session 的工作，包括要构建什么、完成标准和任务之间的关系。它可以拆成 Tickets，由不同 Session 分别处理。Spec 负责保持整体目标一致，而不是记录每一步命令。

description.en: A handoff artifact scoping one session of work. Stands alone or hangs off a spec. Can block or be blocked by sibling tickets.
description.zh: 界定单个 Session 工作范围的 handoff artifact，可以独立存在，也可以属于 Spec。

en: A handoff artifact scoping one session of work. Stands alone, or hangs off a spec as one of its children. Tickets can block or be blocked by sibling tickets, so the order of work falls out of their dependency graph rather than a linear plan.

The defining constraint is the size: one session. A ticket should be completable before the session drifts out of the smart zone — and that constraint is testable. If sessions on your tickets routinely degrade before the work is done, the tickets are too big; split them. If each session spends most of its context on setup before doing five minutes of work, they're too small; merge them.

A good ticket is written for a reader with no other context. The goal, the acceptance criteria, and context pointers to the relevant files and decisions — enough that the session can start working without re-deriving what the last one knew.

The dependency graph is also what unlocks parallelism. Independent tickets — the leaves of the graph — can each run in their own session at the same time. This is an effective way of running multiple agents at once. In a software factory, a ticket being marked ready is itself the trigger that starts its session.
Usage:
"Where do I start on the migration spec?"
"Look at the ticket graph — the schema change blocks the backfill, the backfill blocks the API switch. Pick a leaf and run a session on it."
zh: 一个界定单次工作 Session 范围的 Handoff artifact。它既可以独立存在，也可以作为某个 Spec 的子项挂在它之下。Ticket 之间可以互相阻塞，也可以被同级的 Ticket 阻塞，因此工作的顺序由它们的依赖图自然浮现，而不是出自一份线性的计划。

决定性的约束是大小：一个 Session。一个 Ticket 应当能在 Session 漂出 Smart zone 之前完成——而这个约束是可检验的。如果你手上的 Ticket 对应的 Session 经常在任务完成之前就开始退化，那说明 Ticket 太大了，拆开它们。如果每个 Session 把大部分 Context 花在准备工作上，真正干活只有五分钟，那说明 Ticket 太小了，合并它们。
好的 Ticket 是为一位不掌握任何其他 Context 的读者写的。目标、验收标准，以及指向相关文件和决策的 Context 线索——足以让 Session 直接开始工作，而不必重新推导上一个 Session 已经知道的东西。
依赖图也是释放并行能力的关键。相互独立的 Ticket——图中的叶子节点——可以同时各自在属于自己的 Session 中运行。这是同时运行多个 agent 的一种有效方式。在 Software factory 中，一个 Ticket 被标记为就绪，这件事本身就是启动其 Session 的触发器。
用法
"迁移 Spec 该从哪里开始？"
"看看 Ticket 图——schema 变更阻塞 backfill，backfill 又阻塞 API 切换。挑一个叶子节点，在它上面跑一个 Session。"

summary.zh: Ticket 是一个 Session 可独立完成的工作单元，说明任务、边界和验收方式。它可挂在 Spec 下，也可单独存在。好的 Ticket 让接手的 Agent 不必依赖前一个 Session 的隐含记忆。

description.en: A handoff done in-memory: the previous session's history is summarised and seeds a fresh session. Lossy — detail traded for headroom.
description.zh: 在内存中把旧 Session 历史总结后交给新 Session；节省空间，但会丢失细节。

en: A handoff done in-memory: the previous session's history is summarised, and the summary seeds a fresh session. Lossy by design: the transcript is a primary source, the summary a secondary source — detail traded for headroom. Triggered manually by the user, or automatically via autocompact.

The mechanism: the context window is finite, and a long session fills it — every tool result, every file read, every wrong turn stays in history. When it gets heavy, the harness asks the model to summarise the session, throws the original history away, and seeds a fresh session with the summary. Whatever didn't make it into the summary is gone from the context. Some harnesses soften this by keeping the old transcript on disk and leaving a context pointer to it in the summary — the secondary source links back to its primary source, so a detail the summary lost can be recovered by re-reading the original.

The summary is written by the model, so it can be prompted. "Preserve the schema decisions" makes the generated artifact more deliberate. Timing matters too — compact at a phase boundary, after the plan is settled, not mid-task.
Contrast with clearing, which drops everything and starts cold: compaction tries to carry the essentials across; clearing bets they're already written down somewhere better.
Usage:
"Context's getting heavy and I still have the test pass to do."
"Compact before you start — write what must survive into the summary prompt so the new session keeps the schema decisions and drops the exploration."
zh: 在内存中完成的 handoff：上一个 session 的历史被总结成摘要，摘要再作为种子开启一个全新的 session。设计上就是有损的：transcript 是 primary source，摘要则是 secondary source——用细节换取空间余量。可由用户手动触发，也可通过 autocompact 自动触发。

机制是这样的：context window 是有限的，而一个长时间的 session 会把它填满——每一个 tool result、每一次文件读取、每一个走错的 turn，都会留在历史里。当它变得沉重时，harness 会让 model 对 session 做总结，把原始历史丢弃，再用这份摘要作为种子开启一个新的 session。凡是没能进入摘要的内容，都会从 context 中消失。有些 harness 会缓和这一点：把旧的 transcript 保留在磁盘上，并在摘要里留下一个指向它的 context pointer——secondary source 由此链回它的 primary source，于是摘要丢掉的某个细节，可以通过重读原文找回来。
摘要由 model 撰写，因此可以被 prompt 引导。写下 “Preserve the schema decisions” 这样的指令，会让生成的产物更有的放矢。时机也很重要——在阶段边界处 compact，在计划已经确定之后，而不是在任务中途。
对照 clearing——它丢掉一切、从冷启动开始：compaction 试图把要点带过去；clearing 则赌这些要点早已被写在某个更好的地方。
用法
“Context 越来越重了，而我还有测试要跑通。”
“先 compact 再开始——把必须存活下来的内容写进摘要的 prompt 里，这样新的 session 就能保留 schema 决策，丢掉那些探索过程。”

summary.zh: Compaction 把已有 Session 历史总结成较短内容，再作为新 Session 的起点。它释放 Context window 空间，但摘要必然会丢细节。关键事实与决策最好保存在可读取的 Primary source 或 Handoff artifact 中。

description.en: Compaction triggered automatically by the harness when the context window approaches full.
description.zh: 当 context window 接近上限时，Harness 自动触发的 Compaction。

en: Compaction triggered automatically by the harness when the context window approaches full.

The harness watches how full the context window is. When it crosses a threshold — often around 80% — it pauses, asks the model to summarise the session so far, and seeds a fresh session with the summary. Work then continues as if nothing happened.

Except something did happen. Compaction is lossy, and autocompact is lossy at a moment you didn't choose. A manual compact happens at a phase boundary, when you can tell the model what to preserve. Autocompact fires mid-task, whenever the threshold is hit — possibly halfway through a refactor, with the summary deciding for itself which of your decisions were worth keeping. The classic symptom: the agent carries on confidently but has quietly forgotten a constraint you established an hour ago, and you only notice when its work starts contradicting it.

The defence is to not let it fire. Watch the context indicator and compact manually at a natural boundary, or write decisions into a plan doc or handoff artifact on disk, where no summary can lose them. Most harnesses also let you customise the buffer — moving the threshold earlier or later, or turning autocompact off entirely — so you can tune how much headroom you keep before it fires.
Usage:
"It doesn't seem to remember what we decided about the schema earlier."
"Autocompact fired between turns — the early decisions got summarised and we must have lost something. Reload the plan doc, or compact manually next time so you control what gets kept."
zh: 由 Harness 在 Context window 接近占满时自动触发的 Compaction。
Harness 会持续监视 Context window 的占用程度。一旦越过某个阈值——通常在 80% 左右——它就会暂停，让 Model 对到目前为止的 Session 做摘要，再用这份摘要开启一个全新的 Session。之后工作照常继续，仿佛什么都没发生过。

但确实有事发生了。Compaction 是有损的，而 Autocompact 的有损发生在你未曾选择的时刻。手动 compact 发生在阶段边界处，那时你可以告诉 Model 该保留什么。Autocompact 则在任务中途触发，只要触及阈值就触发——可能是在一次重构进行到一半时，由摘要自行裁定你的哪些决策值得保留。典型症状是：Agent 自信地继续干活，却已悄悄忘记了你一小时前确立的某条约束，直到它的产出开始与那条约束相矛盾时你才发现。
防御之道是别让它触发。盯住 Context 指示器，在自然的边界处手动 compact，或者把决策写进计划文档或磁盘上的 Handoff artifact——在那里没有任何摘要能把它们弄丢。大多数 Harness 还允许你自定义缓冲区——把阈值提前或推后，或者干脆完全关闭 Autocompact——这样你就能调节它在触发前为你保留多少余量。
用法
"它好像不记得我们早先对 schema 的决定是什么了。"
"Autocompact 在两轮之间触发了——早期的决定被摘要掉了，我们肯定丢了点东西。重新加载计划文档，或者下次手动 compact，好让你掌控哪些内容会被保留。"

summary.zh: Autocompact 是 Harness 在 Context window 快满时自动触发的 Compaction。它能让对话继续，但摘要的内容选择未必完全符合后续任务。重要状态不宜只留在即将被压缩的聊天历史中。

description.en: A system that attempts to make an agent stateful across sessions by persisting to the environment and reloading at session start.
description.zh: 通过保存环境中的信息，并在新 Session 读取，让 Agent 尝试跨 Session 保持记忆的机制。

en: A system that attempts to make an agent stateful across sessions. Persists information into the environment during a session and reloads it into the context window at the start of future ones, so the agent carries continuity beyond the user clearing the session.

A memory system has two halves. The write path: during a session, the agent records what it learned — a preference you stated, a fact about the project — as files in the environment. The read path: at session start, the harness loads those files, or an index of them, back into the context window. Many harnesses ship their own memory system — Claude Code's /memory is one — but you can also build one yourself: a directory of notes plus an instruction in AGENTS.md to consult it.

The same trade-offs as any always-loaded content apply. Memories accumulate, so most systems load a one-line index and leave the bodies behind context pointers rather than inlining everything. And memories are secondary sources, so they drift: a fact recorded in March is loaded with equal confidence in June, after the project has moved on. A memory system needs pruning, the same way AGENTS.md does.
Usage:
"I keep having to re-tell it I'm on Postgres, not MySQL."
"Wire up a memory system — write what it learns to the filesystem on the first turn, reload it at session start. The model itself is stateless; the memory layer fakes continuity."
zh: 一种试图让 Agent 跨 Session 保持 Stateful 的系统。它在 Session 期间把信息持久化到 Environment 中，并在未来 Session 开始时将其重新载入 Context window，因此即便用户 Clearing 了 Session，Agent 依然保有连续性。

Memory system 分为两半。写入路径：在 Session 期间，Agent 把它学到的东西——你陈述过的某项偏好、关于项目的某个事实——记录为 Environment 中的文件。读取路径：在 Session 开始时，Harness 把这些文件或它们的索引载回 Context window。许多 Harness 都自带 Memory system——Claude Code 的 /memory 就是其中之一——但你也可以自己搭一个：一个笔记目录，外加 AGENTS.md 中一条查阅它的指令。
与任何常驻加载的内容相同的权衡同样适用。记忆会不断累积，因此大多数系统只加载一行式索引，把正文留在 Context 指针之后，而不是把全部内容都内联进来。而且记忆是二手来源，会漂移：三月记录的一条事实，到了六月、项目早已向前推进之后，仍会以同样的置信度被加载。Memory system 需要修剪，就像 AGENTS.md 一样。
用法
“我总得反复告诉它，我用的是 Postgres，不是 MySQL。”
“接一个 Memory system——在第一个 Turn 就把学到的东西写进 Filesystem，在 Session 开始时重新载入。Model 本身是 Stateless 的；记忆层伪造了连续性。”

summary.zh: Memory system 把值得保留的信息写到环境中，并在新 Session 读取，让 Agent 看起来具有跨会话记忆。它改变的是 Context 的来源，不会修改 Model 的 parameters。记忆的有效性取决于保存、检索和更新是否准确。

description.en: A file in the environment that the harness loads into the context window at session start — the project's standing brief to the agent.
description.zh: 环境中的指令文件，Harness 可在 Session 开始时把它加载进 context window。

en: A file in the environment that the harness loads into the context window at session start — the project's standing brief to the agent. Cross-harness convention; some harnesses also have their own variant (Claude Code's is CLAUDE.md).

Because it loads automatically, it's one way to avoid repeating yourself across sessions. The model is stateless — a correction you give in one session is gone in the next, and you end up telling every fresh session that the project uses pnpm, that tests run with a particular flag, that a directory is generated and shouldn't be touched. When you've corrected the agent for the same thing twice, that correction is a candidate line for AGENTS.md.

Suitable content is whatever the agent can't derive from the code: build and test commands, conventions the codebase doesn't make obvious, hard constraints ("never edit the generated client"). Short and declarative — it's a brief, not documentation.

The trade-off is that everything in it is always loaded. Instructions accumulate, most of them irrelevant to any given task, and a long AGENTS.md both costs tokens and dilutes itself — the more instructions in context, the less reliably the model follows any one of them.

Avoid: using AGENTS.md for content that should be progressively disclosed — anything in it pays a token cost every turn, in every session, whether or not that session needs it. A style guide can go behind a skill or a context pointer instead; keep AGENTS.md for the lines that apply everywhere.
Usage:
"Why is every session starting with 4k tokens already burned?"
"Check AGENTS.md — someone pasted the entire style guide in there instead of putting it behind a skill."
zh: 位于 environment 中的一个文件，harness 会在 session 开始时把它加载进 context window——也就是项目交给 agent 的常设简报。这是跨 harness 的惯例；有些 harness 还有自己的变体（Claude Code 的是 CLAUDE.md）。

由于它会自动加载，这是避免在多个 session 之间重复自己的办法之一。model 是 stateless 的——你在一个 session 里给出的纠正，到了下一个 session 就消失了，结果你不得不对每一个新 session 反复交代：项目用 pnpm、测试要用某个特定的 flag 来跑、某个目录是生成的不能碰。当你因为同一件事纠正过 agent 两次，那条纠正就是 AGENTS.md 的候选条目。
合适的内容是 agent 无法从代码中推导出来的东西：构建与测试命令、代码库本身不会让它显而易见的约定、硬性约束（“永远不要编辑生成的 client”）。要简短、用陈述句——它是简报，不是文档。
代价是它里面的所有内容始终处于加载状态。指令会不断累积，而其中大多数与任何具体任务都无关；一份很长的 AGENTS.md 既消耗 token，又会稀释自身——context 里的指令越多，model 可靠遵循其中任何一条的程度就越低。
要避免：把本该逐步披露的内容放进 AGENTS.md——其中的任何内容都要在每一个 session 的每一个 turn 付出 token 成本，无论那个 session 是否需要它。风格指南可以改为放在某个 skill 或 context pointer 后面；把 AGENTS.md 留给那些处处适用的行。
用法
“为什么每个 session 一开始就已经烧掉了 4k token？”
“查一下 AGENTS.md——有人把整份风格指南贴了进去，而不是把它放到 skill 后面。”

summary.zh: AGENTS.md 是可被 Harness 读取的项目指令文件，用来告诉 Agent 仓库约定与工作边界。文件不会自动改变 Model；它需要在适当时机进入 Context。指令越具体、越贴近实际代码，越容易执行。

description.en: Loading only the context an agent needs right now, with context pointers to the rest. Borrowed from UI design.
description.zh: 先加载当前需要的上下文，再用 context pointers 按需获取更多内容。

en: Loading only the context an agent needs right now, with context pointers to the rest. Borrowed from UI design, where it means showing users only the controls relevant to their current task and hiding the rest behind a click.

The technique exists because context is a cost twice over. Every token loaded up front is billed as input tokens on every turn, and every token spends attention budget whether the agent needs it or not. An AGENTS.md stuffed with the full style guide, deployment runbook, and database conventions makes the agent worse at all of them — the instructions that matter for the current task are diluted by the ones that don't. The tell is an agent that ignores rules you know are in its context: they're in there, but buried.

Progressive disclosure inverts this. Keep the always-loaded layer small — a sentence per topic and a pointer to where the detail lives. The agent reads the style guide when it's writing a component, the deployment runbook when it's deploying, and neither when it's fixing a test. Skills are the pattern built into the harness: a short description loaded every session, the full instructions only when triggered.
Usage:
"Should I dump the entire style guide into AGENTS.md?"
"No — progressive disclosure. Reference the style guide as a skill the agent loads when it actually needs to write a component. AGENTS.md pays the token cost every turn."
zh: 只加载 Agent 当下需要的 Context，其余部分用 Context 指针指向。这一做法借自 UI 设计，在那里它指的是：只向用户展示与当前任务相关的控件，其余的都藏在一次点击之后。

这项技术之所以存在，是因为 Context 是一份双重成本。预先加载的每一个 Token，都会在每一个 Turn 按 Input tokens 计费，而且无论 Agent 是否需要，每一个 Token 都在消耗 Attention budget。一个塞满了完整风格指南、部署运行手册和数据库规范的 AGENTS.md，会让 Agent 在所有这些方面都表现更差——当前任务真正重要的指令，被那些无关的指令稀释了。破绽就是：Agent 忽略了你明知就在它 Context 里的规则——它们确实在里面，只是被埋住了。
Progressive disclosure 把这一关系倒转过来。让常驻加载的那一层保持很小——每个主题一句话，外加一个指向细节所在位置的指针。Agent 在写组件时才去读风格指南，在部署时才去读部署运行手册，而在修测试时两者都不读。Skill 就是内建于 Harness 的这一模式：每个 Session 加载一段简短描述，完整指令只在被触发时才加载。
用法
"我该把整份风格指南都倒进 AGENTS.md 吗？"
"不——用 Progressive disclosure。把风格指南作为一个 Skill 引用，让 Agent 在真正需要写组件时才加载它。AGENTS.md 是每个 Turn 都要付出 Token 成本的。"

summary.zh: Progressive disclosure 先提供当前步骤必要的信息，更多细节通过 Context pointers 在需要时读取。这样可以节约 Context window，并减少无关内容对注意力的竞争。它不是隐藏信息，而是安排加载顺序。

description.en: A mention in one document that points to another, so the agent can pull it into context only when the task calls for it.
description.zh: 文档中指向其他信息的引用，让 Agent 在需要时再加载对应内容。

en: A mention in one document that points to another, so the agent can pull it into the context window only when the task calls for it. The unit progressive disclosure is built from.

The reason to use a pointer (instead of inlining the content) is cost. A pointer is one line in the context window. The document behind it might be thousands of tokens, but those tokens cost nothing until the agent actually follows the pointer. Inline a 2,000-token runbook in AGENTS.md and every session pays for it; replace it with "deploy process: see internal/deploy.md" and only the sessions that deploy ever load it. The agent follows the pointer with a tool call when the task matches.

A pointer needs two parts to work: a stable path, and enough description for the agent to know when following it is worth it. A bare path is a pointer the agent has no reason to follow; "see internal/deploy.md" with no hint of what's inside gets skipped by a session that needed it. Write the line so it matches how tasks present: "release, deploy, or rollback — read internal/deploy.md first".

Pointers are everywhere once you look: lines in AGENTS.md, skill descriptions (the harness loads the description; the skill body waits behind it), filenames in a directory listing, links between docs.

A pointer can also tie a secondary source back to the primary source it was derived from — the compaction summary that names the original transcript, the doc that names the source file it describes. This makes the secondary source's lossiness recoverable: when the summary turns out not to be enough, the agent follows the pointer and reads the original, instead of working from whatever the summary kept.
