Avoid: "reference" — too dry; doesn't convey that following it pulls more context in. "Portal" — too florid.
Usage:
"AGENTS.md is getting huge."
"Most of it should be context pointers, not content. Keep the always-on rules inline; turn the deploy runbook and the style guide into skills and leave a context pointer behind."
zh: 一个文档中对另一个文档的提及，指向后者，使 Agent 只在任务需要时才把它拉进 Context window。它正是 Progressive disclosure 得以构建的基本单元。

使用指针（而不是把内容内联进来）的理由是成本。一个 Context pointer 在 Context window 里只占一行。它背后的文档可能有数千个 Token，但除非 Agent 真的顺着这个指针去读，这些 Token 不花任何代价。把一份 2,000 Token 的运行手册内联进 AGENTS.md，每个 Session 都要为它付费；把它换成「deploy process: see internal/deploy.md」，就只有真正要部署的那些 Session 才会加载它。当任务匹配时，Agent 会用一次 Tool call 顺着这个指针去读。

一个 Context pointer 要起作用需要两部分：一个稳定的路径，以及足够让 Agent 判断何时值得顺着它读下去的描述。光秃秃的路径就是 Agent 没有理由追随的指针；没有任何内容提示的「see internal/deploy.md」，会被真正需要它的 Session 跳过。写这一行时要让它匹配任务出现的方式：「release, deploy, or rollback — read internal/deploy.md first」。
留心观察，指针无处不在：AGENTS.md 里的行、Skill 描述（Harness 会加载描述；Skill 正文在描述后面等待）、目录列表里的文件名、文档之间的链接。
指针还能把一个 Secondary source 拴回它所派生自的 Primary source——那份指名原始 transcript 的 Compaction 摘要、那份指名自己所描述源文件的文档。这让 Secondary source 的有损性变得可恢复：当摘要被证明不够用时，Agent 顺着指针去读原文，而不是将就于摘要所保留下来的内容。
避免：「reference」——太干瘪；传达不出顺着它读会把更多 Context 拉进来这层意思。「Portal」——太花哨。
用法
「AGENTS.md 越来越大了。」
「它的大部分应该是 Context pointer，而不是内容。把常驻规则保留为内联；把部署运行手册和风格指南变成 Skill，在原处留下一个 Context pointer。」

summary.zh: Context pointer 是文档里指向另一份资料的明确线索。Agent 不必一开始加载所有文件，只需在任务触及相应问题时沿指针读取。好的指针能说明何时、为何要打开目标内容。

description.en: A teachable capability bundled as a unit — kept out of the context window until a context pointer pulls it in for the task at hand.
description.zh: 按需加载的一组可复用 Agent 能力与操作说明。

en: A teachable capability bundled as a unit — instructions and resources for doing one task well, kept in the environment until a context pointer pulls it into the context window for the task at hand. The unit of progressive disclosure in a harness.

Skills are an open standard, defined at agentskills.io — originally developed by Anthropic and since adopted by most major harnesses, so a skill written once works across them. The format is a folder containing:

- A SKILL.md file — metadata (a name and description, at minimum) plus the instructions themselves
- Optionally, scripts the agent can run
- Optionally, templates and reference material the instructions point to

Only the name and description sit in context by default. When the agent's task matches, it loads the rest. Until then, the skill takes up almost no room — a sentence or two of tokens, however large its full instructions are.

This distinguishes skills from AGENTS.md, which is loaded into every session regardless of the task. A skill is read when a particular kind of work comes up — releasing, scaffolding a new service, writing a migration — and ignored the rest of the time.
Avoid: "tool" — a tool is what the agent calls; a skill is instructions it reads.
Usage:
"Where should I put the deploy runbook?"
"As a skill — the agent loads it only when the task involves deploys. In AGENTS.md it'd burn tokens on every turn for something we use weekly."
zh: 一种以单元形式打包的可教学能力——为做好某一项任务所需的指令与资源；它留在 Environment 中，直到某个 Context pointer 把它拉进 Context window，服务于手头的任务。它是 Harness 中 Progressive disclosure 的单位。
Skill 是一个开放标准，定义于 agentskills.io——最初由 Anthropic 开发，此后被大多数主流 Harness 采用，所以一份写好的 Skill 在各家之间都能通用。其格式是一个文件夹，包含：

- 一个 SKILL.md 文件——元数据（至少包含名称和描述）加上指令本身
- 可选：Agent 可以运行的脚本
- 可选：指令所指向的模板与参考资料
默认情况下，只有名称和描述留在 Context 里。当 Agent 的任务与之匹配时，它才加载其余内容。在此之前，这份 Skill 几乎不占空间——无论完整指令有多大，也只占一两句话的 token。
这正是 Skill 与 AGENTS.md 的区别：后者无论任务是什么都会被加载进每个 Session。而 Skill 只在某类特定工作出现时才被读取——发版、搭建新服务、写数据库迁移——其余时间便被忽略。
避免："tool"——Tool 是 Agent 调用的东西；Skill 是它读取的指令。
用法
"部署 runbook 应该放在哪里？"
"作为 Skill——Agent 只在任务涉及部署时才加载它。放在 AGENTS.md 里，它会为一件每周才用一次的事烧掉每一个 Turn 的 token。"

summary.zh: Skill 把某类工作的方法、约束和资源打包成可按需加载的能力。平时只保留简短说明，需要时才读完整内容，以免长期占用 Context window。Skill 提供流程，不会替代实际工具和验证。

description.en: An agent spawned by another agent via a tool call. Runs in its own session, reports a single tool result. Cannot spawn further subagents.
description.zh: 由另一个 Agent 启动、在独立 Session 中工作并返回结果的 Agent。

en: An agent spawned by another agent via a tool call. Runs in its own session with its own context window, and reports a single tool result back. Distinct from a handoff — the parent specifically expects a return; a handoff has no return path. Cannot spawn further subagents — the tree is one level deep. Subagents exist to isolate context, not to compose hierarchies.

The point is to keep noisy work out of the parent's context. A broad search or a long file-reading expedition produces pages of tool results, most of which matter only long enough to find the answer. Run inside the parent and all of it stays in the parent's context for the rest of the session. Run inside a subagent and the noise fills a disposable window instead — only the final report lands in the parent's context. The report is a secondary source: the parent gets the subagent's account of what it found, not the raw results, so anything the report leaves out is invisible to the parent.
Subagents also run concurrently — a parent can fan several out at once over independent pieces of work.
Usage:
"The grep results are blowing out my context."
"Spawn a subagent to do the search — it'll burn its own context window on the noise and report back the two file paths you actually need."
zh: 由另一个 Agent 通过 Tool call 派生的 Agent。它运行在自己的 Session 中，拥有自己的 Context window，最后回传单个 Tool result。它与 Handoff 不同——父级明确期待一个返回，而 Handoff 没有返回路径。它不能再派生更下一级的 Subagent——这棵树只有一层深。Subagent 的存在是为了隔离 Context，而不是用来构建层级结构。

关键在于把嘈杂的工作挡在父级 Context 之外。一次大范围搜索或一场漫长的读文件远征，会产生成页的 Tool result，其中大部分只在找到答案的那一刻有意义。在父级内部运行，这些东西会在本次 Session 余下的时间里一直留在父级 Context 中；在 Subagent 内部运行，噪声填满的则是一个用完即弃的窗口——只有最终报告会落进父级 Context。报告是 Secondary source：父级拿到的是 Subagent 对自己所找到内容的叙述，而不是原始结果，因此报告中没有写出来的任何东西，对父级而言都是不可见的。
Subagent 还可以并发运行——父级可以一次性把若干个 Subagent 铺开到彼此独立的工作上。
用法
"grep 的结果快把我的 Context 撑爆了。"
"派生一个 Subagent 去做这次搜索——它会用自己的 Context window 去消化这些噪声，然后把你真正需要的那两个文件路径报回来。"

summary.zh: Subagent 由另一个 Agent 启动，在独立 Session 中处理有边界的子任务，再把结果返回。它拥有自己的 Context，适合可并行、可清晰交付的工作。主 Agent 仍需核对结果并把它纳入整体任务。

description.en: A working pattern where one or more humans pair with the agent during a session — reviewing, redirecting, or collaborating in real time.
description.zh: 人持续参与 Agent 工作过程，查看进展、给出判断或纠正方向。

en: A working pattern where one or more humans pair with the agent during a session — reviewing, redirecting, or collaborating in real time. The human is present and engaged, not just gating individual actions.

The contrast is with AFK work, where the agent runs unattended and you judge the result afterwards. Human-in-the-loop means catching problems while they're still cheap: you see the agent reach for the wrong file, misread the requirement, or start down a dead end, and you redirect it in one sentence — rather than discovering twenty minutes of confident work built on that mistake. Agents don't reliably know when they're off track; left alone, they tend to push forward rather than stop and ask.

Which pattern fits depends on the work. Well-specified, low-risk, easy-to-verify tasks suit AFK. Tasks that are ambiguous, irreversible, or where you'd struggle to review the finished result — a schema migration, a tricky design decision, anything touching production — suit staying in the loop. The judgement call is essentially: how expensive is a wrong turn, and how late would you catch it?
Some work is in-the-loop by nature, because your reactions are the input. Grilling only works with you there to answer the questions; prototyping only works with you there to react to the artifact.

Staying in the loop costs your attention, which is the scarce resource. Part of getting better with agents is moving more work safely out of the loop — with plans, automated checks, and human review at the end instead of supervision throughout. A software factory takes this further by starting sessions from triggers, so even kicking off the work doesn't need you.
Usage:
"Run this AFK overnight?"
"No, schema migration — keep it human-in-the-loop. I want to see each step and steer if it picks the wrong column to backfill from."
zh: 一种工作模式：在一次 Session 中，一个或多个人与 Agent 结对——实时审查、纠偏或协作。人类全程在场并真正投入，而不只是对单个动作做放行把关。
与之相对的是 AFK 工作：Agent 无人看管地运行，你在事后评判结果。Human-in-the-loop 意味着趁问题还便宜时就抓住它：你看到 Agent 去拿错文件、误读需求，或者开始走进死胡同，然后一句话把它拨回来——而不是在二十分钟之后才发现，这二十分钟自信满满的工作全都建立在那次错误之上。Agent 并不能可靠地察觉自己何时跑偏；没人管的时候，它们倾向于继续往前推，而不是停下来发问。
哪种模式合适取决于工作本身。规格明确、低风险、易于验证的任务适合 AFK。而含糊不清、不可逆，或者你难以审查最终结果的任务——一次 schema migration、一个棘手的设计决策、任何触及生产环境的事——则适合留在 loop 中。这个判断本质上就是：走错一步的代价有多大，而你会多晚才发现？
有些工作天生就是 in-the-loop 的，因为你的反应本身就是输入。Grilling 只有在你在场回答问题时才成立；Prototyping 只有在你在场对产物做出反应时才成立。
留在 loop 中要付出你的注意力，而注意力正是稀缺资源。与 Agent 配合得越来越好的其中一部分，就是把更多工作安全地移出 loop——靠计划、自动化检查，以及在最后做 Human review，而不是全程监督。Software factory 把这一点推得更远：由触发器启动 session，于是连启动工作本身都不需要你。
用法
“这个跑 AFK 过一夜？”
“不行，schema migration——保持 human-in-the-loop。我想看到每一步，如果它选错了要回填的列，我好及时纠偏。”

summary.zh: Human-in-the-loop 指人参与 Agent 的工作过程，在关键步骤提供判断、纠错或批准。人与 Agent 之间存在实时往返，适合需要解释意图、审查风险或做取舍的工作。

description.en: A working pattern where the user kicks off a session and leaves the agent to run unattended (away from keyboard).
description.zh: 用户启动 Agent 后暂时离开、不实时看管的工作模式，即 away from keyboard。

en: Away from keyboard. A working pattern where the user kicks off a session and leaves the agent to run unattended. The throughput multiplier of AI coding — many AFK sessions can run in parallel while you sleep, eat, or work on something else. Usually requires a permissive permission mode plus sandboxing to be safe.

When you're not there, the agent handles ambiguity differently. While you're watching, an ambiguous decision surfaces as a question and you answer it; once you've walked away, the agent picks a default and keeps going, and every later decision builds on that guess. The characteristic failure is coming back to hours of finished, confident work built on a wrong call made in the first ten minutes. The work isn't sloppy — it's coherent, just coherent about the wrong thing.

Since you can't give input during the run, give it before and after instead. Before: resolve the ambiguity up front — a grilling session, a written spec — so there are fewer gaps for the agent to fill alone. During: automated checks and automated review stand in for the attention you're not giving, failing fast on what can be caught mechanically. After: the run ends in something reviewable — a PR, not changes already merged. AFK doesn't remove human review; it defers all of it to the end, which is why what arrives at the end has to be worth reviewing. This is also why AX matters most in AFK runs — with no one watching, the environment is the only support the agent gets.
Avoid: "background agent" — centers the machine ("running in the background") rather than the human pattern ("user has walked away"). AFK names the fact that matters: the user isn't watching.
Usage:
"I'm running this AFK — three sandboxed agents on the refactor, reviewing the PRs in the morning."
"Bypass permissions?"
"Yeah, read-only filesystem, no network."
zh: Away from keyboard（离开键盘）。一种工作模式：用户启动一个 session 之后就离开，让 agent 无人值守地运行。这是 AI coding 的吞吐量倍增器 —— 你睡觉、吃饭或忙别的事情时，多个 AFK session 可以并行运行。通常需要一个宽松的 permission mode，再加上沙箱化，才谈得上安全。
当你不在场时，agent 处理歧义的方式不一样。你在旁边看着的时候，含糊的决定会以提问的形式浮现出来，由你回答；一旦你走开，agent 会自己挑一个默认做法继续往下做，之后每一个决定都建立在这个猜测之上。典型的失败情形是：你回来时看到数小时完成的、自信满满的工作，而它建立在前十分钟做出的一个错误判断之上。这些工作并不潦草 —— 它连贯自洽，只是自洽在错误的那件事上。

既然你无法在运行过程中给输入，那就改在运行前和运行后给。运行前：提前消解歧义 —— 一场 grilling session、一份写下来的 spec —— 这样留给 agent 独自填补的空隙就更少。运行中：automated checks 和 automated review 代替你没能给到的注意力，对机械手段能抓住的问题快速失败。运行后：运行结束时留下可审查的东西 —— 一个 PR，而不是已经合并的改动。AFK 并不会取消 human review，它只是把全部评审都推迟到最后，这正是为什么最后送达的东西必须值得一评。这也是为什么 AX 在 AFK 运行中最要紧 —— 无人看管时，environment 是 agent 唯一能得到的支撑。
避免使用：“background agent” —— 它把重心放在机器上（“在后台运行”），而不是人的行为模式（“用户已经走开”）。AFK 命名的才是真正要紧的事实：用户没有在看。
用法
“我在 AFK 跑这件事 —— 三个沙箱化的 agent 做重构，早上再来 review 这些 PR。”
“绕过权限？”
“对，只读 filesystem，无网络。”

summary.zh: AFK 是 away from keyboard：用户发起任务后暂时不看管，让 Agent 自行推进。它能提高吞吐量，也会放大一开始的错误假设。离开前要写清任务和边界，运行中靠自动检查，回来后做 Human review。

description.en: A deterministic verification that runs in the environment — tests, type checks, lints, build, pre-commit hooks. Pass/fail, no judgement.
description.zh: 在环境中运行的确定性检查，例如测试、类型检查或 lint，结果通常是通过或失败。

en: A deterministic verification that runs in the environment — tests, type checks, lints, build, pre-commit hooks. Pass/fail, no judgement. The signal an agent can self-correct from without involving anyone else. A flaky test is a broken check, not a non-check; automated checks are deterministic by design.

Self-correction works as a loop. The agent makes a change, runs the check as a tool call, and the failure output lands in its context window — a type error with a file and line, a failing assertion with expected and actual values. That's enough for the agent to fix the problem and run the check again, around and around until it passes, with no human in the loop. Determinism is what makes the loop trustworthy: the same code always produces the same verdict, so a pass means something. A flaky check poisons this — the agent "fixes" code that was fine, or retries past a real failure.

This is why good checks are a large part of a codebase's AX. An agent in a repo with strict types, a fast test suite, and a linter catches most of its own mistakes before you see them; an agent in a repo with none of those ships whatever it produces. The difference matters most in AFK runs, where checks are the only verification happening during the run. But a check only catches what it asserts — green checks mean the asserted properties hold, not that the code is right. The judgement-shaped gaps are what automated review and human review are for.
Avoid: "feedback loop" / "backpressure" — both lump checks together with review. Avoid: "test" — tests are automated checks, but not all automated checks are tests.
Usage:
"The agent keeps shipping broken code in the AFK runs."
"What automated checks are wired into the sandbox?"
"Just the unit tests."
"Add typecheck and lint — it'll self-correct from those before the PR ever lands."
zh: 一种在 Environment 中运行的确定性验证——测试、类型检查、lint、构建、pre-commit hooks。只有通过/失败，不做评判。这是 Agent 无需牵扯任何其他人就能据以自我纠正的信号。flaky test 是坏掉的 check，而不是“非 check”；automated checks 在设计上就是确定性的。

自我纠正是以循环的方式运转的。Agent 做出改动，把 check 作为一次 Tool call 运行，失败的输出就落进它的 Context window——带文件名和行号的类型错误、带期望值与实际值的失败断言。这足以让 Agent 修好问题、再次运行 check，如此反复直到通过，循环中没有任何人参与。确定性正是让这个循环值得信赖的原因：同一份代码永远产生同一个判定，所以“通过”才有意义。flaky check 会毒化这一切——Agent 会去“修”本来没问题的代码，或者反复重试从而越过一个真实的失败。

这就是为什么好的 check 是一个代码库 AX 的重要组成部分。在一个拥有严格类型、快速测试套件和 linter 的代码仓库里，Agent 能在你看见之前抓住自己的大部分错误；而在这些都没有的代码仓库里，Agent 产出什么就交付什么。这一差别在 AFK 运行中体现得最明显，因为那里 check 是运行期间唯一发生的验证。但 check 只能抓住它所断言的东西——绿色的 check 意味着被断言的性质成立，而不是代码正确。那些需要判断力来填补的空缺，正是 Automated review 和 Human review 的用武之地。
避免使用：“feedback loop” / “backpressure”——这两个词都把 check 与 review 混为一谈。避免使用：“test”——test 属于 automated checks，但并非所有 automated checks 都是 test。
用法
“Agent 在 AFK 运行中不断交付坏掉的代码。”
“Sandbox 里接入了哪些 automated checks？”
“只有单元测试。”
“加上 typecheck 和 lint——它会在 PR 落地之前就靠这些自我纠正。”

summary.zh: Automated check 是可重复运行、结果明确的机械检查，例如类型检查、测试和 lint。它能快速发现某些错误，但不能评价产品判断或代码意图。Agent 离线工作时，这些检查尤其重要。

description.en: An agent reviewing another agent's work, often with a different model or system prompt. Non-deterministic: it forms a judgement.
description.zh: 由 Agent 对另一 Agent 的工作作出判断的审查，结果不是完全确定的。

en: An agent reviewing another agent's work, often with a different model or system prompt. Non-deterministic: it forms a judgement. Runs anywhere — pre-merge on a PR, post-hoc on commit history, mid-session as a subagent. An LLM-as-judge in CI is automated review, not an automated check; what the assertion does decides the category, not where it runs.

The separation from the working agent is what makes it work. Asking the agent that wrote the code to review its own work gets you very little — the session that produced the bug also contains the reasoning that produced it, and the agent reads its own conclusions back as confirmation. A reviewer with a fresh context window has none of that attachment: it sees the diff the way a stranger would, which is what review depends on. A different model or a review-specific system prompt sharpens this further — different blind spots, and a system prompt scoped to what you actually care about (security, API contracts, performance) rather than a vague "look for problems".

It slots between the other review layers. Automated checks are deterministic and catch what can be asserted mechanically; human review is expensive and scales worst. Automated review sits in the middle: it catches judgement-shaped problems — a misleading function name, a missed edge case — at machine cost. Because it's non-deterministic, it can miss things and flag non-issues; treat it as a filter that raises the floor before a human looks, not a gate that replaces one.
Avoid: "AI review" / "agent review" — too vague to distinguish from the working agent itself.
Usage:
"We're getting too many bad PRs from the AFK runs."
"Add an automated review step before merge — different model, separate system prompt, scoped to security and contract changes."
zh: Agent 审查另一个 Agent 的工作，通常使用不同的 Model 或 System prompt。非确定性：它做出的是判断。它可以在任何地方运行——合并前在 PR 上、事后在 commit history 上、在 Session 中途作为 Subagent。CI 中的 LLM-as-judge 属于 Automated review，而不是 Automated check；决定类别的是断言做了什么，而不是它在哪里运行。

与工作 Agent 的分离，正是它奏效的原因。让写代码的那个 Agent 审查自己的工作收获甚微——产生 bug 的 Session 里同样含有产生它的推理过程，而 Agent 会把自己的结论当作确认读回去。拥有全新 Context window 的审查者没有这种依附：它像一个陌生人那样看 diff，而这正是 review 所依赖的。不同的 Model，或针对审查定制的 System prompt，会进一步强化这一点——不同的盲区，以及一个聚焦于你真正关心之处（security、API contracts、performance）的 System prompt，而不是笼统的「找找问题」。

它嵌在其他 review 层之间。Automated check 是确定性的，能抓住可以被机械断言的东西；Human review 昂贵，且扩展性最差。Automated review 居于中间：它以机器的成本抓住判断形态的问题——一个误导性的函数名、一个被漏掉的边界情况。因为它是非确定性的，它可能漏掉东西，也可能把不是问题的问题标出来；把它当作一个在人看之前抬高下限的过滤器，而不是一个取代人的关卡。
避免：「AI review」/「Agent review」——过于模糊，无法与工作 Agent 本身区分。
用法
「AFK 运行带来的糟糕 PR 太多了。」
「在合并前加一个 Automated review 步骤——不同的 Model、独立的 System prompt，聚焦于 security 和 contract 变更。」

summary.zh: Automated review 由另一个 Agent 阅读变更并提出判断。它与测试不同，结论不是确定性的，也可能遗漏问题。它可帮助发现结构和逻辑风险，但不能替代 Human review。

description.en: The user reading the code the agent produced and forming a judgement on it. Reading the diff counts; reading the summary doesn't.
description.zh: 人亲自阅读代码或变更并形成判断；仅阅读摘要不算完成代码审查。

en: The user reading the code the agent produced and forming a judgement on it. Reading the diff or the changed files counts; reading the agent's description of what it did does not — narration is not the artifact. The description is a secondary source, written by the party being reviewed; the diff is the primary source, and review means reading it.

Agents raise the volume of code produced, so review becomes the bottleneck. One useful idea is layering different review strategies. Automated checks catch the mechanical failures, automated review catches the describable ones, and human review is reserved for what only you can judge — whether the change is the right change, whether the approach fits the codebase, whether this should exist at all.

Review is also cheaper earlier. Reading a plan before work starts, or a small diff mid-flight, takes minutes; excavating a finished branch after an AFK run takes longer. Where you place the review checkpoint is a human-in-the-loop decision, not an afterthought.
Avoid: "code review" alone — ambiguous between human and automated.
Usage:
"I human-reviewed the AFK output."
"You read the diff or just the summary?"
"Diff. The summary said it deleted dead code — turned out the function was called from a generated file."
zh: 用户阅读 Agent 产出的代码并对其作出判断。读 diff 或改动过的文件算数；读 Agent 对自己做了什么的描述不算——叙述不是产物本身。描述是 Secondary source，由被审查的一方写成；diff 是 Primary source，而审查就意味着去读它。
Agent 提高了代码的产出量，于是审查变成了瓶颈。一个有用的思路是把不同的审查策略分层。Automated checks 抓机械性的失败，Automated review 抓可描述的失败，Human review 则留给只有你能判断的部分——这个改动是不是对的改动、这个做法是否契合代码库、这东西到底该不该存在。
审查也是越早越便宜。开工前读一份计划，或在过程中读一份小 diff，只需几分钟；而在一次 AFK 运行之后去挖一条已完成的分支，则要花更久。把审查检查点放在哪里，是一个 Human-in-the-loop 的决定，而不是事后才想起的补充。
避免：只说「code review」——它在人工审查和自动审查之间有歧义。
用法
「我对 AFK 的产出做了 Human review。」
「你读的是 diff，还是只看了摘要？」
「diff。摘要说它删掉了死代码——结果那个函数是被一个生成文件调用的。」

summary.zh: Human review 是人亲自查看代码、变更或产物并形成判断。阅读摘要并不能代替阅读实际差异。它提供责任和上下文判断，尤其适合决定是否接受 Agent 自动完成的工作。

description.en: A working pattern where the user accepts the agent's code without human review. The diff is treated as opaque.
description.zh: 不亲自审查代码细节，直接接受 Agent 产出的工作方式。

en: A working pattern where the user accepts the agent's code without human review. The diff is treated as opaque — what matters is whether the program behaves, not what's inside. Automated review and automated checks may still run; vibe coding is silent on both.

The term comes from Andrej Karpathy, who coined it in early 2025: you "fully give in to the vibes" and "forget that the code even exists" — describe what you want, accept what comes back, and judge it by running it.

Vibe coding trades inspection for speed. Reading diffs is usually the slowest step in agent-driven work, so dropping it removes the main bottleneck. For code whose failures are cheap — prototypes, one-off scripts, internal tools — that's a reasonable trade. The risk scales with the code's lifespan and stakes.

The cost arrives later. Vibe-coded changes accumulate into a codebase nobody has read, and behaviour was the only thing checked — so anything behaviour doesn't surface, like a secret written to logs, a missing edge case, or quietly wrong data handling, ships unseen. The first time someone debugs the system is the first time anyone reads the code. With human review gone, whatever automated verification still runs — tests, types, automated review — is the only gate the code passes through. The same stance applied to a whole codebase, or part of one, whose changes come from a software factory is a dark factory.
Avoid: "vibe coding" as a synonym for "low-quality AI coding" — the term names the review stance, not the resulting code.
Usage:
"Did you read what it changed in the auth flow?"
"Vibe coded it — login still works, that's all I checked."
"Read the diff before you push, vibing on auth is how secrets leak into logs."
zh: 一种工作模式：用户直接接受 Agent 写出的代码，不做 Human review。diff 被视为不透明的——重要的是程序的行为，而不是里面写了什么。Automated review 与自动化检查仍可照常运行；Vibe coding 对这两者不置一词。
这个词出自 Andrej Karpathy，他在 2025 年初创造了它：你“完全交给 vibe 主导”，“忘记代码的存在”——描述你想要什么，接受返回的东西，靠运行它来判断。
Vibe coding 用检查换取速度。阅读 diff 通常是 Agent 驱动工作中最慢的一步，因此跳过它就去掉了主要瓶颈。对于失败代价低廉的代码——原型、一次性脚本、内部工具——这是一笔合理的交易。风险随代码的生命周期和利害大小而放大。

代价在之后才到来。以 Vibe coding 方式写出的改动堆积成一个没人读过的代码库，而唯一被检查过的只有行为——因此凡是行为暴露不出来的东西，比如被写进日志的密钥、缺失的边界情况，或者悄无声息出错的数据处理，都会在无人过目的情况下发布出去。第一次有人调试这个系统之时，就是第一次有人读这些代码之日。随着 Human review 的缺席，仍在运行的任何自动化验证——测试、类型检查、Automated review——就是代码唯一要过的关口。把同样的立场用在由 Software factory 产出改动的整个代码库、或者其中一部分上，那就是 Dark factory。
避免：把“vibe coding”当作“低质量 AI coding”的同义词——这个词命名的是评审立场，而不是由此产生的代码。
用法
“你读过它在认证流程里改了什么吗？”
“用 vibe coding 写的——登录还能用，我检查的就这些。”
“推送前先读 diff，在认证上 vibe coding，密钥就是这样泄漏进日志的。”

summary.zh: Vibe coding 指开发者不审查代码细节，只根据表面效果接受 Agent 的产出。它可以快速探索，但在维护、正确性和安全边界上留下盲点。这个词描述的是审查方式，而不是使用 AI 写代码本身。

description.en: The shared understanding of what's being built, held in common between user and agent but separate from any asset.
description.zh: 人和 Agent 对要做什么形成的共同理解，独立于具体设计稿或资产。

en: The shared understanding of what's being built, held in common between user and agent but separate from any asset. Brooks' term (The Design of Design): the conversation, handoff artifacts, and the code are all assets that try to capture or reach the design concept, but none of them are it. Quality of the design concept is felt through the quality of the conversation that built it.

The term names the gap behind a familiar frustration: the agent writes exactly what you asked for and it's still wrong. The usual cause is that you hadn't fully figured out what you wanted. The design concept wasn't finished in your own head — your prompt captured the parts you'd worked out, and was silent on the parts you hadn't. The agent filled those silences with its own assumptions, because there was nothing to align with. Nothing malfunctioned. There was no shared design concept, because there wasn't yet a whole one to share.

You can tell a design concept is shared the same way you can with a colleague: the other party starts answering questions you haven't asked yet the way you would. Until then, the work is conversation — grilling is the deliberate version — and writing a spec too early just captures the misalignment in a more durable asset. The design concept also moves as you learn; assets lag it, which is why a spec faithful to last week's understanding can still mislead this week's session.
Usage:
"It's writing exactly what I asked for and it's still wrong."
"You don't share a design concept yet — it's filling gaps with assumptions. Keep talking until cancellation, refunds, and partial fulfilment all line up between you before you let it write a spec."
zh: 关于正在构建之物所达成的共同理解，由用户与 Agent 共同持有，但又与任何资产相分离。这是 Brooks 的术语（《The Design of Design》）：对话、Handoff 产物和代码全都是资产，它们试图捕捉或抵达 design concept，但没有一个是它本身。design concept 的质量，要通过构建它的那场对话的质量去感受。

这个词命名了一种熟悉的挫败感背后的缺口：Agent 完全按你要求的那样写了出来，结果却依然是错的。通常的原因是，你还没有真正想清楚自己想要什么。design concept 在你自己的脑子里尚未完成——你的 prompt 捕捉到了你已经想明白的部分，而对还没想明白的部分保持沉默。Agent 用自己的假设填补了这些沉默之处，因为没有任何东西可供对齐。没有任何环节出故障。当时并不存在共享的 design concept，因为还没有一个完整的 design concept 可供共享。

判断 design concept 是否已经共享，方法和你判断一位同事是否与你同步一样：对方开始用你会用的方式，回答你还没有问出口的问题。在那一刻到来之前，工作就是对话——Grilling 是其中刻意为之的那一版——而过早写 Spec，只会把这种错位固化进一件更耐久的资产里。design concept 也会随着你的学习而移动；资产滞后于它，这正是为什么一份忠实于上周理解的 Spec，仍可能误导本周的 Session。
用法
“它完全按我要求的写了，结果还是错的。”
“你们还没有共享同一个 design concept——它在用假设填补空白。继续谈下去，直到取消、退款和部分履约这几件事在你们之间全部对齐，再让它去写 Spec。”

summary.zh: Design concept 是团队对“正在做什么、为什么这样做”的共同理解，独立于最终代码和设计稿。先对概念达成一致，后续实现才有判断依据；否则每个人可能都在完整执行不同的想法。

description.en: A technique for developing a design concept: the agent interviews the user Socratically, one decision at a time.
description.zh: 通过连续追问来检验和澄清设计概念，一次聚焦一个决策。

en: A technique for developing a design concept with an agent: the agent interviews the user Socratically, one decision at a time, proposing a recommended answer for each. Slows the rush to a finished plan — no handoff artifact is written until the concept stabilises.

The technique exists because agents fill gaps silently. Asked to write a spec from a two-line prompt, the agent doesn't stop at the decisions you haven't made — it picks defaults and writes them in. The result looks complete, and the guesses are indistinguishable from the choices, so you discover them late: at review, or when the built feature handles an edge case in a way you never chose. Grilling inverts this — instead of guessing, the agent has to ask.
It's a human-in-the-loop technique: your answers are the input. When a question can't be answered in conversation — you'd have to see the thing — switch to prototyping.
Usage:
"It went straight to writing the spec and got the cancellation logic wrong."
"Grill it first — make it ask you about partial cancels, refunds, and timing before it commits anything to the doc. Cheaper to resolve in conversation than in code."
zh: 一种与 Agent 一起发展 Design concept 的技术：Agent 以苏格拉底式提问的方式访谈用户，每次只处理一个决策，并为每个决策给出推荐答案。它减缓了急于产出最终方案的速度——在概念稳定下来之前，不会写出任何 Handoff artifact。
这项技术之所以存在，是因为 Agent 会静默地填补空白。当被要求根据两行提示写出 Spec 时，Agent 不会在你尚未做出的决策处停下——它会自行挑选默认值并写进去。结果看起来完整无缺，而那些猜测与真正的选择难以区分，于是你发现得太晚：在评审时，或者当已构建的功能以你从未选择过的方式处理某个边缘情况时。Grilling 把这一切颠倒过来——Agent 不再猜测，而是必须提问。
这是一种 Human-in-the-loop 技术：你的回答就是输入。当某个问题无法在对话中得到回答——你必须亲眼看到那个东西才行——就切换到 Prototyping。
用法
"它直接就去写 Spec 了，结果把取消逻辑写错了。"
"先 Grill 它——让它在把任何内容写进文档之前，先来问你关于部分取消、退款和时序的问题。在对话里解决比在代码里解决更便宜。"

summary.zh: Grilling 通过持续追问暴露方案里的模糊点和隐含假设，一次聚焦一个决策。它适合在构建前澄清目标、边界和取舍，而不是用提问拖延已足够明确的实现。

description.en: Having the agent build a quick, rough version when conversation is too low-fidelity and you need a real artifact to talk about.
description.zh: 当讨论不足以判断方案时，先做一个快速原型来验证感觉与行为。

en: Having the agent build a quick, rough version of something, for when conversation is too low-fidelity and you need a real artifact to talk about.

Grilling resolves design decisions in conversation. Conversation is cheap, but it's low-fidelity: some questions can't be answered in words — how an interaction feels, whether an API shape is ergonomic in real calling code, whether the layout works at real data sizes. The interview hits a question and your honest answer is "I don't know, I'd have to see it." Past that point the discussion circles. Instead, have the agent build the thing, look at it, and come back to the conversation with an answer.

Agents lower the cost of building, which is what makes this practical. A rough version that used to take a day to mock up now takes minutes, so it's worth doing routinely. It's a human-in-the-loop technique: the prototype is there for you to react to.

You usually don't stop at one look. Iterate with the prototype — react, ask for a change, react again — so each round resolves another decision against the real artifact, at a higher fidelity than conversation allows.

A prototype doesn't have to be all-scrappy. You can build the pieces you're actually evaluating to production quality, so when the decision lands, the component or API you reacted to can transfer into the real codebase. This makes prototyping essential material for the spec to reference.
Usage:
"We've spent half an hour arguing about whether the wizard should be one page or three steps."
"Words won't settle it — have the agent prototype both. We'll click through them and know in five minutes."
zh: 让 Agent 快速搭出一个粗略版本，用在对话保真度太低、你需要一个真实产物才能讨论的时候。
Grilling 在对话中敲定设计决策。对话成本很低，但保真度也低：有些问题无法用语言回答——交互手感如何、API 形态在实际调用代码里是否顺手、布局在真实数据规模下能否成立。访谈进行到某个问题，你诚实的回答是「我不知道，我得看到才行」。过了这个点，讨论就开始打转。这时不如让 Agent 把东西做出来，看一看，再带着答案回到对话中。
Agent 降低了构建成本，这才让这种做法变得可行。过去要花一天做原型草稿的东西，现在几分钟就能出来，所以值得把它变成常规做法。这是一种 Human-in-the-loop 技术：原型摆在那里，供你做出反应。
你通常不会只看一眼就停下。拿原型反复迭代——反应、提出修改、再反应——每一轮都针对真实产物敲定另一个决策，保真度高于对话所能达到的水平。
Prototyping 不必全都草率。你正在评估的那部分可以按生产质量标准来构建，这样决策一旦落定，你所反应的那个组件或 API 就能迁移进真实代码库。这让 Prototyping 成为 Spec 引用的关键材料。
用法
「我们已经花了半小时争论这个向导应该做成一个页面还是三个步骤。」
「靠嘴说不清楚——让 Agent 把两种都做出原型。我们点一遍，五分钟就知道了。」

summary.zh: Prototyping 用快速、可丢弃的原型回答难以靠讨论解决的问题。原型的价值在于验证交互、状态或视觉方向，而不是立刻成为正式实现；得到答案后再决定保留什么。

description.en: Developer experience: how easy a codebase and its toolchain make it for humans to do good work — docs, feedback speed, errors.
description.zh: Developer experience，即开发者在代码库中理解、修改和验证工作的体验。

en: Developer experience — how easy a codebase and its toolchain make it for humans to do good work. Good DX is fast feedback, clear error messages, documentation that answers the question you actually have, and setup that works on the first try. The term long predates AI coding; it's in this dictionary mainly as the contrast for AX.

DX is the interaction between the human and the codebase — nothing more. The main difference between the two audiences is that humans are stateful and agents are stateless. A human learns the codebase once and carries that knowledge into every day after, which is why poor DX is survivable: they route around slow CI by batching their pushes, around missing docs by asking in Slack once, around confusing structure by remembering where things live. The workarounds accumulate, and a team ends up productive in a codebase that fights them.

Agents face the same codebase with none of that accumulation. Stateless across sessions, an agent re-learns the codebase from scratch every time — it benefits from the fast test suite and the clear error messages, but anything it figured out yesterday is gone unless it was written into the environment, which the agent only perceives through tool results. That's the gap AX names: the parts of DX that survive when the developer is an agent, plus concerns humans don't have, like keeping the context window free.

The overlap means DX investment often improves AX for free — strict types, fast tests, and predictable structure help both. The divergence means it doesn't always: a beautiful onboarding doc helps a human for a week and an agent not at all unless it's reachable from AGENTS.md.
Usage:
"Our DX is fine — new hires are productive in a week."
"Productive because someone sits with them for that week. The agent doesn't get that week; check the AX separately."
zh: Developer experience——代码库及其工具链让人类做好工作变得有多容易。好的 DX 是快速反馈、清晰的错误信息、能回答你实际遇到的问题的文档，以及一次就能跑通的初始搭建。这个词远早于 AI coding 出现；它被收入本词典，主要是作为 AX 的对照。

DX 就是人与代码库之间的交互——仅此而已。这两类受众之间最主要的不同在于：人类是 Stateful 的，而 Agent 是 Stateless 的。人类把代码库学一遍，就能把这份认知带进之后的每一天，这也是糟糕 DX 尚可忍受的原因：他们用攒批推送绕开缓慢的 CI，用在 Slack 里问一次绕开缺失的文档，用记住东西放在哪里绕开令人困惑的结构。这些变通做法不断累积，团队最终在一个处处与自己为敌的代码库里依然保持高产。

Agent 面对同一个代码库时，没有任何这类积累。跨会话 Stateless 的 Agent 每次都要从头重新学习代码库——它能受益于快速的测试套件和清晰的错误信息，但凡是昨天弄明白的东西都已消失，除非它被写进了 Environment，而 Agent 只能通过 Tool 结果感知 Environment。这正是 AX 所命名的缺口：DX 中在开发者是 Agent 时依然留存的那部分，再加上人类所没有的关切，比如让 Context window 保持空闲。
两者的重叠意味着 DX 上的投入往往能免费提升 AX——严格的类型、快速的测试和可预测的结构对双方都有帮助。两者的分歧则意味着它并不总是如此：一份漂亮的入职文档能帮上人类一周，对 Agent 却毫无用处，除非它能从 AGENTS.md 抵达。
用法
“我们的 DX 没问题——新人一周就能上手。”
“那是因为那一周有人陪着他们。Agent 没有那一周；AX 要单独检查。”

summary.zh: DX 即 Developer experience，关注开发者在项目里理解结构、修改代码和获得反馈的难易程度。清晰的模块边界、可运行的检查和可靠文档，都会影响 DX。

description.en: Agent experience: how well the environment is set up for an agent to do good work — checks, architecture, and free context.
description.zh: Agent experience，即环境是否便于 Agent 完成工作，包括检查、架构和可用上下文。

en: Agent experience — how well the environment is set up for an agent to do good work in a codebase. The agent-facing counterpart to DX. When the same agent performs well in one repo and badly in another — same model, same harness — the difference is usually AX. The instinct is to blame the model or rewrite the prompt; the fix is more often in the repo.
Good AX has three main dimensions:

| Dimension        | What good AX looks like                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Automated checks | Fast, deterministic automated checks — types, tests, lints — that the agent can self-correct from without a human                                                                                                          |
| Architecture     | A codebase the agent can navigate without reading everything: predictable structure, a lot of behaviour behind small interfaces, names that say what things do                                                                                       |
| Free context     | AGENTS.md, skills, and tools kept lean, so most of the context window is available for the task and the agent stays in the smart zone instead of drowning |

AX and DX overlap — good checks and clean architecture help both audiences — but they diverge. Humans tolerate tribal knowledge, slow CI, and "ask Sarah about the billing module"; agents can't. Agents don't benefit from IDE tooltips or pretty dashboards; they need failures as text in a tool result. A codebase can have good DX and poor AX.
Avoid: treating AX as a synonym for DX — the audiences need different investments.
Usage:
"The agent writes great code in the API repo and garbage in the frontend."
"The API repo has strict types and a fast test suite; the frontend has neither and forty always-loaded skills. That's an AX gap, not a model problem."
zh: Agent experience——衡量 environment 为 agent 在代码库中把活干好而搭建得有多好。它是 DX 面向 agent 的对应物。同一个 agent 在一个仓库里表现出色、在另一个仓库里一塌糊涂——model 相同、harness 也相同——差异通常就出在 AX 上。人的本能是去怪 model 或者重写 prompt；但真正要修的地方，往往在仓库本身。
好的 AX 有三个主要维度：
AX 与 DX 有重叠——良好的检查与整洁的架构对两类受众都有帮助——但二者也会分化。人类能容忍口口相传的隐性知识、缓慢的 CI，以及“账单模块去问 Sarah”；agent 做不到。agent 无法从 IDE 的工具提示或漂亮的仪表盘中获益；它们需要的是以文本形式出现在 tool result 里的失败信息。一个代码库完全可能 DX 很好而 AX 很差。
要避免：把 AX 当作 DX 的同义词——两类受众需要的是不同的投入。
用法
“这个 agent 在 API 仓库里写出好代码，在前端却写出一堆垃圾。”
“API 仓库有严格的类型和快速的测试套件；前端两样都没有，却有四十个始终加载的 skills。这是 AX 上的差距，不是 model 的问题。”

summary.zh: AX 即 Agent experience，关注环境是否帮助 Agent 做出正确工作。可发现的结构、明确的规范、便宜的验证，以及可用的 Context，能减少 Agent 猜测和返工。

description.en: A system of work where triggers, not humans, start agent sessions, so more work runs AFK and HITL time is saved for what needs it.
description.zh: 由触发器启动 Agent Sessions、自动推进工作的代码生产流程。

en: A system of work where agent sessions are started by triggers — an issue being created, a schedule, a CI failure, another session finishing — rather than by a human, so more work runs AFK and human attention is spent on the human-in-the-loop decisions that remain.

Without a factory, every session starts because someone started it. Even fully AFK work waits on a person to open the session, point it at the ticket, and set it going. Teams want to ship more than that allows. A factory takes the human out of starting sessions, and not necessarily out of anything else.
Common triggers and the sessions they start:

| Trigger                        | Session it starts                    | Example                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Issue created or labelled      | Exploration, bug fix, implementation | An issue labelled ready-for-agent gets a session that opens a PR                                                        |
| Schedule (cron)                | Recurring maintenance                | One lint rule fixed per night                                                                                             |
| CI failure or monitoring alert | Diagnosis, fix attempt               | A failing build on main gets a session that finds the breaking commit and proposes a fix                                  |
| Another session finishing      | Follow-on work                       | A PR opened by one agent triggers an automated review, whose comments trigger a fix-up session |

A factory doesn't have to cover the whole software process. One cron job that runs one kind of session and opens one reviewable PR is a factory. Starting that small is useful: a narrow loop produces small, similar PRs, and reviewing them shows how far the loop can be trusted before it's widened.

Humans can sit anywhere in a factory — writing and labelling the issues that trigger sessions, approving a plan before implementation starts, doing human review before merge. Deciding which of those decisions stay human is the main design question. A codebase, or part of one, where no human reviews the factory's output is a dark factory.
Usage:
"Who fixed all the no-floating-promises violations?"
"The factory. Cron job picks one lint rule a night, opens a PR. I just review it in the morning."
zh: 一种工作系统：agent session 由触发器启动——创建 issue、定时计划、CI 失败、另一个 session 完成——而不是由人启动，因此更多工作在 AFK 状态下运行，人的注意力则花在那些仍需 human-in-the-loop 的决策上。
没有工厂时，每个 session 之所以启动，都是因为有人启动了它。即便是完全 AFK 的工作，也要等人打开 session、把它指向 ticket、再让它跑起来。团队想交付的规模超出了这种方式所能允许的上限。工厂把人从「启动 session」这件事里拿掉，但不一定把人从其他任何环节里拿掉。
常见的触发器，以及它们启动的 session：

| 触发条件 | 启动的 Session | 示例 |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 创建或加标签的 Issue | 探索、bug 修复、功能实现 | 带 ready-for-agent 标签的 Issue 会启动一个 Session 并打开 PR |
| 定时调度（cron） | 周期性维护 | 每晚修复一条 lint 规则 |
| CI 失败或监控告警 | 诊断、尝试修复 | main 上的构建失败会启动一个 Session，找出导致失败的 commit 并提出修复方案 |
| 另一个 Session 完成时 | 后续工作 | 一个 agent 打开的 PR 会触发 automated review，其评论又会触发一个修复 Session |
工厂不必覆盖整个软件流程。一个 cron job，只运行一种 session、只开出一个可评审的 PR，就是一个工厂。从小处起步是有用的：窄的循环产出小且相似的 PR，评审它们就能看出这条循环在被扩大之前可以被信任到什么程度。
在一座工厂里，人可以处在任何位置——撰写并给那些触发 session 的 issue 打标签、在实现开始前批准方案、在合并前做 human review。决定其中哪些决策保留给人，是主要的设计问题。一个代码库，或代码库的一部分，若没有任何人对工厂的产出做评审，那就是一座 dark factory。
用法
“谁把所有 no-floating-promises 违规都修好了？”
“工厂。定时任务每晚挑一条 lint 规则，开一个 PR。我早上评审一下就行。”

summary.zh: Software factory 是由触发条件启动 Agent Sessions 并推进工作的一套流程，而不总是由人手动开启对话。它把自动执行、检查、审查和交付串联起来，使人把时间放在关键判断上。

description.en: A codebase, or part of one, where a software factory writes the code and no human ever reviews it.
description.zh: Agent 编写代码且没有人逐项审查的 software factory。

en: A codebase, or part of one, where a software factory writes the code and no human reads it. There is no human review. Humans can still write the issues that start the work. But nobody reads the code that comes out. The name comes from "lights-out" factories, which make things with no people on the floor.

A dark factory is vibe coding for an area of code, not for one change. When you vibe code, you choose not to read a change that you asked for. But you know that the change exists. In a dark factory, the team makes that choice one time, for the full area. After that, no person asks for each change or sees it. Changes arrive as fast as the triggers start new work.

The problem shows when something breaks. You do not know what changed, because nobody read the changes. You must debug code that nobody on the team has read. The cause can be in any of many changes, and each one passed the checks.
Automated checks and automated review are the only gates. If they do not find a problem, the problem goes into the code.
Avoid: calling a codebase "dark" only because its factory runs with nobody watching. If agent sessions run AFK and a human reviews their PRs, that is a software factory. It is not a dark factory.
Usage:
"Who changed the retry logic in the billing service? Nobody on the team remembers it."
"The billing service is a dark factory. The agents merge all changes that pass CI. Nobody read that change."
zh: 一个代码库，或代码库的一部分，其中由 Software factory 编写代码，没有任何人阅读它。不存在 Human review。人类仍然可以编写启动工作的 issue。但没有人阅读产出的代码。这个名字来自 "lights-out" 工厂，即车间里没有人也能生产的工厂。
Dark factory 是针对某个代码领域的 Vibe coding，而不是针对某一次变更。当你进行 Vibe coding 时，你选择不去阅读自己请求的那次变更。但你知道这次变更是存在的。在 Dark factory 中，团队为整个领域一次性做出这个选择。此后，没有人再为每一次变更提出请求，也没有人看到它。变更以触发器启动新工作的速度不断到来。
出故障的时候，问题就显现了。你不知道改了什么，因为没有人读过这些变更。你必须调试团队里没有人读过的代码。原因可能存在于许多变更中的任何一个，而每一个变更都通过了检查。
Automated checks 和 Automated review 是仅有的关卡。如果它们没有发现问题，问题就进入了代码。
要避免：仅仅因为某个代码库的 factory 在无人注视的情况下运行，就称它为 "dark"。如果 Agent 会话以 AFK 方式运行，而人类审查它们的 PR，那是一个 Software factory，不是 Dark factory。
用法
"谁改了计费服务里的重试逻辑？团队里没有一个人记得。"
"计费服务就是一个 Dark factory。Agent 会合并所有通过 CI 的变更。没有人读过那次变更。"

summary.zh: Dark factory 是一种没有人逐项审查代码的 Software factory。它把实现与验证更多交给自动化系统，因此对检查、边界和可追溯性要求更高；“无人审查”是它的核心特征。
